genres.name: Ambient
genres.description: Emphasizes texture and tone over traditional musical structure, aimed at evoking a particular atmosphere or mood.

genres.name: Ambient Americana
genres.description: Made using traditional Americana and Country instrumentation, typically to evoke a pastoral atmosphere.

genres.name: Dark Ambient
genres.description: Emphasizes an ominous, gloomy, and dissonant atmosphere.

genres.name: Black Ambient
genres.description: Incorporates elements such as guitars, synthesizers, harsh or whispered vocals, raw production, or other elements associated with Black Metal and Dungeon Synth.

genres.name: Ritual Ambient
genres.description: Dark, disturbing, ritualistic, and occult atmosphere, often taking inspiration from various existing ritual practices around the world.

genres.name: Space Ambient
genres.description: Flowing and relaxing synthesizer-based music derived from Progressive Electronic, often oriented around imagery of outer space.

genres.name: Tribal Ambient
genres.description: Combines the theory and atmosphere of Ambient with traditional instruments and sounds from around the globe.

genres.name: Blues
genres.description: Originated toward the end of the 19th century in African American communities in the United States, particularly the Deep South; drew on traditional Spiritual and Work Song; highly influential to the whole of Western popular music.
genres.track: I Want a Little Sugar In My Bowl

genres.name: Acoustic Blues
genres.description: Developed out of Work Song and Spiritual to become the most prominent early form of Blues.

genres.name: Acoustic Chicago Blues
genres.description: Unplugged Blues made in the Chicago region, primarily during the 1930s and 1940s.

genres.name: Acoustic Texas Blues
genres.description: Laid-back swing rhythms and guitar ornamentation, including solos.

genres.name: Jug Band
genres.description: Usually features a jug as the bass instrument as well as other homemade (or easily affordable) instruments, such as kazoos and washboards.
genres.album: Dave Van Ronk And The Ragtime Jug Stompers

genres.name: Piedmont Blues
genres.description: Developed in the early 20th century in the southern Appalachian foothills and characterized by a syncopated but melodic Ragtime-based finger-picking acoustic guitar style.
genres.track: Since I've Laid My Burden Down

genres.name: Boogie Woogie
genres.description: Early, uptempo Blues featuring the piano as the main instrument, with soloing and improvisation played over the top of a repetitive eight note bassline.

genres.name: Country Blues
genres.description: Various styles of Blues originating in the rural US South, typically relying on expressive vocal delivery and featuring simple, usually acoustic instrumentation.
genres.track: Let The Mermaids Flirt With Me

genres.name: Delta Blues
genres.description: One of the earliest forms of Blues, named for the Mississippi Delta region of the United States where it developed, with a highly rhythmic style and a typical 12-bar structure.

genres.name: Bentonia School
genres.description: Brooding, hypnotic minor-key open-tuning guitar style with a looser structure, often featuring high, "haunting" vocals.
genres.album: greatest of the delta blues singers

genres.name: Hill Country Blues
genres.description: Emphasizes a steady hypnotic groove, sparse percussive and highly energetic guitar riffs, and often features meandering structures with unconventional and usually fewer chord changes compared to Delta Blues.

genres.name: Electric Blues
genres.description: Major development in sound and reach of Blues when it became possible to amplify the instruments of small combos.

genres.name: British Blues
genres.description: Heavily influenced by the burgeoning United States Blues scene, particularly Chicago Blues.

genres.name: Chicago Blues
genres.description: Heavily inspired by old-time rural blues, transferring it into a small band setup, while maintaining the rough and gritty edges of its ancestry.

genres.name: Electric Texas Blues
genres.description: Originating in (but not limited to) Texas; includes Jazz influences like Swing rhythms and sometimes the addition of a horn section.

genres.name: Swamp Blues
genres.description: Originated in Baton Rouge, Louisiana in the 1950s, with a laid-back and relaxed sound that takes influence from Zydeco and Cajun Music.

genres.name: Jump Blues
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1930s with influence from Jazz styles such as Swing and Big Band, featuring fast tempos and raucous performances.

genres.name: Piano Blues
genres.description: Features the piano as a lead instrument performed solo or with a small ensemble, ranging from mid-tempo ballads to fast-paced dance styles.

genres.name: Soul Blues
genres.description: Shares similarities with Soul and incorporates the eponymous soulful inflections of Gospel, Jump Blues and soul into the vocals.
genres.album: I Got Dem Ol' Kozmic Blues Again Mama!

genres.name: Vaudeville Blues
genres.description: Vaudeville incorporating heavy Blues elements.

genres.name: Classical Music
genres.description: Part of a broad generalization about the structure and function of music throughout history across the globe, describing traditions distinct from Traditional Folk Music and popular music.

genres.name: East Asian Classical Music
genres.description: Covers all the forms of pan-East Asian Classical Music sharing origins in Chinese Classical Music.

genres.name: Chinese Classical Music
genres.description: Classical Music of China, encompassing royal court music.

genres.name: Baisha xiyue
genres.description: Mainly performed for funeral ceremonies of the Naxi ethnic group in the Yunnan province in China.
genres.track: Ancient Music of the Naxi People: Suite of Baisha Xiyue
genres.album: Ancient Chinese Music: Autumn Reflections by the Dongting Lake

genres.name: Chinese Literati Music
genres.description: Music of the Chinese literati; primarily played on the guqin and invoking emotional restraint, self-cultivation, and introspection.

genres.name: Dongjing
genres.description: Rooted in Chinese Taoist Ritual Music from the Nakhi (Naxi) people, historically performed around Yunnan and Sichuan.

genres.name: Yayue
genres.description: Incorporates folk and religious traditions of Chinese Music; literally translated as 'elegant music'.
genres.artist: The Hubei Song and Dance Ensemble

genres.name: Japanese Classical Music
genres.description: Classical music of Japan.
genres.artist: Koto Ensemble of the Ikuta School
genres.track: Otone no Nagare ni Sote (Along the Grand Tone River)

genres.name: Gagaku
genres.description: One of the oldest forms of Japanese Classical Music, based on the pentatonic Yo scale, characterized by an elegant sound that is typically solemn, slow-paced, and resonant.

genres.name: Heikyoku
genres.description: Semi-classical bardic tradition in Japan analogous to the troubadour music of medieval Europe.

genres.name: Honkyoku
genres.description: Japanese Classical Music performed solo on a bamboo flute shakuhachi.

genres.name: Jiuta
genres.description: Originally created by solo performers singing and playing shamisen, but since the late 18th century increasingly often performed by sankyoku ensembles (shamisen, koto and shakuhachi or kokyu).
genres.artist: Master Musicians of the Ikuta School
genres.album: Japanese Koto Consort: Kotos, Jushichigen, Shamisen, Shakuhachi and Voice

genres.name: Jōruri
genres.description: Consists of a singing narrator (tayū) with shamisen accompaniment.

genres.name: Meiji shinkyoku
genres.description: Meiji-era compositions, using a distinctive, brighter scale, usually performed with two kotos.

genres.name: Nagauta
genres.description: Japanese Classical Music used in Kabuki, a form of theatre oriented to dance-drama.
genres.album: nagauta music and original music and arrangements from older classics

genres.name: Noh
genres.description: Played by an hayashi ensemble, consisting of a fue (flute), a kotsuzumi (shoulder drum), a ōtsuzumi (hip drum), and a taiko (stick drum).

genres.name: Shōmyō
genres.description: Japanese Buddhist chant that utilizes the yō scale.
genres.album: You Who Are Leaving To Nirvana

genres.name: Sōkyoku
genres.description: Gained popularity during the Edo period, played with a koto or a guzheng and sometimes accompanied by shamisen and/or shakuhachi.
genres.album: Art of the Koto: The Music of Japan

genres.name: Danmono
genres.description: Sōkyoku composed for koto, a thirteen-string traditional instrument.

genres.name: Kumiuta
genres.description: Typically performed by a single singer playing koto or less often shamisen for accompaniment, often with lyrics adapted from classical poetry.

genres.name: Korean Classical Music
genres.description: Classical Music of Korea.

genres.name: Dang-ak
genres.description: Korean Classical Music that dates back to the Later Silla period of 668–935.

genres.name: Hyang-ak
genres.description: One of the most common and oldest surviving forms of Korean court music.
genres.album: 김계희 생황 정악 II 鳳笙之曲 (Kim Gye Hee Saenghwang Korean Classical Music)

genres.name: Jeong-ak
genres.description: Also known as proper music; dates back to the Later Silla period of 668–935.

genres.name: Gagok
genres.description: Vocal songs derived from Korean Classical Music backed by a small orchestra of Jeong-ak ("aristocratic or proper music").

genres.name: Vietnamese Court Music
genres.description: Traditional court music of Vietnam, specifically that of the Nguyễn dynasty.
genres.track: Khai tràng, nhip môt and/et nhip ba
genres.album: Vietnam Court Theatre Music / Musique du théâtre de Cour : Hat-bôi

genres.name: Inkiranya
genres.description: Influential drumming style originating in Burundi carried out by a percussion ensemble.

genres.name: Maqāmic Music
genres.description: Originating in the Middle East and founded upon maqāmāt scales, encompassing an extensive and diverse cultural and musical legacy that spans from Morocco to Southeast Asia.
genres.album: Moon Rise Over The Silk Road

genres.name: Arabic Classical Music
genres.description: Arabic Classical Music tradition, whose guidelines for modulation, rhythm, and tuning were set down in treatises in the 8th and 9th centuries, based around Maqāmic Music.
genres.album: ألف ليلة وليلة [Alf leila wa leila]

genres.name: Andalusian Classical Music
genres.description: Arabic Classical Music tradition that had its beginnings in Al-Andalus, the medieval Islamic Iberian peninsula, which later spread and developed in the Maghreb.
genres.track: Inshād Rasd Ad - Dail - Insiraf Darj Raml Al-Mâya

genres.name: Iraqi Maqam
genres.description: Highly structured but semi-improvised and rhythmically complex compositions built around set structures which consist of specific maqam modes.
genres.track: حالي به يحلو (He Fills My Spirit to the Brim)

genres.name: Sawt
genres.description: Poetic vocal form with complex rhythms, emotive singing, and distinctive lute-backed melodies commonly found in the Gulf region and based on a maqam system.

genres.name: Azerbaijani Mugham
genres.description: Highly improvisational form of modal music characterized by the singing style and the themes of Azerbaijan’s history.

genres.name: Persian Classical Music
genres.description: Traditional art music of the Persian civilization.

genres.name: Shashmaqam
genres.description: Modal suite that brings together lyrical and instrumental songs, poetry, and dance shared by Tajik Music and Uzbek Music.

genres.name: Sufiana kalam
genres.description: Classical music from Kashmir, the northernmost part of the Indian subcontinent.
genres.album: Cachemire: Le sufyana kalam de Srinagar (Kashmir: Sufyana Kalam from Srinagar)

genres.name: Turkish Classical Music
genres.description: Classical music of Turkey, which uses the makam modal system, with the primary emphasis often being on the singers, who are accompanied by small ensembles.

genres.name: Turkish Mevlevi Music
genres.description: Traditional music performed among Turkish practitioners of the Mevlevi order of Sufism.

genres.name: Twelve Muqam
genres.description: Uyghur muqam suite of 12 different muqam performances, originating in Southern Xinjiang.

genres.name: Minyue
genres.description: Modernized composition for Chinese instruments on the basis of Chinese Folk Music, incorporating aspects of Western Classical Music.
genres.album: 刘天华二胡演奏曲集 [Liu Tianhua erhu yanzou quji]

genres.name: Pìobaireachd
genres.description: Art tradition which originated in the Scottish Highlands, usually associated with the Great Highland bagpipes.
genres.track: Sir James MacDonald Of The Isles' Lament

genres.name: South Asian Classical Music

genres.track: Tose Lagi Lagan Shyam Salone: Raga Shuddh Kalyan - Khyal in Drut Teental

genres.name: Carnatic Classical Music
genres.description: Culture shared by the Dravidian cultures in South India separate from regional folk genres.
genres.album: Le violon de l'inde du sud

genres.name: Hindustani Classical Music
genres.description: North Indian traditional music (including parts of Pakistan, Afghanistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, and Bhutan) with roots reaching back to the 12th century CE.
genres.track: Kali Kali Zulfon Ke Phande Nah Dalo

genres.name: Dhrupad
genres.description: Ancient style of classical Hindustani vocal and instrumental music.

genres.name: Kafi
genres.description: Sufi vocal style popular in Pakistan, differentiated from Qawwali by its small ensemble size and simple arrangements.
genres.track: Yaar Ko Hamne Ja Baja Dekha

genres.name: Khayal
genres.description: Predominant vocal style, often with a significant amount of improvisation.

genres.name: Klasik
genres.description: Encompassing the various styles of Afghan Classical Music, which diverged from the North Indian styles.
genres.album: Music Of Central Asia, Vol. 3: Homayun Sakhi - The Art Of The Afghan Rubâb

genres.name: Qawwali
genres.description: Sufi Music in India and Pakistan using the raga and tala templates of Hindustani Classical Music, with an emphasis on ecstatic performance and devotional lyricism.

genres.name: Shabad kirtan
genres.description: Religious Sikh Hymn backed by specially selected ragas and taal.
genres.artist: ਹੰਸ ਰਾਜ ਹੰਸ [Hans Raj Hans] & चरणजीत आहूजा [Charanjit Ahuja]

genres.album: Musik aus Pakistan: Khyāl and Tāranā

genres.name: Thumri
genres.description: Hindustani classical style based on North Indian folk literature.
genres.album: Raga Jaijaiwanti / Raga Jaunpuri / Bhairavi Thumri

genres.name: Odissi Classical Music
genres.description: Traditional dance and classical music from the Odisha region of Eastern India.
genres.album: L'Inde : Musique traditionnelle de danse Odissi

genres.name: Southeast Asian Classical Music
genres.description: Formal music developed in Southeast Asian countries (Burma, Cambodia, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, East Timor, Brunei Darussalam) usually in form of gong-chime orchestras such as gamelan, kulintang and pi phat.

genres.name: Burmese Classical Music
genres.description: Traditional court music of Myanmar, developed from Southeast Asian, Hindu and Chinese influences.
genres.artist: စောင်းဦးဘသန်း [Saung U Ba Than]
genres.track: ပွဲကြိုက်ခင်
genres.album: စောင်းတိးနည်းသင်‌ဓိူး အခြေခံအမှတ်(၁) [Basic Method in Harp Music No. 1]

genres.name: Gamelan
genres.description: Originated in the island of Java; played by an ensemble typically consisting of metallophones and gongs, sometimes augmented with drums, flutes, and human voices.

genres.name: Balinese Gamelan
genres.description: Broad classification grouping various forms of Gamelan with native roots in Bali.
genres.album: Music From the Morning of the World

genres.name: Gamelan angklung
genres.description: Takes its name from the angklung, an instrument made of bamboo tubes.
genres.album: Balaganjur of Pande and Angklung of Sidan, Bali

genres.name: Gamelan beleganjur
genres.description: Loud, chaotic, highly percussive, and with heavy tempo changes.
genres.album: The Gamelan of the Walking Warriors: Gamelan Beleganjur and the Music of the Ngaben Funerary Ritual in Bali

genres.name: Gamelan gender wayang
genres.description: Performed with two/four metallophones made out of bronze keys with suspended bamboo tube resonators connected to them.
genres.album: music for the balinese shadow play

genres.name: Gamelan gong gede
genres.description: Ceremonial style characterized by a simpler and more melodic approach with clearer and more stable progressions compared to other Balinese orchestras.
genres.album: Bali: Musique pour le gong gédé

genres.name: Gamelan gong kebyar
genres.description: Free compositional techniques and rapidly changing dynamics.
genres.album: american works for balinese gamelan orchestra

genres.name: Gamelan jegog
genres.description: Played entirely on marimba-like instruments made from bamboo which widely differ in size.
genres.album: Jegog: The Bamboo Gamelan of Bali

genres.name: Gamelan selonding
genres.description: Ensemble consists of four to six musicians playing metallophones made out of iron in a seven-tone scale.

genres.name: Gamelan semar pegulingan
genres.description: Originated in the 16th-17th centuries; features a soft, delicate, and ethereal sound.

genres.name: Gamelan degung
genres.description: Sundanese Gamelan performed by a small orchestra of bronze gongs and metallophones.

genres.name: Javanese Gamelan
genres.description: Broad classification grouping Gamelan genres native to Javanese culture.
genres.track: Damarwulan Bids His Lover Anjasmara Farewell

genres.name: Gamelan sekaten
genres.description: Javanese ceremonial Gamelan played with large instruments, strictly unaccompanied by vocals.

genres.name: Solonese Gamelan
genres.description: Style originating from Surakarta; known for its subtle and more delicate sound.

genres.name: Kacapi suling
genres.description: Sundanese music played by an ensemble consisting of one or two kacapis (zithers), one suling (flute), and occasionally a set of kendangs (drums).
genres.album: Kacapi Suling: Sundanese Flute and Zither

genres.name: Kulintang
genres.description: Southeast Asian gong-chime ensemble consisting mainly of gong-chimes of various sizes, with the addition of larger gongs, various drums, and occasionally xylophones and non-percussion instruments.

genres.name: Mahori
genres.description: Thai and Khmer traditional orchestra combining xylophones and gong-chimes of Piphat/Pinpeat with strings of Khrueang sai ensemble.

genres.album: The Nang Hong Suite: Siamese Funeral Music

genres.name: Malay Classical Music
genres.description: Traditionally played in the royal courts of the several Malay kingdoms, empires and sultanates that existed throughout history.

genres.name: Pinpeat

genres.album: Echoes From The Palace: Music From The Cambodian Court

genres.name: Saluang klasik

genres.name: Tembang Sunda Cianjuran

genres.name: Western Classical Music

genres.name: Elizabethan Song

genres.name: Ballet de cour

genres.name: Comédie-ballet
genres.description: French form of musical drama from the 17th century that combines operatic singing, classical dance, and theater.

genres.description: Incorporates prominent "squelching", resonant low pass filter sounds typical to Acid House, and often other "trippy" effects into intense, syncopated, broken rhythms in the tempos of 110-150 BPM.

genres.name: Baltimore Club
genres.description: Drew on the "booty bass" syncopation of Miami Bass, combined with Breakbeat rhythms around 130 BPM and chopped up vocal samples as found in Ghetto House.
genres.album: in case we never get to rave again

genres.name: Big Beat
genres.description: Popular in Britain during the late 1990s, driven by edited breakbeats and prominent basslines.

genres.name: Breakbeat Hardcore
genres.description: Originated from the combination of sampled breakbeats and energetic rhythms with the "rave" influences set by early-1990s Techno and Acid House, including upbeat "stab" riffing and sample-based production.

genres.name: Darkside
genres.description: Dark atmosphere and fast rhythms; served as a forerunner of Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Hardcore Breaks
genres.description: Revival of Breakbeat Hardcore which emerged in the 2000s, bringing in modern influences and production techniques.

genres.name: Breakbeat Kota
genres.description: Indonesian style that slows down the syncopated rhythms of Funkot to moderate tempos around 130 BPM.

genres.name: Jungle Dutch
genres.description: Combines the high-pitched synth leads of Dutch House with the frantic "tribal" rhythms of Jungle Terror.

genres.name: Florida Breaks
genres.description: Developed during the mid-1990s, combining major influences of Hip Hop derivatives such as Miami Bass and Electro along with elements of 1990s Electronic Dance Music genres like House or Techno.

genres.name: Funky Breaks
genres.description: Merging popular 1990s breaks styles like Big Beat with major Funk and Soul elements.
genres.album: You've Come a Long Way Baby

genres.name: Nu Skool Breaks
genres.description: Developed in the late 1990s and early 2000s; takes elements from Drum and Bass, UK Garage, and Techno.

genres.name: Progressive Breaks
genres.description: Derivative of Progressive House that incorporates its lush, melodic synth leads and atmospheres into Breakbeat's syncopated and broken rhythms.
genres.album: Angel13: From The Hyper Speed Forest 聖なる森へ～天河の詩～

genres.name: Psybreaks
genres.description: Uses Psytrance-derived sound design, such as squelchy sounds and psychedelic effects.

genres.name: West Coast Breaks
genres.description: Combines the earlier breakbeats of Hip Hop and early Breakbeat or even Miami Bass, with various 1990s Electronic Dance Music genres like Trance and Techno.

genres.name: Broken Beat
genres.description: Choppy, syncopated grooves and loose influence from 1970s Jazz-Funk, with eclectic roots spanning Drum and Bass, Deep House, Acid Jazz, and Afrobeat.

genres.name: Bubblegum Bass
genres.description: Originated in the early 2010s, exaggerating the cutest and most feminine parts of 2000s Pop and combining them with bouncy, plastic synths over rhythms and sounds derived from a variety of contemporary club styles.

genres.name: Bubbling
genres.description: Originating in the Netherlands in the late 1980s, fusing sped-up Dancehall with Dutch Antillean music and contemporary Dutch rave.

genres.name: Budots
genres.description: Originated from the southern Philippines; notable for its distinct high-pitched synth hooks.

genres.name: Bérite Club
genres.description: Originated in the underground club scene of Paris in the mid-to-late 2010s, drawing on a variety of international club styles for its combination of prominent and erratic drum programming with freezing and looping chopped-up samples.

genres.name: Coupé-décalé
genres.description: Bass-heavy and minimal style of Ivorian popular dance music, drawing heavily from Zouglou and Congolese rhythms.

genres.name: Cruise
genres.description: Fast-paced Nigerian dance music, utilising chopped, often humorous, samples.

genres.name: Dariacore
genres.description: SoundCloud-based scene developed in the early 2020s, combining prominent vocal samples and distorted, dense production with influences from a wide range of Electronic Dance Music genres, often incorporating musical and visual references to popular media and internet culture.
genres.track: 17 yo silly EDM artist from Japan vs. the World

genres.name: Deconstructed Club
genres.description: Emerged in the 2010s as the hybridization of diverse Electronic Dance Music genres with an abrasive Post-Industrial sound.

genres.name: Dek Bass
genres.description: Prominent heavy, sustained bass tones, percussion derived from South Asian Music, and often high-pitched sound effects or samples; commonly played at extreme volumes in DJ/sound system competitions.

genres.name: Digital Cumbia
genres.description: Mixes an Electronic sound into traditional Cumbia through influences from House, Dancehall, Hyphy, and Dubstep.
genres.album: gonzalo martinez and his thinking congas

genres.name: Drum and Bass
genres.description: Fast, syncopated breakbeat patterns (often sampled or programmed) with prominent basslines, commonly within the 160-180 BPM range.

genres.name: Atmospheric Drum and Bass
genres.description: Prominent in the mid-1990s, uses faster, de-emphasized breakbeats, and places a greater focus on melodic elements such as slow, warm basslines and atmospheric melodies inspired by Ambient and Ambient House.
genres.track: the last thing she sent me
genres.album: we had good times together dont forget that

genres.name: Dancefloor Drum and Bass
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s as a more accessible and polished style with melodic, prominent synth leads derived from Jump-Up and punchy, often synthesized drums.

genres.name: Darkstep
genres.description: Hard, uptempo and uses heavy breakbeats, Post-Industrial-influenced sound design, and horror movie samples to create a sinister, claustrophobic atmosphere.

genres.name: Crossbreed
genres.description: Harsh and dense mixture of Darkstep with Hardcore [EDM] developed in the late 2000s.

genres.name: Skullstep
genres.description: Repetitious, aggressive, off-beat rhythms often programmed using distorted, harsh, and noisy percussion that usually resembles clangy "pots and pans", machine gun-like snares.

genres.name: Deep Drum and Bass
genres.description: Sub-bass-rich, repetitive, minimalist, and rhythm-focused production.

genres.name: Drumfunk
genres.description: Focuses on complex drum beats made to emulate live recordings.

genres.name: Drumstep
genres.description: Dancefloor-friendly, loud, and heavy combination of the drum programming and tempo of Jump-Up with the half-time rhythm and midrange LFO wobble of Brostep.

genres.name: Dubwise Drum and Bass
genres.description: Implementing Reggae and Dub influences, usually vocal dubs, delay effects, and reggae instrumentation, with the clean production and rhythms of post-2000s styles.

genres.name: Footwork Jungle
genres.description: Combining Footwork's archetypal percussion, skittering drum fills, handclaps, and syncopated rhythms, with Drum and Bass drum programming and breakbeats, merging the two into unconventional, frantic drumming and dense, off-kilter rhythms.

genres.name: Halftime
genres.description: Offshoot of Drum and Bass (mainly Neurofunk) characterized by off-kilter rhythms playing at around 80-85 BPM (half of normal DnB pace), influenced by Dubstep, Wonky, Trap [EDM], and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Hardstep
genres.description: Very compressed and sparse drumming, extensive use of kick drums and gritty, minimalistic production style with emphasis on simple, deep, modulated bass patterns.

genres.name: Jazzstep
genres.description: Combines the rhythm and speed of Drum and Bass with the melodies, composition, and instrumentation of Jazz.

genres.name: Jump-Up
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s, characterized by loud "wobbling" basslines, simpler drum loops, and a light-hearted and warm sound.
genres.track: Hit Man (Jungle アサシン mix)

genres.name: Jungle
genres.description: Developed in the early 1990s from Breakbeat Hardcore, featuring rapid, chaotic-sounding breakbeats and strong basslines; known as the forerunner of most Drum and Bass styles.
genres.album: If You're Into It I'm Out of It

genres.name: Ragga Jungle
genres.description: Developed in the early 1990s in London, combining Jungle breakbeats with heavy influence from Ragga.

genres.name: Liquid Drum and Bass
genres.description: Atmospheric and melodic genre that developed in the early 2000s; utilizes polished and smooth production, simpler structures, and originally sampled Funk and Soul.

genres.name: Sambass
genres.description: Combines Drum and Bass tempos and drum patterns, in addition to its Funk and Soul influences, with various styles of Brazilian Music.
genres.track: Só Tinha de Ser Com Você

genres.name: Minimal Drum and Bass
genres.description: Minimalist, sparse sound; emerged in two main 2000s strains, one Dubstep-inspired and one IDM-inspired, which crossed paths in the 2010s.

genres.name: Autonomic
genres.description: Mechanical, machine-like, "autonomic" rhythms that take primary influence from the cold, minimal sounds of mid-2000s UK Dubstep.

genres.name: Microfunk
genres.description: Minimal, glitchy, and "bleep"-y sound inspired by IDM.

genres.name: Neurofunk
genres.description: Focuses on technical songwriting with warped, complex bass sounds, distorted and modulated synths (often with repeated stabs over the basslines), and dark but clean production.

genres.name: Technoid
genres.description: Influenced by the repetitive and mechanical sound of Techno.

genres.name: Techstep
genres.description: Futuristic, dark, and gritty sound; quantized and compressed drum breaks, distorted bass lines, and a focus on a sci-fi atmosphere and sampling sources.

genres.name: Trancestep
genres.description: Combination of Trance melodies and structure with the breakbeats, fast tempos, and rolling basslines of Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Dubstep
genres.description: Half-time syncopated and sparse beats set around 140 BPM with heavy sub-basses; emerged in South London in the early 2000s.

genres.name: Brostep
genres.description: Offshoot of Dubstep which replaces its sub-bass-oriented sound with an emphasis on catchy or aggressive mid-range melodies.

genres.name: Briddim
genres.description: Combining the kick-clap rhythms and syncopation of Riddim with Brostep sound design.

genres.name: Colour Bass
genres.description: Combines aggressive wobbling basses with the euphoric drops of Melodic Dubstep and Future Bass.

genres.name: Deathstep
genres.description: Darker, heavier form of Brostep that uses "machine gun" basses, atonal synths, and elements from genres like Death Metal and Metalcore.

genres.name: Minatory
genres.description: Extreme, experimental style of Deathstep, with a harsh sound and sudden BPM changes.

genres.name: Tearout [Brostep]
genres.description: Heavy and distorted, closely affiliated with Deathstep and other styles of Brostep.

genres.name: Chillstep
genres.description: Relaxed Dubstep influenced by Downtempo and Ambient.
genres.track: 雪の降る街で、あなたを待っている。

genres.name: Dungeon Sound
genres.description: Commonly features dark textures, spatial production, and midrange basses.

genres.name: Melodic Dubstep
genres.description: Melodious, tuneful drops, rich, lush synth leads, powerful stretched chords, and light and harmonious sound design.

genres.name: Purple Sound
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s out of the Dubstep scene of the time, incorporating synth leads and basslines inspired by 1980s Synth Funk and 1990s G-Funk, and Video Game Music, into a rhythmic palette mostly derived from dubstep and Grime.

genres.name: Riddim
genres.description: Repetitive and relatively simplistic style inspired by mid-to-late-2000s UK Dubstep, often using robotic and/or squishy sound design along with bouncy square basses and less prominent buildups.

genres.name: Future Riddim
genres.description: Melodic and futuristic style inspired by Future Bass, and to a lesser extent Colour Bass and Melodic Dubstep.

genres.name: Liquid Riddim
genres.description: Distinct for its atmospheric production, overpowering ambience, watery synths, and melodic bass patterns.

genres.name: Tearout
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s, characterized by a gritty, aggressive sound and closely affiliated with early, deep Dubstep.

genres.name: EBM
genres.description: Melodic and dancefloor-friendly take on Post-Industrial music that developed in the early 1980s.

genres.name: Dark Electro
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1990s in Europe, incorporating the abrasiveness of old school Industrial but with a greater focus on a horror-inspired atmosphere and harsh, distorted vocals.

genres.name: Aggrotech
genres.description: Merges aggressive-sounding synths and apocalyptic atmospheres with harsh 4/4 beats and fast tempos.
genres.album: UGLY DEATH NO REDEMPTION ANGEL CURSE I LOVE YOU

genres.name: Futurepop
genres.description: Derivative of EBM, retaining its apocalyptic worldview but incorporating heavy influence from the melodic style of Synthpop.

genres.name: New Beat
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s in Belgium; characterized by dark basslines, hard-hitting grooves and a slow tempo.
genres.artist: My Life With the Thrill Kill Kult

genres.name: Hard Beat
genres.description: Short-lived, harder, harsh form of New Beat with Industrial, Acid House and EBM-influenced arrangement.

genres.name: East Coast Club
genres.description: Group of club styles from the US East Coast that combines Miami Bass rhythms with influence from Breakbeat and Ghetto House.

genres.name: Jersey Club
genres.description: Emerged in Newark in the late 2000s; features fast tempos, hard kicks, and less prominent breakbeats.

genres.name: Philly Club
genres.description: Builds on Baltimore Club with a faster tempo and sometimes influences from more modern genres like Trap [EDM].

genres.name: Electro
genres.description: Syncopated rhythms programmed on the Roland TR-808 drum machine, often resembling Funk breaks, along with simple funky basslines.

genres.name: Electro Swing
genres.description: Upbeat, energetic style that splices Swing with Electronic Dance Music, looking to recapture the atmosphere of late 1920s to mid-1940s Jazz within a more updated club-friendly medium.

genres.name: Electro latino
genres.description: Mixes elements of Merengue and Reggaetón with polished production from mainstream House subgenres; often shares traits with Latin Pop, having anthemic melodies and verse-chorus structures.

genres.name: Electroclash
genres.description: Draws from 1980s styles such as Electro, New Wave, and Electro-Disco combined with Techno, resulting in minimal, throbbing beats and basslines, buzzing synthesizer parts, vocoders and often monotone, half-spoken, half-sung vocals.

genres.name: Eurobeat
genres.description: Fast-paced with roots in Hi-NRG and Italo-Disco; became mainly popular in Japan in the 1990s.

genres.name: J-Euro
genres.description: Italian-oriented Japanese scene of Eurobeat, which emerged with Japanese-language covers of Italian songs in the early-to-mid-1990s.

genres.name: Eurodance
genres.description: Takes elements of Euro-Disco, House, Techno, and Hi-NRG while featuring on-beat kick, hi-hat and snare sounds at around 110 to 150 bpm.
genres.album: Love And Glitter, Hot Days And Muzik

genres.name: Italo Dance
genres.description: Appeared in the 1990s after the decline of Italo-Disco, featuring rhythmic influence from that genre.

genres.name: Flex Dance Music
genres.description: Largely instrumental; infused with Electronic Dance Music elements.

genres.name: Footwork
genres.description: Extensive use of drum fills, tom drums, handclaps, and snares within fast-paced, highly syncopated beats not bound to a 4/4 kick rhythm.

genres.name: Funk mandelão
genres.description: Simple lyricism, raw and minimalistic production, and distinct drops with bursting bass.

genres.name: Beat bruxaria
genres.description: São Paulo-originated Funk brasileiro with aggressive, distorted and high-pitched beats featuring minimalistic percussion and diversified sampling.

genres.name: Brazilian Phonk
genres.description: Merges Funk automotivo's rhythms, vocals, and energy, with the energetic and nocturnal production typical of the Drift Phonk scene, and Phonk House.

genres.name: Funk automotivo
genres.description: Catchy, repetitive synths accompanied by a strong four-on-the-floor kick and loud, reverberated vocals.

genres.name: Ritmada
genres.description: Short, repetitive and resonant beats with more danceable, immersive grooves drawn out of Afro-Brazilian instrumentation, a cleaner, more radio-friendly sound and greater focus on lyrics.
genres.track: Três Movimentos Que Te Conquista Fácil

genres.name: Funkot
genres.description: Fast-paced Indonesian form of Electronic Dance Music that combines Eurodance and Trance synths with the syncopated rhythm from Dangdut koplo.

genres.name: Future Bass
genres.description: Woozy, detuned synthesizers, 7th chords, harsh basslines, syncopated percussion with fast-paced hi-hats and a melodic, carefree atmosphere.
genres.album: Dariacore 2: Enter Here, Hell to the Left

genres.name: Kawaii Future Bass
genres.description: "Cute" style of Future Bass rooted in anime and video game culture; emerged in Japan in the mid-2010s.

genres.name: Future Core
genres.description: Blends the speed, basslines, and rhythms of UK Hardcore (mostly coming from the J-core sphere) with euphoric, woozy synths, 7th chords and arpeggios, and vocal chops of Future Bass, particularly Kawaii Future Bass.

genres.name: Future Rave
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2010s by combining the mainstage EDM approach with influences from then-popular forms of Techno and old-school Trance/rave-inspired grooves and atmospheres.

genres.name: Ghettotech
genres.description: Fuses the syncopation and synthesized sounds of Electro and Detroit Techno with the cut-up samples of Ghetto House and fast rhythms of Miami Bass.
genres.track: Ask your parents permission before going online

genres.name: Glitch Hop [EDM]
genres.description: Tempos around 100-110 BPM, swung, bouncy drum patterns, and a focus on upbeat, danceable drops and buildups.

genres.name: Ghetto Funk
genres.description: Rich sampling, drawing from classic Hip Hop as well as from Funk and Soul, and strong midtempo break grooves.

genres.name: Neurohop
genres.description: Features the complex bass of Neurofunk and a frantic and mechanical sound design.

genres.name: Gqom
genres.description: Emerged in the 2010s in Durban townships, features highly syncopated, bass-heavy, stripped-down beats and dark, raw atmosphere, often with ominous synth pads and aggressive vocal chants.

genres.name: Grime
genres.description: UK Garage-derived production style characterized by dark, fast-paced, often aggressive beats that commonly features fast-paced MCing.

genres.name: Neo-Grime
genres.description: Mixes Wave with Grime and other forms of UK Electronic music.

genres.name: Weightless
genres.description: Typically instrumental, leftfield Grime style characterized by sparse, "weightless" percussion and spectral, atmospheric production.

genres.name: Hard Dance
genres.description: Umbrella term for EDM mainly developed out of Hard Trance and UK Hard House; usually characterized by fast tempos, hard kick drums and a "bouncy" syncopated groove.

genres.name: Hard Trance
genres.description: Rave-oriented form of Trance infusing its atmospheres with faster, thumping rhythms and strong melodic / bassline sections, initially spawning out of the first wave in early-1990s Western Europe.

genres.name: Hardstyle
genres.description: Hard, four-on-the-floor kick drums, fast tempo around 150 BPM, reverse bass and harsh, distorted synths.

genres.name: Dubstyle
genres.description: Characterized by the incorporation of the half-time rhythms and wobbly basslines of Dubstep.

genres.name: Early Hardstyle
genres.description: Forerunner subgenre that emerged around the turn of the 2000s from Hard Trance and Gabber, distinguished by the signature reverse bass groove, slower tempo around 140 BPM and straightforward, repetitive sound.
genres.track: Save The Day - Showtek Youries Cut

genres.name: Euphoric Hardstyle
genres.description: Melodic, more lighthearted, and accessible Hardstyle.

genres.name: Nustyle
genres.description: Developed out of Early Hardstyle from the mid-to-late 2000s, by incorporating distorted, crunchy, pitched kicks, faster tempo around 150 BPM, and detuned supersaw/square synth leads playing stompy, dramatic melodies.
genres.album: Under the Radar Over the Top

genres.name: Psystyle
genres.description: Prominent Psytrance influences, especially the basslines and energy of mainstream psytrance.

genres.name: Rawstyle
genres.description: Incorporates earlier Hardstyle and Hardcore [EDM] influences into the sound of 2010s hardstyle, creating a distinctly harsh, simplistic, raw, and dark sound, with fast BPM.
genres.track: Dragoon - Sword of the valiant Ver.

genres.name: Rawphoric
genres.description: Combines raw harsh kicks with the uplifting melodies of Euphoric Hardstyle.

genres.name: Jumpstyle
genres.description: Features a heavy 909 kick drum, four-on-the-floor beat, and a tempo between 140 and 150 BPM.

genres.name: Lento violento
genres.description: Features a "slow and violent" sound between 70-120 BPM with hard kicks inspired by Hardcore [EDM] and Hardstyle.

genres.name: NRG
genres.description: Derived from UK Hard House; featuring darker, more anthemic Trance beats and a tempo of 155-165 BPM.

genres.name: UK Hard House
genres.description: Defined by offbeat bass patterns, compressed 909-style drums, buildup-drop structures, hoover sounds, and tempos between 120 and 155 BPM.
genres.track: DIE LIEBE KOMMT NICHT AUS BERLIN

genres.name: Scouse House
genres.description: Features an upbeat and energetic sound often described as being "bouncy", influenced somewhat by Happy Hardcore.

genres.name: Hardbass
genres.description: Bouncy hard bass beats, fast tempo, usually 150-175 BPM, and occasional lyrics or rapping.
genres.track: Give Me Your Money feat. Tommy Cash

genres.name: Speed House
genres.description: Mixes busy, dirty sound design and intense drums derived from Bass House with fast tempos from 140-160 BPM, pumping basslines, and other UK Hard House influences.

genres.name: Hard Drum
genres.description: Highly percussive, syncopated rhythms, influences from global contemporary genres, and lack of melodic elements, with a tempo lingering around 130 BPM.
genres.album: Desde los oídos de un sapo

genres.name: Hardcore [EDM]
genres.description: Umbrella term for a wide variety of fast-paced and energetic Electronic Dance Music styles that have been developed since the early 1990s.

genres.name: Acidcore
genres.description: Developed out of the 1990s Acid Techno scene utilizing its prominence of "acid" TB-303 bassline sequences into more intense rhythms derived from earlier Hardcore [EDM], Gabber and Trance music.

genres.name: Amigacore
genres.description: Gabber-like forms of Hardcore [EDM] written in first-gen trackers for the Amiga like ProTracker and OctaMED, resulting in a minimalistic raw lo-fi sound.

genres.name: Belgian Techno
genres.description: Early form of Hardcore [EDM], resulting from the further evolution of New Beat due to the strong influence of Techno and EBM.

genres.name: Breakcore
genres.description: Mixes Hardcore [EDM] with cut-up, complex, and frequently noisy breakbeats at very high tempos inspired by Jungle and Drum and Bass, often with heavy use of sampling.
genres.track: Burn This Moment Into the Retina of My Eye

genres.name: Lolicore
genres.description: Heavily distorted or high-pitched Anime vocal samples and complex cut-up breakbeats with extreme tempos.

genres.name: Mashcore
genres.description: Sampling, particularly from Pop and Electronic Dance Music, as well as playful melodies, hard kicks, and the typical breakcore breakbeats.

genres.name: Raggacore
genres.description: Prominently incorporates samples from Ragga and Dancehall, typically through shouted vocal lines and Reggae-influenced instrumentals.

genres.name: Darkcore
genres.description: Aggressive, dark, and often midtempo with influences from Doomcore, Industrial Hardcore, and Nu Style Gabber.

genres.name: Deathchant Hardcore
genres.description: Took shape in the UK in the late 1990s and early 2000s, characterized by rapid rhythms with Gabber-influenced kicks, frequent use of breakbeats and Hip Hop-inspired sampling.
genres.track: A Journey Of Force - Bastard Mix

genres.name: Digital Hardcore
genres.description: High-tempo fusion of Hardcore Punk and Electronic, combining harsh vocals and electric guitars of the former with electronic instruments.
genres.album: …Because I’m Young Arrogant and Hate Everything You Stand For

genres.name: Doomcore
genres.description: Often somber and contemplative in mood, a feature achieved by the common use of long-stretched ambient pads, and sometimes even samples of screaming and other "spooky" sounds.

genres.name: Frapcore
genres.description: Emerged in France in the mid-2010s, uses French rapping with 4-on-the-floor Hardcore [EDM] and especially Gabber instrumentals.

genres.name: Freeform Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s, combining fast and hard-hitting rhythms with heavy influence from the synthesizers of Trance.
genres.album: the recovery of the absolute artifact

genres.name: Frenchcore
genres.description: Off-beat, bouncy rhythmic patterns and tempos around the 200 BPM range.

genres.name: Gabber
genres.description: Fast-paced and energetic, often in the 160-220 BPM range, with a hallmark of a distinctive distorted kick sound.

genres.name: Nu Style Gabber
genres.description: Emerged near the end of the 1990s; deeper, more harmonic bassdrums with constant use of supersaw melodies, breakdown sections and slower tempos closer to the 150-180 BPM range.

genres.name: Happy Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the 1990s from the UK Breakbeat Hardcore scene; characterized by saccharine vocals, uplifting piano riffs and spacey effects, gradually developing to emphasize extremely fast-paced four-on-the-floor beats.

genres.name: Bouncy Techno
genres.description: Average tempo of 160 to 180 BPM, four-on-the-floor beats, melodic and repetitive synth melodies, drums with hard kicks, short breaks, progressive stomping rhythms, and offbeat notes.

genres.name: UK Hardcore
genres.description: Four-on-the-floor beat around 175 BPM, thick, prominent basslines, and uplifting synth leads, with a cleaner and more accessible sound than other forms of Hardcore [EDM].

genres.name: Powerstomp
genres.description: Prominent, "stomping", and slightly distorted kick, relentless, repetitive reverse basses on the offbeats (borrowed from Hardstyle) that drive the tracks, giving the genre its distinct energetic sound, and cacophonous, noisy riffs and synth leads.

genres.name: Hardtek
genres.description: Modern version of the "tribecore" sound featuring deep alternating basses and festival EDM-influenced drops.

genres.name: Raggatek
genres.description: Influenced by Reggae, Ragga and Dancehall, combining half-time instrumental sections with Hardtek's fast four-on-the-floor rhythms, as well as vocal samples, clean basslines and skank rhythms.

genres.name: Industrial Hardcore
genres.description: Fuses the sonic palettes and aesthetics of Industrial with the intense rhythms of Gabber, Speedcore, Doomcore and other subsequent styles.

genres.name: Speedcore
genres.description: Exceedingly fast tempos, frequently above 300 BPM, and often aggressive themes and samples.

genres.name: Extratone
genres.description: At and above the threshold of 1000 BPM where sequences of kick drums begin to form a continuous pitch.

genres.name: Splittercore
genres.description: Faster version of Speedcore with BPM ranging from around 600 to 1000.

genres.name: Terrorcore
genres.description: Utilizes rhythms from earlier Gabber with a faster BPM (usually no more than 300) and darker approach.

genres.name: Uptempo Hardcore
genres.description: Utilizes lo-fi production, harsh kicks, and elements borrowed from Rawstyle and other gritty Hardcore [EDM] styles while usually sitting at around 185-220 BPM.

genres.name: Hardvapour
genres.description: Influenced by Hardcore [EDM] and Techno and made in response to the Vaporwave movement.

genres.name: Hardwave
genres.description: Harder, festival-oriented offshoot of Wave, combining its "reese" basses and icy synths with Trap [EDM] drum patterns, build-up-drop structures, and fuller sound influenced by Trance and Hardstyle.

genres.name: House
genres.description: Generally features a four-on-the-floor beat within 110-140 BPM, a groove built on swing and syncopation, synthesized basslines, repetitive melodic elements, and an upbeat mood.

genres.name: Acid House
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s, characterised by repetitive basslines created with the distinctive modulated "squelching" sound of the Roland TB-303 synthesiser.

genres.name: Afro House
genres.description: Emerged by fusing Deep House with Southern African Music, characterized by hypnotizing drum patterns of shakers and congas, often sampled African vocals or soulful original features, and spiritual, organic, melodic atmosphere.

genres.name: 3-Step
genres.description: Distinct three-kick-drum rhythm, blends influences from Amapiano and Broken Beat, resulting in relaxed, freeform, playful, Jazz-like feel.

genres.name: Amapiano
genres.description: House from South Africa deriving from previous popular genres including Gqom, Kwaito, and Deep House.

genres.name: Afropiano
genres.description: Blends the easy-going, poppy, and melodic Afrobeats sound and rhythms with major Amapiano elements, like lush, jazzy, and laid-back atmospheres often featuring light piano chords.

genres.name: Ambient House
genres.description: Primarily British genre developed in the 1990s with beats, synthesizers, and vocals in styles similar to House, treated with effects that are often described as "dream-like" or "chilled out".

genres.name: Ballroom
genres.description: Emerging from the predominantly Black and LGBT Harlem ballroom culture, it is characterized by hard-hitting rhythms, generally improvised chanting by MCs known as commentators, and a distinctive crash sample.

genres.name: Bass House
genres.description: Busy, punchy percussion, prominent basslines and dirty, distorted synths resembling other bass music genres, with influences including Brostep, Fidget House, Bassline, Speed Garage, and Tech House.
genres.track: ぉ─ゑぅぇﾚヽずﾚヽω､ﾅ″ﾅょﾚヽー⊂めぁ [ʚ ♥ɞ]

genres.name: Bassline
genres.description: Strong emphasis on intricate basslines as well as four-on-the-floor beat patterns.

genres.name: Big Room House
genres.description: Energetic, festival-oriented style characterized by heavy reverb, intense build-ups, strong kicks, minimalistic drop melodies, and sparse, raw breakdowns.

genres.name: Brazilian Bass
genres.description: Originated in the 2010s in Brazil, taking influences from Deep House and Tech House, characterized by deep, punchy basslines making use of detuning and filtering effects.

genres.name: Mega funk
genres.description: Blends funk vocal performances with production derived from mainstage 2010s House genres like Brazilian Bass and Slap House.

genres.name: Slap House
genres.description: Taking influences from Brazilian Bass and Future House, characterized by prominent, "bouncy" bassline and simple, upbeat melodies.

genres.name: Bubbling House
genres.description: Developed in the Netherlands in the 2000s, combining the older style of Bubbling with more modern House, especially Dutch House.

genres.name: Changa tuki
genres.description: Emerged in Caracas; highly influenced by 1990s Techno and Tribal House, featuring fast tempos, strident synthesizers, hard-thumping percussion lines, and plenty of breakbeats.

genres.name: Chicago Hard House
genres.description: Originated from Chicago around the mid-1990s as a development of Ghetto House, emphasizing hard-hitting, off-beat drum patterns, fast tempos, and lack of melodies.

genres.name: LA Hard House
genres.description: Distorted, minimalistic TR-909 derived rhythms, basic climaxing structures and heavy reliance on high-pitched synthesizer / hoover sounds.

genres.name: Chicago House
genres.description: Umbrella term for a broad variety of House that originated from Chicago in the (mostly mid-to-late) 1980s and early 90s.

genres.name: Deep House
genres.description: Emerged in the United States during the mid-1980s, featuring a relaxed tempo and influences from Jazz, Funk, and Soul.
genres.track: Grand Central, Pt. I (Deep Into the Bowel of House)

genres.name: Lo-Fi House
genres.description: Primarily distinguished from earlier styles of outsider house by its stricter reliance on deep house elements, cranky, nocturnal, and nostalgic atmospheres, and a distinct dreamy, lo-fi aesthetic.

genres.name: Diva House
genres.description: Dominant, anthemic female vocals, common use of piano stabs, and energetic, driving four-on-the-floor rhythms.
genres.track: Love Is A State Of Mind (feat. Ramona Renae)

genres.name: Hardbag
genres.description: Development of handbag / Diva House characterized by heavier, hard hitting percussion, more pronounced rave and early Hard Dance elements, and fewer vocals.

genres.name: Electro House
genres.description: Warm analog basslines, punchy percussion, crisp high-pitched synthesizer leads, and clipped vocal samples.

genres.name: Complextro
genres.description: Features densely-layered sound design, fast-paced cut-up sections, aggressive stabs, and common crossover with Brostep and Fidget House.

genres.name: Dutch House
genres.description: High-pitched wonky synth melodies and heavy influence from Fidget House which developed in the Netherlands around 2007-08.

genres.name: Noiadance
genres.description: Blends Dutch House production with Funk brasileiro vocals and drumming on top of Moombahton rhythms.

genres.name: Fidget House
genres.description: Makes heavy use of Breakbeat Hardcore-esque synth stabs, pitch bending of basslines, and cut-up vocal samples, as well as glitchy, or "choppy", 4/4 rhythms.

genres.name: French Electro
genres.description: Mixes Electro House with major elements of genres such as Electroclash, Nu-Disco, Synth Funk, and even Electro-Industrial, resulting in a harsh, punchy, and funky midtempo sound.

genres.name: Melbourne Bounce
genres.description: Offbeat basslines giving it a "bouncy" groove, and minimalistic, side-chained melodies often making use of Dutch House-influenced synths, horns or vocal chops, resulting in a flippant, party-oriented atmosphere.

genres.name: Eletrofunk
genres.description: Blends Funk brasileiro vocals with production from popular late 2000s and early 2010s House.

genres.name: Euro House
genres.description: Vocal-focused style emerging in the late 1980s in Europe, developing in parallel with Eurodance.

genres.name: Festival Progressive House
genres.description: Uplifting, melodic, energetic but clean drops, featuring modern supersaws and pianos, taking influences from Progressive House, Uplifting Trance, but applying them to a form structurally closer to Big Room House and Electro House.

genres.name: French House
genres.description: Originated in France in the mid-1990s, characterized by the use of filtered (low-pass, phaser, etc.) samples of Funk and Disco.

genres.name: Funky House
genres.description: Funky, warm, catchy basslines on top of looped Funk or Disco samples, resulting in an upbeat, bouncy, and pacy groove.

genres.name: Future Funk
genres.description: Sample-based style influenced by French House and Synth Funk that utilizes Vaporwave editing techniques.

genres.name: Future House
genres.description: Features distinctive metallic-sounding drops and frequency-modulated basslines at around 120-130 BPM.

genres.name: Future Bounce
genres.description: Fusion of Melbourne Bounce and Future House that combines the former's basslines and bouncy, upbeat drops with the latter's metallic, pronounced synth leads.
genres.album: ネオンストライド 001 [Neon Stride 001]

genres.name: G-House
genres.description: Deep, dark form of House music that primarily incorporates rap samples or original rapping on top of minimal, bassy beats.

genres.name: Garage House
genres.description: Disco-influenced style of House that developed in the 1980s, incorporating elements of Gospel, Soul, and Dub, before evolving into a more upbeat style that prominently features crisp syncopated hi-hats and synth stabs.

genres.name: Gospel House
genres.description: Incorporates heavy Gospel elements and singing borrowed from classic and contemporary gospel, usually in the form of choir vocals and call-and-response chants.

genres.name: Jersey Sound
genres.description: Soulful, melodic, Gospel-infused House music developed in Newark, NJ in the late 1980s and early 1990s with an emphasis on songcraft.

genres.name: Ghetto House
genres.description: Rough sound based around minimal drum machine-driven tracks and heavy usage of vocal samples.
genres.track: In Da Club Before Eleven O' Clock

genres.name: Juke
genres.description: Faster than Ghetto House, playing at 160bpm, and makes striking use of unconventional drum patterns which differ wildly from other House styles.

genres.name: Hip House
genres.description: Incorporates production elements of early Hip Hop and usually rapping into 1980s House.

genres.name: Italo House
genres.description: Originated in Italy during the late 1980s, making use of anthemic pianos, diva vocals, and Dance-Pop song structures.

genres.name: Jackin' House
genres.description: Punchy, 'shuffly' percussion, strong grooves, funky basslines, and chopped-up samples.

genres.name: Kwaito
genres.description: Emerged from South Africa in the early 1990s, taking influence from Disco and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Bacardi
genres.description: Bacardi is a type of House music from South Africa derived from Kwaito, delivering upbeat, danceable rhythms with lively snares and hi-hats.

genres.name: Latin House
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Latin music (various Hispanic American Music and Brazilian Music genres), including their melodies, vocals, and instruments, as well as additional Latin percussion.

genres.name: Melodic House
genres.description: Arpeggiated synth lines, focus on a chilled and laid-back atmosphere, and influence from genres such as Progressive House and Deep House.

genres.name: Microhouse
genres.description: Stripped-down, minimal form of House, originating in the late 90s, which takes influence from Minimal Techno, Glitch and IDM.

genres.name: Organic House
genres.description: Subtle drums and grooves, slow tempos, and acoustic, traditional instrumentation, resulting in an organic, warm sound and spiritual atmosphere.

genres.name: Outsider House
genres.description: Mostly derived from Deep House; intentional use of rough, lo-fi production, often utilizing a mix of analog/analog-like and digital instrumentation.

genres.name: Phonk House
genres.description: Merges Drift Phonk's nocturnal atmospheres, cowbell melodies, vocal samples, and energetic production, with House rhythms and tempos, characterized by a banging and upbeat sound.

genres.name: Progressive House
genres.description: Trance-influenced strain of House that grew to prominence in the early 1990s, using polished production and gradual progressions.

genres.name: Speed Garage
genres.description: Primarily British style that paved the way for UK Garage, combining cut-up vocal samples and sped up four-on-the-floor Garage House rhythms with Jungle-esque basslines.

genres.name: Stutter House
genres.description: Emerged in the 2020s taking influences from Melodic House, Trance, and Future Garage; features distinctive chopping of vocal samples and pads.

genres.name: Tech House
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s taking influences from Techno, broadly characterized by minimalistic and repetitive melodies, focus on the bassline, and constant groove recognizable by prominent off-beat hi-hats.

genres.name: Deep Tech
genres.description: Incorporates UK Garage rhythms and synths stabs, influences from British rave music, UK Bass and UK Deep House, resulting in an urban, subdued, but danceable sound with deep, muted basslines.

genres.name: Rominimal
genres.description: Hypnotic, minimal, and "dubby" loops, featuring subtle and intricate synth pads, cranky, clicky percussion, and bouncy, pulsing basslines.

genres.name: Tribal House
genres.description: Prominent, syncopated rhythms of tribal drums such as toms and bongos on top of a House beat, usually resulting in a percussive, energetic sound, while ranging in mood.

genres.name: Guaracha [EDM]
genres.description: Originated in Colombia, featuring "fluttering" trumpets, accordion, and tambora drums.

genres.name: Tropical House
genres.description: Offshoot of Deep House featuring slow tempos around 100-115 BPM, light percussion and acoustic instrumentation, setting out to create a relaxed, summery, beach-like atmosphere.

genres.name: UK Jackin'
genres.description: Successor to British Bassline, characterized by strong basslines, dark atmospheres, and dominant grooves.

genres.name: Vinahouse
genres.description: Fast-paced House popular in Vietnam, remixing Vietnamese melodies.
genres.track: Ngủ Ngon Nhé Em - Club Mix

genres.name: Hyper Techno
genres.description: Exaggerated fast form of Belgian Techno for the Japanese market, focusing mainly on synth sounds and samples typical of 1990s dance music.

genres.name: Hypertechno
genres.description: Emerged in the 2020s by mixing fast tempos, prominent basslines, and hard-hitting drums derived from popular Techno with simplistic, catchy melodies and vocals, often influenced by 2000s Hard Dance, Eurodance and Electropop.

genres.name: Jungle Terror
genres.description: Emerging mostly from Dutch House and Big Room House, incorporates Tribal House-influenced percussion, hard kicks, and animal sounds resulting in a wild, jungle-resembling atmosphere in a festival EDM-oriented context.

genres.name: Krushclub
genres.description: Bitcrushed synths and occasionally bitcrushed vocals, energetic Jersey Club-derived beats, and elements of Sigilkore's dark production style.

genres.name: Kuduro
genres.description: Angolan music combining traditional Kilapanga and Semba with Techno and House.

genres.name: Batida
genres.description: Initially developed in the late '80s in Luanda, Angola, as a mixture of Soca- and Zouk-based percussion samples.

genres.name: Makina
genres.description: Spanish Techno developed in the early 1990s; strongly influenced by New Beat and EBM, but aiming for a lighter sound.

genres.name: Manyao
genres.description: Asian Electronic Dance Music that mixes vocals and melodies from Mandopop with fairly hard, melodic EDM.

genres.name: Melodic Bass
genres.description: Outgrowth of Melodic Dubstep with euphoric sound design taking influences from Future Bass, guitar melodies and pop-driven structures

genres.name: Midtempo Bass
genres.description: Harsh synth leads and a usual tempo of around 90-110 BPM.

genres.name: Moombahcore
genres.description: High-pitched synth leads, gritty percussion, a kick-snare pattern, aggressive bass drops, and around 110 BPM while often paralleling Complextro or Brostep.

genres.name: Moombahton
genres.description: Offshoot of Dutch House characterized by tempos in the 100-110 BPM range, Reggaetón-influenced rhythms, bass-heavy kicks and high-pitched synths.

genres.name: Nerdcore Techno
genres.description: Stylistically diverse form of underground Japanese Electronic Dance Music utilizing energetic beats built around samples from pop and/or nerd culture.

genres.name: Post-Dubstep
genres.description: Minimalistic, atmospheric sound design and eclectic drum patterns, derived from but not fitting Dubstep.

genres.name: Shangaan Electro
genres.description: South African genre with very fast BPM (around 180) featuring MIDI keyboard sounds and marimba.
genres.track: I Made You / You Made Me

genres.name: Singeli
genres.description: Developed in Tanzania in the mid-2000s; fuses incredibly rapid beats, usually between 180-300BPM, with MCing and musical influences from older Tanzanian genres.

genres.name: Skweee
genres.description: Mid-2000s offshoot of the Nordic Electro scene which uses simple, analogue or Chiptune-inspired synthesizer leads and basslines to create stripped-down, midtempo grooves drawing on Synth Funk and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Slimepunk
genres.description: Loud synth leads with a distorted, gritty, and "slimy" sound design, usually laid on top of production inspired by or taken directly from genres such as Halftime, Trap [EDM], Brostep, and other forms of 2010s EDM.

genres.name: Techno
genres.description: Highly beat-driven, repetitive, and mechanical, typically featuring minimal chord variation and melodies, focuses on rhythms and timbral variety; generally produced for club environments.
genres.album: OIL OF EVERY PEARL'S UN-INSIDES NON-STOP REMIX ALBUM

genres.name: Acid Techno
genres.description: Incorporates "squelching" synths from Acid House into a mechanical and usually more energetic Techno context.

genres.name: Ambient Techno
genres.description: Blends the mechanical, repetitive beats of Techno with atmospheres and textures inspired by Ambient music, resulting in slower tempos and more understated rhythms.

genres.name: Bleep Techno
genres.description: Established in the late 1980s in the breakdancing and early rave scene of Yorkshire in the North of England, notable for its "bleepy" synth lines and heavy sub-bass.

genres.name: Detroit Techno
genres.description: Features a signature mechanical, detached sound that echoed the atmosphere of Detroit's nightlife and incorporated influences from Electro and Chicago House as well as Synthpop and Electro-Disco.

genres.name: Freetekno
genres.description: Originated in the early 1990s, commonly played at free parties in Europe, and features a repetitive pounding kick drum at tempos of 170 BPM or above.

genres.name: Hard Techno
genres.description: Typically rave-oriented form characterized by hard, prominent kick drums, pounding rhythms, fast tempos around 140-160 BPM, and aggressive, often distorted sounds.

genres.name: Schranz
genres.description: Characterised by fast tempos, aggressive "whooshing" beat patterns, heavy compression and straightforward song structures.

genres.name: Hardgroove Techno
genres.description: Features shuffling grooves with heavy emphasis on layered percussive elements; often includes a mix of samples and drum machines played at a range of 135-140 BPM.

genres.name: Industrial Techno
genres.description: Harder, darker style of Techno which draws parallels with factories and the rhythm of machinery.

genres.name: Birmingham Sound
genres.description: Cold, mechanical, and hypnotic tracks, typically lacking the harsher and noisier elements of later Industrial Techno.

genres.name: Melodic Techno
genres.description: Trance-influenced subgenre that was established in the mid-to-late 2010s, characterized by gradually progressing structure, and hypnotizing, atmospheric sound with arpeggiated, minor melodies, playing at around 120-125 BPM.

genres.name: Minimal Techno
genres.description: Stripped-down and sparse, often featuring a dark sound and a slow, steady development through the track.

genres.name: Dub Techno
genres.description: Fuses elements of Minimal Techno with characteristics of Dub.

genres.name: Peak Time Techno
genres.description: Hard, dynamic, energetic and accessible subgenre featuring strong kicks, massive dirty synths, tempos around 130 BPM, more suspenseful structures with breaks and build-ups, and big, modern, festival-oriented sound; rose to high popularity in the late 2010s.

genres.name: Wonky Techno
genres.description: Strays from the standard beat of Techno, opting for a more fractured sound.

genres.name: Techno Bass
genres.description: Minimal, stripped-down with an emphasis on low-frequency bass partitions.

genres.name: Car Audio Bass
genres.description: Slow and minimalistic extreme form, focused on ultra-low frequency sine wave notes and mainly intended for stress testing subwoofer sound systems.

genres.name: Trance
genres.description: Evolving, tension-building structures with rapid, minor arpeggios on top of a hypnotic, four-on-the-floor drum patterns at fast tempo around 130-150 BPM.

genres.name: Acid Trance
genres.description: Incorporates "squelching" acid basslines into Trance's evolving structure.

genres.name: Big Room Trance
genres.description: Incorporates production features associated with Big Room House and dirty, distorted leads influenced by Electro House, Dutch House and Hardstyle.
genres.track: This Is What It Feels Like

genres.name: Dream Trance
genres.description: Slow tempo (about 130 BPM) with strong roots in Progressive House, using beats typical of Eurodance and Dance-Pop; emphasizes a laid-back, carefree, and dreamlike sound.

genres.name: Euro Trance
genres.description: Emerged as a fusion with Eurodance, features fast tempos, more accessible grooves and structures, and simple, catchy melodies with vocals and saw synth leads.

genres.name: Hands Up
genres.description: Prominent, melodic supersaw leads, Dance-Pop derived hooks, and a strong reliance on sidechained basslines and hard, powerful drums.

genres.name: Buchiage Trance
genres.description: Japanese style that emerged in Shibuya's club scene in the 2000s and was primarily marketed to gyaru, infused with melodic and rhythmic influence from Eurobeat.

genres.name: Hi-Tech Full-On
genres.description: Largely Japanese genre with an energetic and glitchy sound derived from Full-On Psytrance and Complextro.

genres.name: Ibiza Trance
genres.description: Builds on the relaxing island atmosphere of Balearic Beat, though with a slightly faster tempo of around 130 BPM.
genres.track: Don't Give Up - Chicane Lockdown Remix

genres.name: Progressive Trance
genres.description: Combination of Trance and Progressive House which emerged in Western Europe in the early to mid-1990s.

genres.name: Psytrance
genres.description: Emphasizes a psychedelic feel and an energetic sound; based around influences from Goa Trance and Acid Trance.

genres.name: Dark Psytrance
genres.description: Uses more complex sound design based on dark atmospheres and fast tempos.
genres.track: Travelling At The Speed Of Thought

genres.name: Hi-Tech Psytrance
genres.description: Glitchy sound design, morphing synth lines, strange sounds typically evoking futuristic or alien-like atmospheres, and faster tempos than most other forms of Psytrance.

genres.name: Psycore
genres.description: Pushes the dark atmospheres of Dark Psytrance to the extreme through the usage of exceptionally high tempos and experimental soundscapes influenced by Dark Ambient and Glitch.

genres.name: Forest Psytrance
genres.description: Mimicks the ambience of a forest by using swarming and teeming effects as well as natural samples; features straightforward song structures.

genres.name: Full-On Psytrance
genres.description: Faster and more intense, usually set around 145-150 BPM and featuring harder rolling basslines, vocal samples and "spacey" effects.

genres.name: Goa Trance
genres.description: Forerunner of Psytrance styles that emerged in the early 1990s, distinguished by old-school, organic sound with rapid, oriental-inspired melodies.

genres.name: Nitzhonot
genres.description: Fast-paced, featuring rapid melodic lines and usually hard and high-pitched kicks.

genres.name: Progressive Psytrance
genres.description: Emerged in the early 2000s, featuring a slow tempo range and clean production.

genres.name: Zenonesque
genres.description: Experimental and leftfield approach to Progressive Psytrance, mixing the atmospheric and clean Psytrance production typical of it with funky and jazzy elements.

genres.name: Suomisaundi
genres.description: Finnish-based deviation of Psytrance with an emphasis on free-form experimentation and humor.

genres.name: Tech Trance
genres.description: Late 1990s-emerging subgenre characterized by energetic percussion with loud kicks, filtered hi-hats and tribal drums; side-chained, detuned and repetitive leads, as well as other raw, distorted, and complex sounds influenced by Techno, Hard Trance and Electro House.

genres.name: Uplifting Trance
genres.description: Euphoric melodies, buildup-breakdown-anthem structures, common usage of supersaws, and a BPM range of usually around 135-142.

genres.name: Vocal Trance
genres.description: Melodic, polished, Pop-like, and vocal-focused with around 120-145 BPM and frequent overlap with Progressive Trance, Uplifting Trance, and Euro Trance.

genres.name: Trap [EDM]
genres.description: Trap-influenced syncopated percussion with 808 samples and fast-paced hi-hats.
genres.album: F*CK U SKRILLEX YOU THINK UR ANDY WARHOL BUT UR NOT!! <3

genres.name: Festival Trap
genres.description: Massive, sub-bass-heavy drops with simple melodies, synth leads and production influenced by Big Room House; highly popular from 2013 to 2015.

genres.name: Hard Trap
genres.description: Often abrasive subgenre of Trap [EDM] with heavy influence from Hardstyle.

genres.name: Heaven Trap
genres.description: Blends Trap [EDM]’s signature percussion and sub-basses with euphoric, uplifting, melodious drops prominently derived from Festival Progressive House, contrary to the gritty, "dirty" nature of other EDM trap styles.

genres.name: Hybrid Trap
genres.description: Blending Trap [EDM]'s typical percussion and sub-basses with major influences from heavy bass music genres, and in particular, metallic, gritty, and off-kilter sound design, originally derived from Brostep.

genres.name: Twerk
genres.description: Fast-paced; draws influence from Bounce and Miami Bass.

genres.name: Tribal Guarachero
genres.description: Features percussion from Cumbia and Mexican Folk Music with upbeat Electro House-derived production and fast, triplet-oriented rhythmic patterns.

genres.name: UK Bass
genres.description: Prominent bass/sub-basses, a deep, dark, airy, and mechanical sound derived from Dubstep, and eclectic production influenced by UK Funky, Juke/Footwork, Techno, and Breakbeat.

genres.name: UK Funky
genres.description: Influenced by UK Garage-related styles and the regional styles of British immigrants, including Soca and West African-inspired Tribal House.

genres.name: UK Garage
genres.description: Shuffling rhythms and influences from sources including Contemporary R&B and Hip Hop, as well as many forms of Electronic.

genres.name: 2-Step
genres.description: Originating in London and popular in the late 1990s; jittery, shuffling rhythms rarely following a four-on-the-floor pattern.
genres.track: Friendly Pressure - Into The Sunshine Mix

genres.name: Breakstep
genres.description: Hard-hitting Breakbeat rhythms and heavy, rolling basslines.

genres.name: Future Garage
genres.description: Combines the rhythms of late 1990s and early 2000s 2-Step with novel moods and production approaches, commonly featuring jittery, broken rhythms, vocal chops, and warm synth pads and plucks.

genres.name: Wonky
genres.description: Off-kilter fusion of Dubstep and Hip Hop which first developed in the mid-to-late 2000s.

genres.name: Aquacrunk
genres.description: Syncopated, half-time rhythms inspired by Dubstep and Grime, funky, sludgy, "aquatic"-sounding synths and sound design.

genres.name: Miami Bass
genres.description: Sustained Roland TR-808 kick drums and faster tempos, along with a distinct Electro influence.

genres.name: Atlanta Bass
genres.description: Originated in Atlanta, slower tempos and a more melodic approach than Miami Bass.
genres.album: レディー・フォー・ザ・ワールド [Ready for the World]

genres.name: Tamborzão
genres.description: Adds Afro-Brazilian percussive elements such as the atabaque sound into the Miami Bass kick drums.

genres.name: Wa Euro
genres.description: Traditional form of J-Pop that emerged in the second half of the 1980s from late Hi-NRG, '80s British Dance-Pop and Italo-Disco/Eurobeat.

genres.name: Easy Listening
genres.description: Typically instrumental, including lush arrangements and melodies played by orchestras or big bands aiming for light entertainment.

genres.name: Cocktail Nation
genres.description: Decidedly ironic take on Lounge that emerged in the early 1990s.

genres.name: Exotica
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1950s as the United States developed a fascination with Polynesia and the South Pacific, incorporates traditional instruments and rhythms from these cultures into a Western Pop context.

genres.name: Sitarsploitation
genres.description: Variant of Exotica capitalising on the surge of Western interest in Indian music in the late 1960s; featured melodies played on the sitar (or instruments imitating it) atop Easy Listening accompaniment.

genres.name: Lounge
genres.description: Emerged in the United States during the 1950s, emphasizing a chilled-out atmosphere with light instrumentation and sometimes vocals indebted to Vocal Jazz.

genres.name: Pops Orchestra
genres.description: Orchestra that plays covers of popular songs as well as famous classical compositions.

genres.name: Space Age Pop
genres.description: Inspired by the excitement and optimism of the Space Age during the 1950s and 1960s, frequently experimenting with futuristic sounds made possible by contemporary technology.

genres.name: Electronic
genres.description: Uses non-traditional electronic instrumentation and sound manipulation technology as the primary backbone of a composition.

genres.name: Acholitronix
genres.description: Fusion of traditional Acholi rhythms and melodies with Electronic production, originating in the city of Gulu.

genres.name: Algorave
genres.description: Generative dancefloor-oriented music produced live via algorithms.

genres.name: Binaural Beats
genres.description: Auditory illusions created when two different frequencies are played simultaneously in separate ears.

genres.name: Bit Music
genres.description: Created by sound chips, cards, and sequencers found in video game consoles, personal computers, and arcade machines, as well as synthesizers emulating these sounds.

genres.name: Chiptune
genres.description: Used primarily in the 1980s within the context of 8-bit Video Game Music, combining simple synthesized waveforms and noise in a compositionally limited but overtly melodic style.
genres.album: スーパーマリオワールド [Super Mario World]

genres.name: FM Synthesis
genres.description: Sound synthesis that combines the simple waveforms of Chiptune with modulating oscillators to create a bouncier synthesizer sound that would be used in arcade cabinets and home video game consoles like the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis in the late 1980s.

genres.name: MIDI Music
genres.description: Intended for real-time sequenced playback via MIDI protocol on MIDI devices and used primarily in 1990s PC Video Game Music, arranger keyboards and karaoke.
genres.album: 夢違科学世紀 ～ Changeability of Strange Dream

genres.name: Black MIDI
genres.description: Consists of extremely dense MIDI piano compositions, impossible to play on physical instruments.

genres.name: Sequencer & Tracker
genres.description: Composed for early home computer and game consoles from the late 1980s to the late 1990s, primarily for video game soundtracks.

genres.name: 16-bit
genres.description: Created using video game consoles with audio hardware using 16-bit audio samples, most notably the Super Nintendo Entertainment System.

genres.name: Tracker Music
genres.description: Vertical text-based step-sequencer software sampler music in the first and second gen module formats like .MOD, .MED, .S3M, .XM and .IT.

genres.name: Demostyle
genres.description: Traditional eclectic style of the Demoscene with a special emphasis on tracker techniques and samples, and combining numerous elements of completely different genres - from Italo-Disco, Progressive Electronic and Funk to Belgian Techno, Ambient and Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Bitpop
genres.description: Fuses Bit Music with additional synths, beats, guitars and modern production values, emphasizing highly catchy melodies and relatively fast tempos.
