genres.name: Celtic Electronica
genres.description: Fusion of Celtic Folk Music with various types of Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Chillout
genres.description: Broad category of many relaxed styles of Electronic music which predominantly draw influence from Electronic Dance Music subgenres and Ambient.

genres.name: Ambient Dub
genres.description: Takes cues from Ambient and Dub reggae, featuring the atmosphere of the former and the Jamaican-style basslines, percussion, and psychedelic production techniques of the latter.

genres.name: Ambient Trance
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1990s mainly in the form of Chillout remixes of Trance tracks; incorporates its arpeggiated synthesizer sound into Downtempo and Ambient contexts.

genres.name: Barber Beats
genres.description: Borrows elements from Downtempo, Trip Hop, and Instrumental Hip Hop; emulates 1990s and 2000s Chillout music.

genres.name: Downtempo
genres.description: Atmospheric and groove-based with relaxed tempos and mellow beats.

genres.name: Trip Hop
genres.description: Evokes a surreal, trippy, dreamy, and sometimes dark atmosphere with offbeat turntable scratches, light vocal melodies, and Hip Hop-influenced beats.

genres.name: Psybient
genres.description: Heavy influence from Psytrance and Goa Trance incorporated in an atmospheric Ambient context.

genres.name: Digital Fusion
genres.description: Incorporates the hardware-limited sounds of Chiptune and other Bit Music into compositions drawing on Jazz, Cinematic Classical, progressive music, and other Electronic styles, sometimes augmented with live instrumentation.

genres.name: Drift Phonk
genres.description: Busy, noisy production inspired by lo-fi Memphis Rap; frequently features 808 cowbell melodies and chopped, compressed samples.

genres.name: Dungeon Synth
genres.description: Focuses on evoking epic and atmospheric soundscapes primarily associated with fantasy and medieval settings through the usage of synthesizers, keyboards, lo-fi production, and drum machines.

genres.name: Comfy Synth
genres.description: Calm, peaceful and soothing sounds, as well as nostalgic, sentimental, or childish atmospheres and aesthetics; often incorporates wholesome themes while utilizing lo-fi or hazy recordings and influences from New Age.

genres.name: Winter Synth
genres.description: Cold, minimalistic, and repetitive soundscapes, commonly invoking imagery of winter.

genres.name: Electro Hop
genres.description: Emerged in the mid 2000s featuring upbeat rap verses and catchy hooks over four-on-the-floor Electropop and Electro House-inspired production.

genres.name: Electro-Industrial
genres.description: Formed in the late 1980s and early 1990s; grew out of a combination of EBM and Industrial.

genres.name: Electroacoustic
genres.description: Manipulation and processing of sound sources to create atmospheric pieces.

genres.name: Acousmatic Music
genres.description: Fixed-media Electroacoustic music designed to be reproduced by multiple loudspeakers without the presence of instrumentalists and visual cues.

genres.name: EAI
genres.description: Slow paced, physical, textured aesthetic - often created using unconventional instruments processed through a computer.

genres.name: Musique concrète
genres.description: Manipulation of recorded sounds, mostly Field Recordings, natural sounds, and real-world noises, as a process of abstracting "concrete" sounds, or "sound objects", from their acoustic origins.

genres.name: Electropop
genres.description: Dense, layered, and compressed production, usually coupled with a distinct fuzzy and "warm" low-frequency synthesizer style.

genres.name: Epic Collage
genres.description: Cinematic, dense digital collage; frequently utilizes a Deconstructed Club sonic palette and decontextualized novel samples.

genres.name: Flashcore
genres.description: Fast-paced short sounds, complex structures with erratic progression, and often dense and atmospheric abstract sound design, featuring recontextualized elements from IDM, Speedcore, Industrial Hardcore, and Breakcore.
genres.track: For Liza, beyond the event horizon.
genres.album: For Liza, beyond the event horizon.

genres.name: Folktronica
genres.description: Combines sound design techniques from IDM and Glitch with acoustic instrumentation inspired by Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Funktronica
genres.description: Originated in eastern North America around the turn of the 21st century, combining trends of Synth Funk and Italo-Disco.

genres.name: Glitch
genres.description: Uses abstract sound design and malfunctioning electronics—CD skips, data corruption, and hardware noise—as main compositional elements.

genres.name: Glitch Hop
genres.description: Incorporation of IDM-derived production into drum patterns inspired by Hip Hop beats.
genres.album: By the Time I Get to Phoenix

genres.name: Graphical Sound
genres.description: Compositional technique in which markings are manually applied to a medium, then processed by a machine to produce synthetic sound from the markings in real time.
genres.album: Solaris, The Mirror, Stalker: Music From Motion Pictures

genres.name: HexD
genres.description: Heavily bit-crushed, sometimes sped-up and pitched-up vocals, and highly compressed, distorted production, typically using preexisting material from other genres.

genres.name: Horror Synth
genres.description: Combines eerie and haunting synth pads and sharp, abrasive sounds to create atmospheres that accentuated the dark, unnerving, violent, or ghostly themes of horror films.

genres.name: Hyperpop
genres.description: Developed and took inspiration from Bubblegum Bass and popular 2000s-2010s Electropop, characterized by eclectic, unconventional, mechanical-sounding and dense production; and by manipulated, usually auto-tuned vocals.

genres.name: IDM
genres.description: Emerged through the development of Electronic Dance Music idioms into a less club-oriented and more experimental direction, often incorporating unconventional sound design and complex rhythms.
genres.album: Music Has The Right To Children

genres.name: Drill and Bass
genres.description: Frenzied, intricate beat programming inspired by Drum and Bass.

genres.name: Illbient
genres.description: Combines Ambient soundscapes with Hip Hop drum patterns, breaks, and samples through the busy effect layering of Dub.

genres.name: Indietronica
genres.description: Leftfield or DIY approach characterised by simpler Pop-informed melodies, often incorporating vocals or live instrumentation alongside Electronic production.

genres.name: Chillwave
genres.description: Emulates vintage aesthetics and popular musical styles of the 1980s/1990s altered by modern recording technology to create a hazy dreamlike atmosphere.

genres.name: Chillsynth
genres.description: Mixes Synthwave with major Chillwave elements, characterized by a dreamy and relaxed sound.

genres.name: Glitch Pop
genres.description: Incorporates elements of more experimental Electronic styles like IDM and Glitch.

genres.name: Picopop
genres.description: Originated in the early 2000s as an offshoot of the Japanese Shibuya-kei movement when artists introduced more prominent "bleepy" electronic elements and faster tempos.

genres.name: Latin Electronic
genres.description: Combines Electronic with Latin American influences; started at the end of the 1990s.
genres.album: The Light That You Gave Me to See You

genres.name: Electrotango
genres.description: Combines Tango rhythms and melodies with Electronic music.

genres.name: Nortec
genres.description: Samples and synthesizes Mexican styles like Banda sinaloense and Norteño into a sound related to IDM and House.

genres.name: Livetronica
genres.description: Incorporates Electronic instrumentation into live Rock jamming, drawing on a wide variety of Electronic Dance Music and Downtempo styles.

genres.name: Maloya électronique
genres.description: Combines the 6/8 ternary rhythm with Electronic production, using computer music, synthesizers and drum machines.

genres.name: Micromontage
genres.description: Arrangement of microsounds on an incredibly small time scale.

genres.name: Minimal Wave
genres.description: Retrospective term for more Electronic and minimal forms of New Wave, Post-Punk, Synthpop, and related styles, tending towards a more sparse and lo-fi sound.

genres.name: Minimal Synth
genres.description: Minimal and distinctly DIY take on Synthpop with a bleak and naive aesthetic.

genres.name: Moogsploitation
genres.description: Moog synthesizer-led music often associated with a wave of Novelty records in the 1960s and 1970s.
genres.track: Title Music From A Clockwork Orange (From Purcell's "Music for the Funeral of Queen Mary")

genres.name: Nightcore
genres.description: Based around the technique of speeding and pitching up pre-existing songs.

genres.name: Nu Jazz
genres.description: Electronic styles which feature aesthetics and occasionally instrumentation inspired by Jazz.

genres.name: Power Electronics
genres.description: Waves of feedback, screeching analog synthesizers, and harsh, screamed vocals.

genres.name: Death Industrial
genres.description: Combines the abrasive textures of Noise and Industrial music with dark, brooding drones and atmospheres.
genres.track: For I Am The Light (And Mine Is The Only Way)

genres.name: Power Noise
genres.description: Combines looped samples of Noise with Electronic rhythms.

genres.name: Progressive Electronic
genres.description: Synthesizer-driven genre focusing on developing, often longform compositions and drawing inspiration from various sources such as Progressive Rock, Western Classical Music, and Ambient.

genres.name: Berlin School
genres.description: Atmospheric, multi-layered synthesizer textures; pioneered in Berlin in the 1970s as an offshoot to the Krautrock movement.

genres.name: Synth Punk
genres.description: Appropriates the harsh elements of Punk Rock but replaces the predominance of guitars with synthesizers and drum machines.

genres.name: Synthpop
genres.description: Led by melodic synthesizer sounds, often with reverberating drum machine patterns; commonly associated with the 1980s.

genres.name: Pon-chak disco
genres.description: Heavily influenced by Electro-Disco, featuring cheap "electronic organ" synth leads and minimalistic, repetitive rhythms.

genres.name: Techno kayō
genres.description: Offshoot of 1980s Kayōkyoku and Idol kayō incorporating characteristics from Synthpop.

genres.name: Synthwave
genres.description: Rooted in 1980s synth music, characterized by large, throbbing "retro" synths and visual elements, often features upbeat percussion and/or epic, cinematic atmospheres.

genres.name: Darksynth
genres.description: Incorporates atmospheric Horror Synth and faster tempos into a much heavier and darker sound.

genres.name: Sovietwave
genres.description: Scene of Synthwave that emerged in the early 2010s, taking its inspiration from Soviet Electronic electronic music and Soviet pop.

genres.name: Tecnobrega
genres.description: Fast and electronic-based style that evolved from Brega calypso, particularly associated with peripheral areas of the city of Belém.

genres.name: Tecnofunk
genres.description: Raw and vulgar Tecnobrega and Funk brasileiro fusion developed in the late 2010s by DJs in Belém do Pará.

genres.name: Vapor
genres.description: Meta-genre beginning with the rise of Vaporwave and the aesthetics that it spawned.

genres.name: Dreampunk
genres.description: Accentuates ambiance and a dreamy, futuristic atmosphere, taking influence from Progressive Electronic, as well as Cyberpunk and Dystopian movies.
genres.album: 新しい日の誕生 [Birth of a New Day]

genres.name: Utopian Virtual
genres.description: Emulates late 20th century futuristic and corporate aesthetics, often using "tacky"-sounding instruments likened to MIDI Music, in contrast to Vaporwave's sample-based approach.

genres.name: Vapornoise
genres.description: Uses Noise and other avant-garde techniques not typically found in Vaporwave.
genres.track: Enchanted Encryption of The Subconscious Mind
genres.album: My Detrimental Wormhole, Vin Diesel. Telepathic Gothika Issue #3

genres.name: Vaportrap
genres.description: Incorporates a blend of Trap percussion set to the re-utilization of old samples, such as 1990s pop culture or old computer library sounds.

genres.name: Vaporwave
genres.description: Sample-based, involving heavily synthesized and processed manipulation of corporate mood and background (elevator) music, though source material can also include Pop, Contemporary R&B, and Synth Funk.
genres.artist: テレパシー能力者 [t e l e p a t h]

genres.name: Broken Transmission
genres.description: Manipulates samples from TV broadcasts, advertisements, film, radio, and other sources.

genres.name: Eccojams
genres.description: Simple, prototypical Vaporwave style, heavily influenced by Chopped and Screwed and Glitch, that features short, slowed-down, lyric focused, sampled loops smothered in reverb and continuously repeated, usually taken from late 20th century music.

genres.name: Mallsoft
genres.description: Blends the main characteristics of Vaporwave with what can be described as background/elevator music.
genres.artist: Cat System Corp. 猫 シ Corp.

genres.name: Slushwave
genres.description: Utilizes a distinct form of sample manipulation to create a “slushy” sound, usually sequenced in soft Ambient-based soundscapes.

genres.name: Wave
genres.description: Melancholic, atmospheric, melodic beats, defined by its Trap and Cloud Rap influence, ethereal and cold production style, and abundant use of sub bass.
genres.album: things will be better from now on

genres.name: Witch House
genres.description: Nocturnal, occult-themed/horror-inspired, and murky beats with altered, slowed down and heavily processed samples laid on top of slow Hip Hop-derived drum rhythms and droning, dense synthesizers.

genres.name: Experimental
genres.description: Most radical approaches throughout history, featuring non-traditional production methods resulting in sounds and styles that go largely beyond traditional boundaries.

genres.name: Conducted Improvisation
genres.description: Collective improvisation directed by a conductor.
genres.artist: Sun Ra and His Myth Science Arkestra

genres.name: Data Sonification
genres.description: Usage of data to create sound, soundscapes and music mostly as a way to illustrate its information.
genres.track: So You Want To Write A Fugue

genres.name: Drone
genres.description: Focuses on long, sustained tones and tone clusters, or repetition of single notes.

genres.name: Free Improvisation
genres.description: Improvised music which, in descending from Free Jazz and classical Indeterminacy, further abandons the prescriptions of harmonic or rhythmic structures which characterized those genres.

genres.name: Industrial
genres.description: Emerged out of Punk and avant-garde art movements in the mid-1970s, often characterized by a bleak, mechanical atmosphere, the use of metallic percussion as well as other unconventional instruments, and extensive use of sampling influenced by Musique concrète.

genres.name: Modern Creative
genres.description: Style of semi-improvisation that derives heavily from both the composition of Modern Classical and the techniques of Avant-Garde Jazz.
genres.album: Intents and Purposes: The Jazz Artistry of Bill Dixon

genres.name: Noise
genres.description: Strays away from conventional structure, tonality, and composition and consists predominantly of noise.

genres.name: Ambient Noise Wall
genres.description: Soft, sparse textures inspired by the static composition of Harsh Noise Wall.
genres.album: イルミラージュ・ソーダ 〜終わる世界と夏の夢〜

genres.name: Black Noise
genres.description: Incorporates unconventional sounds with overpowering or constant Noise and Black Metal elements, often being heavily texture-oriented, abrasive, dissonant, atonal, or repetitive.
genres.track: The Great Escape From Capricorn City
genres.album: civilization is the tomb of our noble gods

genres.name: Gorenoise
genres.description: Combines and subverts Goregrind and Grindcore with brash Noise and even faster drum tempos.

genres.name: Harsh Noise
genres.description: Highly aggressive walls of sound that assault the listener.

genres.name: Harsh Noise Wall
genres.description: Harsh, distorted walls of sound that feature few dynamic variations and often take the form of long compositions with little to no change or progression over time.

genres.name: Plunderphonics
genres.description: Compositional technique of utilizing and manipulating one or more recognizable recordings to create a new composition.

genres.name: Reductionism
genres.description: Experimental music that centers around quiet dynamics and use of silence.

genres.name: Lowercase
genres.description: Centered around the digital amplification and processing of quiet sounds.

genres.name: Onkyo
genres.description: Exploration of the physical traits of sound rather than music as expression.

genres.name: Sound Art
genres.description: Incorporates elements from Experimental music and visual arts, with sound utilized as its primary medium and subject.

genres.name: Sound Collage
genres.description: Compositional method emphasizing the rough layering of sampled elements, presenting an impression similar to a visual collage.
genres.album: 革命京劇 Ver.1.28 [Revolutionary Pekinese Opera Ver.1.28]

genres.name: Sound Poetry
genres.description: Emphasis is placed upon phonetics and the sounds of syllables rather than the meaning of the words themselves.

genres.name: Tape Music
genres.description: Explores the nature of audio recorded to magnetic tape and the act of playing sound from it.

genres.name: Turntable Music
genres.description: Has its roots in the early half of the twentieth century, with experimental artists using the turntable (as well as the vinyl records it plays) as a distinct instrument in the creation of compositions.
genres.track: 悲しき天使 (Those Were the Days)

genres.name: Folk
genres.description: Rooted in mostly oral traditions of the peoples of the world, encompassing international Traditional Folk Music as well as Western Contemporary Folk which arose in the 1940s.

genres.name: Contemporary Folk
genres.description: Generally acoustic and rooted in modernized Traditional Folk Music; originated with the 20th-century American folk revival.
genres.track: In the Aeroplane Over the Sea
genres.album: In the Aeroplane Over the Sea

genres.name: American Primitivism
genres.description: Blends avant-garde and neo-classical compositions with traditional Country Blues fingerpicking techniques.

genres.name: Anti-Folk
genres.description: Rawer approach to folk, with an often self-mocking and sarcastic tone.
genres.album: Divorce Lawyers I Shaved My Head

genres.name: Avant-Folk
genres.description: Experimental-influenced and playing with instrumentation, rhythm, and other factors not commonly found in folk.
genres.album: the dance of the moon and the sun

genres.name: Free Folk
genres.description: Incorporates improvisation, repetition and extended song lengths.
genres.album: Night Coercion into the Company of Witches

genres.name: Campus Folk
genres.description: Born in Taiwan in the mid-1970s, this movement originated with university students creating their own modern-style songs in the wake of international tensions like Taiwan's isolation from the United Nations and the United States' embrace of the PRC as a diplomatic partner.
genres.album: 之乎者也 [Chih Hu Che Yeh]

genres.name: Chamber Folk
genres.description: Gentle fingerpicked acoustic guitar or harp-led music that commonly includes a backing ensemble of harpsichords, strings, horns, or other orchestral instruments.

genres.name: Folk Baroque
genres.description: Originated in England in the early 1960s, featuring a distinctive guitar fingerpicking style of the same name and the DADGAD guitar tuning.

genres.name: Folk Pop
genres.description: Blends Contemporary Folk with a Pop sensibility, most popular in the late 1960s and early 1970s and featuring influence from the contemporary Folk Rock style.

genres.name: Stomp and Holler
genres.description: Highlights driving "stomping" rhythms and shouted group vocal harmonies, often drawing influences from Pop Rock, Indie Folk, and other genres, while maintaining a characteristically mellow and commercial sound.

genres.name: Indie Folk
genres.description: Combines the melodic sensibilities and production style of Indie Rock and Indie Pop with acoustic instrumentation and influences from Folk, Singer-Songwriter, and sometimes Country.

genres.name: Loner Folk
genres.description: Lo-fi, downbeat, and frequently depressive atmosphere with psychedelic undertones that emerged among independent creators following the collapse of the counterculture in the 1970s.

genres.name: Neofolk
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s from the Post-Industrial scene, with a dark, often martial atmosphere.
genres.album: White Light from the Mouth of Infinity

genres.name: Dark Folk
genres.description: Minimalistic and melancholic sound with influence from Nordic Folk Music and even Ambient.

genres.name: Neofolklore
genres.description: Short-lived movement that reincorporated traditional Chilean folklore into modern production and styling inspired by foreign musicians.

genres.name: Progressive Folk
genres.description: Draws from a variety of sources to subvert traditional acoustic song forms, with diversity ranging from Jazz to Medieval music to various Regional Music traditions.

genres.name: Psychedelic Folk
genres.description: Acoustic forms that capture an atmosphere that is at turns dream-like, 'spaced-out', whimsical, haunting, mystical, and melancholic.

genres.name: Freak Folk
genres.description: Loosely defined 2000s Psychedelic Folk revival closely associated with the New Weird America movement, sometimes also a shorthand for certain leftfield styles of psychedelic and Indie Folk.

genres.name: Udigrudi
genres.description: Movement that emerged in the Brazilian city of Recife during the 1970s that combines psychedelic elements with music of Northeastern Brazil.
genres.artist: Lula Côrtes e Lailson de Holanda

genres.name: Wyrd Folk
genres.description: Closely tied to mysticism, old folk beliefs, and Folk Horror; often described as 'witchy' or 'pagan.'

genres.name: Skiffle
genres.description: Grew out of British Trad Jazz, drawing influence from 1920s Jug Bands and the strong rhythms of 1950s Honky Tonk and Rock & Roll.

genres.name: Traditional Folk Music
genres.description: Informed by a long history of tradition in a specific culture or region, mostly associated with the peasantry and non-aristocratic public.

genres.name: African Folk Music
genres.description: Indigenous music of Africa that is passed down orally from generation to generation, the authors of the songs are usually unknown.
genres.artist: Ashanti Tribe Of Ghana / Ewe Tribe Of Ghana

genres.name: Ambasse bey
genres.description: African Folk Music developed by the Yabassi people of Cameroon.

genres.name: Apala
genres.description: Yoruba Music developed by Muslims during the late 1930s and early 1940s in the Ijebu region of Yorubaland, the current Ogun state.

genres.name: Batuque
genres.description: Tradition from Cape Verde, unusual among the islands' music due to its lack of polyphonic singing and its usage of polyrhythms.

genres.name: Dagomba Music
genres.description: Music of the Dagomba people of northern Ghana.

genres.name: Gnawa
genres.description: A mystical musical tradition centred around the qraqab castanets and guembri bass lute, named after its originators, the Afro-Maghrebi Gnawa people.

genres.name: Malagasy Folk Music
genres.description: Melodic, chordophone-dominated sound; based on the Austronesian Music of the first settlers that arrived on the island from Borneo.

genres.name: Mbenga-Mbuti Music
genres.description: Music of the Mbenga and Mbuti people, Pygmy ethnic groups in Central Africa.
genres.track: Nzombi (Music for the Return from a Hunt)

genres.name: Ngoma
genres.description: Played in Swahili-speaking African countries; primarily focused on rhythm.

genres.name: Southern African Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of southern Africa.
genres.album: Afrique du Sud: Le chant des femmes Xhosa

genres.name: Afrikaner Folk Music
genres.description: Musical traditions developed by the Afrikaner community in southern Africa.
genres.artist: Josef Marais and His Bushveld Band
genres.album: Songs of the South African Veld

genres.name: Khoisan Folk Music
genres.description: Encompasses traditions of the Khoisan ethnic family groups.
genres.track: Gut Pluriarc with Three Men's Voices
genres.album: Instrumental Music of the Kalahari San

genres.name: Nguni Folk Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Nguni ethnic family groups, a southern Bantu ethnicity.

genres.name: Sotho-Tswana Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Sotho-Tswana ethnic family groups from southern Africa.

genres.name: Tchinkoumé
genres.description: Tradition from the central region of Benin around Savalou, played with water percussion.

genres.name: Traditional Maloya
genres.description: Derived from Traditional Séga, this is the original dance music of La Réunion.

genres.name: Traditional Séga
genres.description: Séga dance music born in the 18th century, before its later adoption of Western pop elements.

genres.name: Zinli
genres.description: Traditional rhythmic chanting and percussion adapted to multiple West African contexts in the 20th century.

genres.name: American Folk Music
genres.description: Traces back through the history of European and West African settlement and migration to North America, including parts of northern Mexico and Canada in addition to the United States.

genres.name: Appalachian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk of the Appalachian Mountains in the Eastern United States.

genres.name: Old-Time
genres.description: Pre-Bluegrass North American string band styles, particularly those rooted in Appalachian Folk Music.

genres.name: Field Hollers
genres.description: Created by African-American slaves working on cotton plantations, featuring expressive vocals to no strict rhythm.
genres.artist: Big Louisiana, Willy Rafus & Arthur Davis

genres.name: Ring Shout
genres.description: Ritual practiced by African-Americans in the US South, characterized by shouting, chanting and people dancing in a circle while praying and clapping.
genres.album: Slave Shout Songs from the Coast of Georgia

genres.name: Sacred Harp Singing
genres.description: Predominantly 19th-century English hymns with tunes derived from old folk melodies.
genres.artist: The Old Harp Singers of Eastern Tennessee

genres.name: Spiritual
genres.description: African American folk song based around Christian themes, originating during enslavement and emphasizing solidarity and freedom; musical features include call-and-response, "blue" notes, and expressive vocal timbres.
genres.track: Dig My Grave with a Silver Spade

genres.name: Talking Blues
genres.description: American Folk Music with spoken or nearly spoken vocals; often features dry humor and social commentary.
genres.track: Dusty Old Dust (So Long It's Been Good to Know Yuh)

genres.name: Traditional Black Gospel
genres.description: Born out of Spiritual in the early 20th century with influence from Southern Gospel and Blues, often featuring passionate or energetic vocal performances, motifs of salvation, and testaments of hardship.

genres.name: Traditional Cajun Music
genres.description: Earliest and most "pure" form of Cajun Music, employing basic rhythms and frequent fiddle double stops.
genres.album: the good times are killing me

genres.name: Arabic Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Arabic people.

genres.name: Aita
genres.description: Arabic Folk Music from rural Morocco with piercing singing, scratchy viola, and rollicking hand drums.
genres.track: Suwwel ya L-Kubida / 'Ala Qablu Jaya / Ghzali Ghzali / Rja' Ya L-Mkhasmni

genres.name: Arabic Bellydance Music
genres.description: Accompaniment to traditional belly dances.

genres.name: Raqs baladi
genres.description: Egyptian folk dance and its associated musical accompaniment, appearing in the 20th century.

genres.name: Ayyalah
genres.description: Traditional Khaliji-Bedouin weapon performance, commonly found across the United Arab Emirates and Northwestern Oman.

genres.name: Sa'idi
genres.description: Traditional folkloric performance and form of Arabic Folk Music originating from Upper Egypt.

genres.name: Australian Folk Music
genres.description: Folk traditions of the European colonists and convicts in Australia.

genres.name: Brazilian Folk Music
genres.description: Comprises the various traditions of folk music found in Brazil, often resulting from the interplay of Indigenous, African and European music.

genres.name: Aboio
genres.description: Cattle-herding songs originating in rural Northeastern Brazil.
genres.album: Pranto e dor de um vaqueiro

genres.name: Aboio cantado
genres.description: Aboio that features rhyming verses.
genres.album: Os bridões de ouro: aboios e toadas

genres.name: Banda de pífano
genres.description: Lively music played by bands consisting of two fifes and percussion.
genres.track: A Briga Do Cachorro Com a Onça - BANDA DE PÍFAROS DE CARUARU

genres.name: Candomblé Music
genres.description: Music of the Afro-Brazilian Candomblé religion that influenced the secular Afoxé.

genres.name: Cantoria
genres.description: Sung poetry of itinerant cantadores from Northeastern Brazil.

genres.name: Repente
genres.description: Contest of fully improvised poetry sung in different stanza formats.
genres.track: O verdadeiro romance de João de Calais

genres.name: Capoeira Music
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian style that accompanies and sets the rhythm and energy of the capoeira martial art, originating in the 19th century with the relocation of African slaves to the states of Bahia and Rio de Janeiro.

genres.name: Jongo
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian cultural manifestation involving music and dance; composed of percussion instruments and chants.

genres.name: Ponto de umbanda
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian religious ritualistic praise sung by priests to evoke entities; typically accompanied by claps and traditional drums known as atabaque.
genres.artist: Heitor dos Prazeres e Sua Gente

genres.name: Lundu
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian music and dance that emerged in the 18th century with influences from African drumming with European fandango.

genres.name: Maracatu
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian genre which accompanies the cultural manifestation of the same name, hailing from the northeastern state of Pernambuco.

genres.name: Modinha
genres.description: Popular during the 18th and 19th centuries in Brazil; characterized by sentimental works with amorous themes, poetic lyrics, acoustic instrumentation and operatic vocals.

genres.name: Philly Drill
genres.description: Apocalyptic and haunting choirs, keys, and strings with gruesome narratives and slow, sparse drums.

genres.name: Digicore
genres.description: Developed in the late 2010s and characterized by frantic, bombastic, and glamourous production, usually derived from Trap, that serves to accompany highly melodious, auto-tuned, and hi-pitched vocal performances, often done with breathy voice singing and sing-rapping.

genres.name: Dirty South
genres.description: Originated in the Southern US during the mid-1990s, defined by a bouncy rhythm, fast-tempo snares, 808s, heavy bass, and often rapped in a rhythmic delivery consisting of explicit lyrics.

genres.name: Disco Rap
genres.description: Most prevalent from 1979 to 1982, featuring MCs rapping over popular Disco breaks.

genres.name: Drill
genres.description: Originated in Chicago in the early 2010s; broadly characterized by complex, energetic rhythms coupled with gang-oriented, street-conscious, and violent lyrics.

genres.name: Chicago Drill
genres.description: Bass-heavy, dense, and typically syncopated percussion, featuring ticking hi-hats and gunshot-like snare rolls, usually accompanied by menacing synth melodies and violent Gangsta Rap lyricism.

genres.name: Bop
genres.description: Grew out of the Chicago Drill scene in the early 2010s, characterized by autotuned vocals and upbeat synth melodies.

genres.name: Free Car Music
genres.description: Chaotic and metallic percussion with clanging rides, rapid hi hat rolls, and tense kick buildups typically coupled with staggered, punched-in rapping.

genres.name: Jersey Drill
genres.description: Mixes Drill and Jersey Club production, characterized by an energetic sound and distinct syncopated rhythms.

genres.name: New York Drill
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2010s, characterized by energetic, bouncy tresillo rhythms, creating a warmer, more booming tone than UK Drill, which prominently inspired it.

genres.name: Sample Drill
genres.description: Prominent, recognizable samples set to tresillo-styled Drill hi-hats and counter snares.

genres.name: Sexy Drill
genres.description: Emotive and sensual melodies, samples, and basslines set to driving stomps and bouncy Drill percussion typically joined by lyrical themes of sex, love, clubbing, and heartbreak.

genres.name: UK Drill
genres.description: Deep bass and complex rhythm which denotes a Grime influence in the production.

genres.name: Drumless
genres.description: Stripped-down production style pioneered in the early 2010s and identified by a lack of drums or minimal, subtle percussion left untouched from the original sample or filtered out.

genres.name: Emo Rap
genres.description: Moody, melancholic production combining atmospheric Cloud Rap, and Trap's typical drum programming, with sampling from Alternative Rock, Midwest Emo, Emo-Pop, and Pop Punk.

genres.name: Experimental Hip Hop
genres.description: Incorporates experimental and eccentric elements considered unconventional or unorthodox compared to more traditional hip hop.

genres.name: Industrial Hip Hop
genres.description: Incorporates harsh elements inspired by Industrial music such as blaring, noisy synths, distorted and metallic percussion, as well as more aggressive and off-kilter rapping styles.

genres.name: G-Funk
genres.description: Relaxed and organic sound featuring live instrumentation, use of P-Funk samples, and high-pitched synth lines.

genres.name: Genge
genres.description: Combines elements of Dancehall with various traditions of Kenya.

genres.name: Gengetone
genres.description: Takes strong influence from Reggaetón and modern Dancehall, featuring more explicit lyrics and harder beats.

genres.name: Hardcore Hip Hop
genres.description: Confrontation and aggression, whether in the lyricism, vocal delivery, hard beats, heavy production, or any combination thereof.

genres.name: Britcore
genres.description: British subgenre from the late 1980s and early 1990s featuring fast breakbeats and rapping.

genres.name: Chopper
genres.description: Originated in the Midwest Hip Hop scene in the 1990s; initially defined by slow jam beats rapped over with very fast flows and resonant choruses.

genres.name: Gangsta Rap
genres.description: Lyrics from a gangster's perspective.

genres.name: Coke Rap
genres.description: Lyrics with heavy reference to street-level drug dealing, specifically cocaine.

genres.name: Mafioso Rap
genres.description: Themed around organized crime, particularly the Mafia, often featuring cinematic production and lavish aesthetics.
genres.track: Ice Cream (feat. Ghostface Killah, Method Man & Cappadonna)

genres.name: Road Rap
genres.description: Emerged in the mid 2000s from Brixton and Peckham featuring abrasive tones, prominent Grime influence, and lyrics depicting circumstances of street gang violence in the UK.

genres.name: Scam Rap
genres.description: Lyrics that focus on various forms of fraudulent activities.

genres.name: Horrorcore
genres.description: Lyrical and aesthetic focus on the macabre and morbid, with production generally of a darker nature than is typically found in other Hip Hop.

genres.name: Memphis Rap
genres.description: Minimalistic half-time drum machine programming with droning bass, often paired with aggressive rapping and a double time flow.

genres.name: Dungeon Rap
genres.description: Combines the dark production of Memphis Rap with the fantasy aesthetics and sound design of Dungeon Synth.

genres.name: Phonk
genres.description: Modernized, eclectic take on classic Memphis Rap production, featuring various influences from other Hip Hop genres, especially drum programming inspired by other Southern Hip Hop as well as frequent jazzy, funky elements somewhat akin to West Coast Hip Hop and from Electronic music.

genres.name: Mid-School Hip Hop
genres.description: Based around heavy, stripped-down drum machine beats.

genres.name: Trap Metal
genres.description: Loud, distorted 808s and basslines, as well as aggressive vocals that are usually yelled or screamed.

genres.name: Hipco
genres.description: Developed in Liberia, often featuring conscious and political lyrics and influences from local dance styles.

genres.name: Hiplife
genres.description: Fusion of Ghanaian Highlife with Hip Hop.

genres.name: Houston Sound
genres.description: Features slow to medium tempos, heavy bass, prominent organs and horns, and live instruments such as keyboards, bass guitar and wah-wah pedal.

genres.name: Hyphy
genres.description: Party-focused style with upbeat tempos, heavy bass and prominent synths, all underpinned by a distinctive West Coast-style rhythm, claps on beats 2 and 4, and a strong kick drum on beats 1, 2, and either 3 or 4.

genres.name: Jerk Rap
genres.description: Sparse beats, simple melodies, and party-centric lyrics geared towards a style of dance called “jerkin’.”

genres.name: Instrumental Hip Hop
genres.description: Can take the form of instrumental versions of songs that normally feature rapping, or hip hop originally released and always intended to be instrumental.

genres.name: Rare Phonk
genres.description: Primarily features eclectic sampling and lush, jazzy beats, usually set to Trap rhythms with prominent influences of Memphis Rap.

genres.name: Jazz Rap
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Jazz through the use of samples or live instrumentation.

genres.name: Jerk
genres.description: Sparse, snare-heavy drum patterns loosely inspired by Jerk Rap, which take major elements from other prominent 2010s and 2020s underground hip hop genres like Plugg.

genres.name: Jersey Club Rap
genres.description: Incorporates Jersey Club's distinct kick-heavy rhythms, which are modified to better suit rapping, featuring less sampling and more atmospheric production than earlier Jersey club.

genres.name: Jigg
genres.description: Club-oriented genre characterized by heavy 808-driven beats, imposing synthesized brasses and an uptempo rhythm.

genres.name: Jook
genres.description: Eclectic mix of influences on booty bass music developed in Tampa and Miami in the mid-2000s revolving around uptempo rhythms, airy chords, and party-oriented lyrics.

genres.name: Latin Rap
genres.description: Primarily done in Spanish; incorporates Hispanic American Music elements into its sound.

genres.name: Chicano Rap
genres.description: Latin Rap with a Mexican twist.

genres.name: Lo-Fi Hip Hop
genres.description: Relaxed, laid-back form of Hip Hop, typically instrumental and influenced by Jazz Rap and Downtempo.

genres.name: Lowend
genres.description: Rhythms driven by steady eighth-note digital handclaps, rattling bass, fast tempos, upbeat sound, and laid-back flows.

genres.name: Mobb Music
genres.description: San Francisco Bay Area production style that samples slowed down Funk to create a slow, pounding, and menacing sound with live studio instrumentation and Roland TB-303 basslines.
genres.track: Treal Man (feat. E-40 & Da' Unda' Dogg)
genres.album: Mac Dre Presents the Rompalation 2006: Thugz of Honor

genres.name: Motswako
genres.description: Mainly rapped in a mixture of Setswana and English, incorporating additional languages and local South African and Botswanan influences, particularly Kwaito.

genres.name: Nerdcore Hip Hop
genres.description: Themes touch on such nerd mainstays as science, computers, and science fiction.

genres.name: Nervous Music
genres.description: Dark, sinister and menacing sound, heavy sub-basses, simple melodies and slow, sparse and slamming drums.

genres.name: Philly Club Rap
genres.description: Mixes the fast and energetic production of Philly Club with similarly frantic and fast rapping.

genres.name: Political Hip Hop
genres.description: Features explicitly political lyrics and themes.
genres.album: It Takes A Nation Of Millions To Hold Us Back

genres.name: Pop Rap
genres.description: Fuses Hip Hop's rapping and production traits with Pop elements such as melodious vocals and light, catchy tunes.

genres.name: Frat Rap
genres.description: Light-hearted and laid-back with lyrical focuses on subjects such as partying and college life.

genres.name: Futuristic Swag
genres.description: Playful tone with bright square wave melodies, singsong rapping, joyful intonations, and triumphant brass leads.

genres.name: Ratchet
genres.description: Club-oriented style defined by a repeated synth melody and a sparse drum pattern often accompanied by a "hey" chant.

genres.name: Sigilkore
genres.description: Dark and hyperactive production, featuring rapping laced with layers of effects.

genres.name: Snap
genres.description: Sparse production, pounding 808 bass, occasional use of third-beat finger snaps, and simple melodies reminiscent of ringtones.

genres.name: Stoner Rap
genres.description: Heavily features lyrics about cannabis and stoner culture, usually with a laid-back flow and relaxing production.
genres.album: Man On The Moon: The End Of Day

genres.name: Trap
genres.description: Originated in Atlanta in the early 2000s; distinctive fast hi-hat sound and heavy bass at moderate tempos.

genres.name: New Jazz
genres.description: Colorful, repetitive synths and synthetic instruments, playful vocal chops, and wonky bass selections set to bouncy Trap drums.

genres.name: No Melody
genres.description: Usage of minimalistic, repetitive midtempo drum patterns, and simple, prominent 808s.

genres.name: Plugg
genres.description: Use of sparse and compact drum and hi-hat patterns, subby 808s and heavy low end; commonly features piano samples, airy pads, and icy synths.

genres.name: Ambient Plugg
genres.description: Strong atmosphere and texture taken from Ambient music; featuring tight drums and minimal low-end and 808s.

genres.name: Dark Plugg
genres.description: Ominous, sinister synth pads and lead melodies, skittering hi-hats, and fast percussion and snare rolls.

genres.name: PluggnB
genres.description: Emphasizes more melodic and layered synth leads, denser and faster drum programming, and a lesser reliance on the laid-back, minimalistic atmosphere of earlier Plugg styles.

genres.name: Asian Rock
genres.description: Dense PluggnB percussion in combination with airy bells, synth plucks, and soaring synthetic guitar leads.

genres.name: Terror Plugg
genres.description: Harsher and noisier, with 808s distorted to create a high-frequency sound.
genres.track: How U Say Nikka Fukk Uno Bitxh Fukk U

genres.name: Rage
genres.description: Dense, buzzing synth work with repetitive chord progressions and melodic synth leads.

genres.name: Regalia
genres.description: Lush, sweeping string arrangements, dreamy piano passages, and other orchestral instrumentation set to cinematic Trap percussion.

genres.name: Trap Soul
genres.description: Mixes passionate vocals derived from Contemporary R&B with laid-back, nocturnal and atmospheric Trap production.

genres.name: Trap latino
genres.description: Distinguished by its Reggaetón and Latin Rap roots, with smooth and moody production inspired by Alternative R&B and Contemporary R&B.

genres.name: Tread
genres.description: Icy or futuristic synths with busy and high-tempo drum programming using distinctive 808 patterns.

genres.name: Trap shaabi
genres.description: Combining Trap percussion and rhythms with Egyptian Shaabi and especially Mahraganat.

genres.name: Turntablism
genres.description: Manipulating and re-appropriating vinyl records using a turntable and DJ mixer in a Hip Hop context, often featuring constant scratching and beat juggling between two or more recordings into original, distinctive tracks.

genres.name: Industrial & Noise
genres.description: Umbrella encompassing Noise and Industrial, as well as later derivatives that combine the latter aesthetics with other styles and in more accessible directions which fall under Post-Industrial.

genres.name: Post-Industrial
genres.description: Umbrella group of genres that combine the dark, mechanical aesthetic of early Industrial music with more accessible genres, such as Rock and Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Industrial Metal
genres.description: Incorporates the abrasive and heavy sound of Industrial into Metal, using elements like synthesizers and drum machines.

genres.name: Cyber Metal
genres.description: Originated around 1999, influenced by EBM and Aggrotech with more melodic and less repetitive riffs as well as harsh vocals.

genres.name: Neue Deutsche Härte
genres.description: Alternative Metal and Industrial Metal that incorporates various aspects of electronic music, specifically Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Industrial Rock
genres.description: Incorporates abrasive guitars and synthesizers inspired by Industrial and various Post-Industrial styles.

genres.name: Machine Rock
genres.description: Emphasises a mechanical sound that centres heavy, Punk Rock-inspired guitar riffs over Electro-Industrial beats, while incorporating cyberpunk themes and imagery.

genres.name: Martial Industrial
genres.description: Incorporates elements of traditional European military marches with Neoclassical Darkwave, Dark Ambient, Industrial, and Neofolk.

genres.name: Jazz
genres.description: Originating in African American communities in the Southern United States around the turn of the 20th century, building on New Orleans Brass Band ensemble and influences from Ragtime and Blues to become a very popular style by the emergence of Swing in the 1930s.
genres.album: The Black Saint And The Sinner Lady

genres.name: Afro-Jazz
genres.description: African-styled percussion and rhythms.

genres.name: Arabic Jazz
genres.description: Blending of Arabic Music and Jazz.
genres.album: Sun Ra Arkestra Meets Salah Ragab In Egypt

genres.name: Avant-Garde Jazz
genres.description: Combines traditional or mainstream Jazz stylings with non-traditional techniques of avant-garde art music by experimenting with characteristics such as rhythm, harmony, structure, melody, and instrumentation.
genres.track: A Love Supreme, Pt. I – Acknowledgement

genres.name: Experimental Big Band
genres.description: Dispensing with traditional Jazz structures and Swing sounds, instead performing Avant-Garde Jazz and pushing the boundaries of the medium.

genres.name: Free Jazz
genres.description: Attempts to break free from the conventions and patterns of earlier Jazz subgenres through the use of elements such as dissonance, atonality, and free-flowing rhythmic structures.

genres.name: European Free Jazz
genres.description: Arose in Europe in the late 1960s and early 1970s, moving even further from the Jazz tradition by often dropping the swinging rhythm, taking liberties with the use of atonality and noise.

genres.name: Bebop
genres.description: Fast tempos, improvisation, melodic chromaticism, and complex harmonies and chord progressions.
genres.artist: Dizzy Gillespie, Sonny Rollins, Sonny Stitt
genres.track: On The Sunny Side Of The Street

genres.name: Big Band
genres.description: Commonly associated with the golden era of Swing in the 1930s and 1940s, performed by a large ensemble including brass, woodwinds, and usually a rhythm section.
genres.track: The Shoes of the Fisherman's Wife Are Some Jive Ass Slippers

genres.name: Progressive Big Band
genres.description: Introduces Western Classical Music compositional techniques into Big Band.
genres.album: sonnys dream birth of the new cool

genres.name: British Dance Band
genres.description: Came from the dancehalls of the 1920s and 1930s, combining a British take on Jazz with the Music Hall tradition.

genres.name: Bulawayo Jazz
genres.description: Emerged from the city of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe in the early 1950s, led by the alto sax and accompanied by ensembles.

genres.name: Cape Jazz
genres.description: Developed parallel to American Jazz in the early 20th century, named for its origin in Cape Town, South Africa.
genres.track: Blue Notes For Mongezi: First Movement

genres.name: Cartoon Music
genres.description: Zany and uptempo; incorporates elements of Western Classical Music and Modern Classical into frantic Big Band arrangements, playfully chaotic to match the on-screen actions of Cartoon characters and the beat of their movements.
genres.album: Bug Music: Music of the Raymond Scott Quintette, John Kirby & His Orchestra, and the Duke Ellington Orchestra

genres.name: Chamber Jazz
genres.description: Made by mostly small acoustic-based ensembles with emphasized improvisation and influenced by Neoclassicism and Traditional Folk Music.

genres.name: Cool Jazz
genres.description: Developed in the late 1940s alongside and in response to Bebop, featuring a more restrained, emotionally "cool" style.
genres.track: Freddie Freeloader (feat. John Coltrane, Cannonball Adderley, Wynton Kelly & Paul Chambers)

genres.name: Crime Jazz
genres.description: Gritty, moody style that emerged in the mid-1950s to accompany film noir movies and hard-boiled detective/crime-themed TV shows.

genres.name: Dark Jazz
genres.description: Melancholic and gloomy Film noir-inspired atmosphere and influence from Crime Jazz and Dark Ambient.

genres.name: Dixieland
genres.description: Developed in New Orleans in the 1910s, incorporating influences from Ragtime and Blues into cacophonous, polyphonic arrangements with instruments trading places between accompaniment and soloist.
genres.album: Louis Armstrong Plays W. C. Handy

genres.name: ECM Style Jazz
genres.description: Primarily associated with ECM Records, combining elements of Jazz Fusion with the subdued atmosphere of Cool Jazz and the Western Classical Music bent of Third Stream.

genres.name: Ethio-Jazz
genres.description: Unique blend of traditional Ethiopic Music and Jazz.
genres.artist: ሙላቱ አስታጥቄ [Mulatu Astatke] feat. ከፋቃደ አሞደ መስቀል [Fekade Amde Maskal]

genres.name: Flamenco Jazz
genres.description: Combination of Jazz with Flamenco nuevo, the contemporary style of Flamenco, which was pioneered in the late 1960s.

genres.name: Hard Bop
genres.description: Continuation of Bebop that reintroduces more traditional African-American musical features, such as bluesy melodies, slow to medium tempos, and a more groove-oriented sound, while retaining the expressive improvisation.

genres.name: Indo Jazz
genres.description: Fuses the various musical traditions of the Indian subcontinent with jazzy musical structures.

genres.name: Jazz Fusion
genres.description: Near-universal usage of electric guitars and keyboards coupled with influences from genres such as Rock, Rhythm & Blues, Funk, and Traditional Folk Music, and a relative degree of harmonic simplicity.

genres.name: Jazz Poetry
genres.description: Emerged in the 1920s, incorporating the style and rhythms of Jazz as both art forms spread throughout African-American communities in the United States.

genres.name: Jazz manouche
genres.description: Combines Jazz with several aspects of Romani Folk Music.

genres.name: Jazz-Funk
genres.description: Jazz highly influenced by Funk.

genres.name: Kréyol djaz
genres.description: Combines Jazz with various styles of French Caribbean Music.

genres.name: Latin Jazz
genres.description: Fusion with Latin American rhythms, especially those of African origin.

genres.name: Afro-Cuban Jazz
genres.description: Combines Jazz with the rhythms of Afro-Cuban music.

genres.name: Samba-jazz
genres.description: Jazz genre from Brazil that incorporates Samba and/or Bossa nova elements.

genres.name: Marabi
genres.description: South African Jazz with origins in the 1920s and rooted in traditional South African music.

genres.name: Kwela
genres.description: Influenced by Zulu music, characterized by its happy melodies, played by pennywhistle flutes and accompanied by a banjo or a guitar.

genres.name: Mbaqanga
genres.description: Emerged from the traditional Marabi Jazz and Swing as well as Kwela popular South African genres.

genres.name: Modal Jazz
genres.description: Utilizes musical modes as harmonic framework over traditionally used chord progressions.

genres.name: Jazz Mugham
genres.description: Combines Jazz with elements of Azerbaijani Mugham, featuring jazz-inspired instrumental compositions, improvisations, wind and vocal elements, as well as modal scales and ornamentation techniques for emotional depth.

genres.name: Post-Bop
genres.description: Grew out of Hard Bop in the early to mid-1960s incorporating certain untraditional elements inspired largely in part from Avant-Garde Jazz, Modal Jazz and eventually, Free Jazz, such as non-diatonic chord progressions, irregular rhythms and amelodic forms.

genres.name: Smooth Jazz
genres.description: Simple melodies and slick production influenced by Pop and R&B.

genres.name: Soul Jazz
genres.description: Appeared during the 1950s when Gospel, Rhythm & Blues and later Soul started to influence the style of prolific Jazz musicians.

genres.name: Spiritual Jazz
genres.description: Emerged in the 1960s, marked by a mixture of Jazz with approximations of ethnic styles, religious music of non-Christian traditions, and the ecstatic, transcendental aspects of Free Jazz.
genres.track: The Creator Has A Master Plan

genres.name: Spy Music
genres.description: Meant to evoke the action and drama of Spy films.

genres.name: Stride
genres.description: Early form of Ragtime-derived Jazz with improvisational tendencies; named for the performers' left hand "striding" across the piano keyboard.
genres.album: The Art Tatum - Ben Webster Quartet

genres.name: Sweet Jazz
genres.description: Early form developed by white bandleaders and highly popular with white audiences in the 1920s, emphasizing arrangements and strong melodies with a straighter rhythmic feel, de-emphasizing improvisation compared to "hot" Dixieland.
genres.album: the beau hunks play the original little rascals music

genres.name: Swing
genres.description: Distinctive rhythm and large backing rhythm section over which solos are performed.
genres.album: And His Mother Called Him Bill

genres.name: Swing Revival
genres.description: Born out of 1990s alternative music; sometimes incorporating elements from newer genres such as Rockabilly, Ska, and Punk Rock.

genres.name: Third Stream
genres.description: A fusion of Jazz and Western Classical Music, with improvisation as a vital component.
genres.artist: Floating Points, Pharoah Sanders & The London Symphony Orchestra

genres.name: Vocal Jazz
genres.description: Focused on vocals, generally using a more traditional, poppy strong structure and reducing the role of improvisation.

genres.name: Vocalese
genres.description: Newly written lyrics set to the melody of an existing instrumental solo, often in a Bebop or Big Band style, and characterized by syllabic phrasing.
genres.album: The Hottest New Group In Jazz

genres.name: West Coast Jazz
genres.description: Laidback style of jazz related aesthetically to Cool Jazz, developed by musicians based in Los Angeles and San Francisco, California in the 1950s.

genres.name: Metal
genres.description: Driving and distorted riffs, aggressive drumming, vigorous vocals, and an all-around show of brute force in its early days, since branching into dozens of subgenres.

genres.name: Alternative Metal
genres.description: Mid-tempo style emphasizing melodicism and rhythmic heaviness; branches outside of the stylistic conventions of Metal.

genres.name: Funk Metal
genres.description: Melds Funk Rock grooves with slap basslines and metallic guitarwork.

genres.name: Nu Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes bouncy, drop-tuned riffs, alternating vocal styles, and genre-bending, often incorporating Hip Hop and Funk Metal elements.

genres.name: Rap Metal
genres.description: Features rapped vocals, typically formed around heavy, mid-tempo, and groove-oriented playing in addition to elements of Hip Hop beats such as record scratching.

genres.name: Avant-Garde Metal
genres.description: Often breaking the bounds of the genre through experimental structures and instrumentation, or by incorporating outside influences.

genres.name: Black Metal
genres.description: Highly distorted, treble-heavy guitars, tremolo-picked riffs, blast beats and double bass drumming, shrieked vocals, and raw, lo-fi production; often focuses on occult, dark imagery and atmosphere.
genres.album: A Blaze in the Northern Sky

genres.name: Atmospheric Black Metal
genres.description: Repetitive riffs and melodies, slower tempos, synthesized ambient textures, and guitar effects creating atmospheric soundscapes.

genres.name: Blackgaze
genres.description: Fuses tremolo-picked riffing, intense drumming and harsh vocal techniques with mellow, dreamy textures, major-key melodies and extended build-ups.

genres.name: Black 'n' Roll
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Hard Rock, Glam Rock, and Heavy Metal.

genres.name: DSBM
genres.description: Lethargic, melancholic, and repetitive sound; depressive and misanthropic themes; vocals ranging from high-pitched wails and screams to strained cleans; often featuring non-distorted sections.

genres.name: Dissonant Black Metal
genres.description: Dissonant atonal riffing, cleaner production style, and complex song structures.

genres.name: Hellenic Black Metal
genres.description: Black metal scene in Greece with more mid-tempo songwriting and pronounced Heavy Metal influence.

genres.name: Melodic Black Metal
genres.description: Stronger emphasis on melody, generally with cleaner production and more diverse arrangements.

genres.name: Pagan Black Metal
genres.description: Folk song-inspired melodies, traditional instruments, acoustic guitar passages, and often cleanly sung vocals, centered on romanticized pagan themes and imagery.
genres.track: Capitel I: I Troldskog faren vild

genres.name: Symphonic Black Metal
genres.description: Symphonic soundscapes, typically but not always synthesized.

genres.name: War Metal
genres.description: Aggressive, chaotic, and heavily Death Metal-influenced, featuring muddy, bass-heavy production and often incorporating war-themed lyrics.

genres.name: Death Metal
genres.description: Heavily distorted, down-tuned guitars, palm-muted, tremolo-picked riffs, double-kick and blast beat percussion, chromatic chord progressions, minor keys, abrupt changes in tempo, and guttural vocals.

genres.name: Brutal Death Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes abrasiveness, chunky rhythmic atonal riffs, and low guttural vocals.

genres.name: Slam Death Metal
genres.description: Focuses on slow or midtempo (as well as breakdown-style) sections built on chromatic, palm-muted riffs - so-called "slams".

genres.name: Death 'n' Roll
genres.description: Incorporates a groove-oriented, Hard Rock-influenced approach while retaining heavily distorted rhythm guitars and gruff or occasionally growled vocals.

genres.name: Deathgrind
genres.description: Combines the intensity and high-pitched screams of Grindcore with the technicality and low guttural vocals of Death Metal.

genres.name: Melodic Death Metal
genres.description: Utilizes the guitar harmonies and melodic focus of Heavy Metal while generally retaining down-tuned, heavily distorted guitars and a harsh, aggressive sound.

genres.name: Gothenburg Sound
genres.description: Pioneering Melodic Death Metal style and scene of Gothenburg, Sweden.

genres.name: Technical Death Metal
genres.description: Focuses on challenging, demanding songwriting and instrumental skill.

genres.name: Dissonant Death Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes discordant, dense songwriting and utilizes pinch harmonics, scratchy guitar leads, and atonality.

genres.name: Djent
genres.description: Groovy polymeters, syncopated power chord chugs, palm-muted, distorted guitars, and significant focus on production and tone.

genres.name: Thall
genres.description: Utilizes rapid release bends and a precise playstyle while contrasting pitch-shifted high and low notes, with ambient sections for atmosphere and buildup.

genres.name: Doom Metal
genres.description: Plodding tempos, repeated chords, and thick, distorted, down-tuned guitars in a style focused on foreboding, atmosphere, and tension.

genres.name: Death Doom Metal
genres.description: Fuses down-tuned guitars, growled vocals, and aggressive, often double-kick drumming with a mournful, somber atmosphere and plodding tempos.

genres.name: Funeral Doom Metal
genres.description: Features exceptionally slow, funeral dirge-like tempos; crushing, sluggish guitars; mournful, melancholic atmosphere; and distant, hushed growls and grunts.

genres.name: Traditional Doom Metal
genres.description: Monotonous and heavy playing style; repetitive, rough, and sometimes atonal guitar riffs; a "rocking to sleep" bass; and influences from both Blues Rock and Psychedelic Rock.

genres.name: Epic Doom Metal
genres.description: Emphasizes Heavy Metal influence and theatrical vocals.

genres.name: Drone Metal
genres.description: Extremely slow tempos, highly sustained, repetitive guitar notes, and minimalist song structures often omitting a traditional rhythm section and vocals.
genres.track: 泣きたがるスピード [the evilone which sobs]

genres.name: Folk Metal
genres.description: Features influences from various types of Traditional Folk Music expressed through melodies and/or traditional instrumentation, notably having a large scene in Europe.
genres.track: A Celebration For The Death Of Man…

genres.name: Celtic Metal
genres.description: Features Celtic Folk Music elements.
genres.album: Auskan Gabiltz Olatun Gainian (1598 Potrobizargorri I)

genres.name: Mittelalter-Metal
genres.description: Emerged as a metallic style in the mid-to-late 1990s from the German Neo-Medieval movement.

genres.name: Gothic Metal
genres.description: Usually low-to-mid-tempo songwriting featuring down-tuned, plodding riffing, a somber atmosphere shaped by ample usage of keyboards and synthesizers, and vocal styles ranging from harsh growls to baritone singing and female operatic vocals.

genres.name: Grindcore
genres.description: Brief and intense song structures featuring a plethora of blast beats, down-tuned and tremolo-picked guitars, and abrasive, usually raw production.

genres.name: Cybergrind
genres.description: Standard conventions of Grindcore taken to an even more discordant and rapid-fire extreme, with added Electronic dimensions of computer-generated noises and drum machines.

genres.name: Goregrind
genres.description: Death Metal-influenced riffs with rhythms ranging from very fast to slower mid-tempos correlated with pitch-shifted vocals, sloppy playing and production, and gore-themed aesthetics.

genres.name: Pornogrind
genres.description: Groovy, mid-tempo style known for its exaggerated bouncy rhythm and common pornographic themes.

genres.name: Mincecore
genres.description: Raw and simplistic with heavy reliance on Punk structures while including political and socially aware themes.

genres.name: Noisegrind
genres.description: Noise-driven, defined by its rawness, feedback usage, and very brief song structures.

genres.name: Groove Metal
genres.description: Midtempo riffs influenced by Thrash Metal but with a greater focus on rhythmic syncopation and heaviness over speed.

genres.name: Heavy Metal
genres.description: Heavier outgrowth of Hard Rock featuring greater distortion and intensity along with lesser Blues influences.

genres.name: Speed Metal
genres.description: Fast tempos, double-time feel, aggressive riffs, precise, often virtuosic soloing and expressive vocal styles.

genres.name: US Power Metal
genres.description: American style influenced by NWOBHM that features heavily distorted guitars paired with more aggressive riffs, mid-tempo Heavy Metal rhythms, and over-the-top theatrical vocals with fantasy or conceptual themes.

genres.name: Kawaii Metal
genres.description: Fuses various Metal substyles with J-Pop's upbeat melodicism and song structures, utilizing kawaii lyricism and an idol music aesthetic.
genres.album: かくれんぼか 鬼ごっこよ [Kakurenbo ka onigokko yo]

genres.name: Metalcore
genres.description: Drop-tuned guitar riffs, constant double kick drumming with varying tempos and techniques, breakdown sections, and screaming or shouting vocals.

genres.name: Deathcore
genres.description: Integrates brutal palm-muted and tremolo-picked riffing, blast beat-focused drumming, and guttural vocals of Death Metal with groovy breakdown sections.

genres.name: Downtempo Deathcore
genres.description: Slow and minimal songs emphasizing breakdowns, atmosphere, and dissonance with downtuned guitars.

genres.name: Mathcore
genres.description: Rhythmically complex, featuring unconventional time signatures, syncopated and dissonant riffs and erratic metric shifts.
genres.track: To Our Friends in the Great White North

genres.name: Melodic Metalcore
genres.description: Originated in the late 1990s when some metalcore bands infused elements of Melodic Death Metal into their sound to create a more metallic and melodic style.

genres.name: Neoclassical Metal
genres.description: Greatly influenced by Western Classical Music in its style of playing and composing.

genres.name: Post-Metal
genres.description: Atmospheric and dense metallic riffs, unconventional songwriting, sonic experimentation, and adoption of eclectic influences.

genres.name: Atmospheric Sludge Metal
genres.description: Combines slow, churning guitar riffs and thunderous percussion with dark, extensive otherworldly sonic landscapes.

genres.name: Doomgaze
genres.description: Gloomy and sombre atmosphere, amplified by the slow tempo and melancholy of Doom Metal, combined with the effects, washes of sound, and vocals found within Shoegaze.

genres.name: Power Metal
genres.description: Developed from Heavy Metal and Speed Metal, emphasizing speed, vocal melody and harmonized lead guitars.

genres.name: Progressive Metal
genres.description: Fuses amplified, guitar-driven sound with technical proficiency, virtuosity, complex compositions, innovative arrangements, eclecticism, and additional instrumentation.

genres.name: Sludge Metal
genres.description: Mixes Doom Metal's slow pacing, down-tuned riffing style and dark atmosphere with Hardcore Punk's aggression, abrasiveness and harsh vocals.

genres.name: Southern Metal
genres.description: Blues-influenced style that primarily incorporates Sludge Metal and Stoner Metal with metallic Southern Rock riffs.

genres.name: Stenchcore
genres.description: Heavier, more metallic form of Crust Punk drawing influence from Thrash Metal as well as Death Metal and Heavy Metal.

genres.name: Stoner Metal
genres.description: Combines elements of Doom Metal with elements of Psychedelic Rock and Blues Rock to create a melodic yet heavy sound.

genres.name: Symphonic Metal
genres.description: Incorporates elements of symphonic and Orchestral Music.

genres.name: Thrash Metal
genres.description: Blistering tempos, palm-muted, technical riffing influenced by Speed Metal, aggressive drumming utilizing double-kick and skank beats, and diverse vocal styles ranging from harsh to clean techniques.

genres.name: Crossover Thrash
genres.description: Mixes the metallic instrumentation of Thrash Metal with the ethos and approach of Hardcore Punk.

genres.name: Technical Thrash Metal
genres.description: Places great emphasis on complex songwriting and demanding instrumental parts.

genres.name: Trance Metal
genres.description: Tempo between 130 and 160 BPM, played with keyboards and metal instrumentation, sung with harsh and aggressive vocals including many clean melodic styles; regularly uses elements of Melodic Death Metal, Symphonic Metal, and Electronic Dance Music.

genres.name: Viking Metal
genres.description: Developed out of Black Metal and embodies an epic, Viking-like aesthetic.

genres.name: Musical Theatre and Entertainment
genres.description: Range of styles of theatre individually popular in the United States or in various countries in Europe, mostly from the 19th century to the mid-20th century.

genres.name: Cabaret
genres.description: Entertainment featuring Comedy, song, dance, and theatre.
genres.track: Der Kleine Leutnant Des Lieben Gottes (The Little Lieutenant of the Loving God)
genres.album: Lost in the Stars: The Music of Kurt Weill

genres.name: Dutch Cabaret
genres.description: Popular comedy form in the Netherlands which evolved out of traditional Cabaret in the 1890s.
genres.track: Madammen Met Een Bontjas - Live Uit Is Er Toevallig Een Urbanus In De Zaal?
genres.album: Is Er Toevallig Een Urbanus In De Zaal?

genres.name: Kabarett
genres.description: Theatrical entertainment consisting of mixed elements of music, sketches, monologues, dialogues, lyric poetry and/or ballads.

genres.name: Kanto
genres.description: Songs performed at the Tuluat Theaters of İstanbul in the late 19th century.

genres.name: Murga
genres.description: Popular carnival music traditional in some cities of Spain and Hispanic America.

genres.name: Murga uruguaya
genres.description: Variant originated in Montevideo that stands out for its rhythms, nasal vocals and choral arrangements.
genres.track: Que el letrista no se olvide

genres.name: Music Hall
genres.description: British theatrical entertainment popular in the 19th and 20th centuries, featuring light and comedic popular songs.

genres.name: Revue
genres.description: French Musical Theatre and Entertainment based on numbers and sketches inspired by the most relevant events of the year.
genres.album: The Real Ambassadors - An Original Musical Production by Dave and Iola Brubeck

genres.name: Rock Musical
genres.description: Style of musical theatre inspired by Rock.
genres.artist: Benny Andersson, Tim Rice & Björn Ulvaeus
genres.track: The Russian and Molokov / Where I Want to Be

genres.name: Show Tunes
genres.description: Originally composed to forward the story or enhance the characters or other plot elements of Broadway productions and other stage music.

genres.name: Siffleur
genres.description: Professional whistlers on the Vaudeville and Music Hall circuits.

genres.name: Vaudeville
genres.description: Performed in American musical theaters typically as part of a lowbrow, often comedic variety performance.

genres.name: New Age
genres.description: Broad genre centered on peaceful, meditative melodies, using a wide variety of instrumentation.

genres.name: Andean New Age
genres.description: Takes heavy influence from Indigenous Andean Music, emphasizing a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere and often using the flute.

genres.name: Celtic New Age
genres.description: Incorporates influences and performing styles from Celtic Folk Music, emphasizing pastoral imagery and wistful themes.

genres.name: Native American New Age
genres.description: Takes heavy influence from Indigenous North American Music, emphasizing a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere and utilizing chants, drumming, and flutes.

genres.name: Neoclassical New Age
genres.description: Strongly influenced by and sometimes also based upon early music and the Baroque Music or Classical Period.

genres.name: New Age Kirtan
genres.description: American development of Kirtan, fusing it with New Age and Western music.

genres.name: Tibetan New Age
genres.description: Incorporates perceived elements of Tibetan Music, particularly singing bowls.

genres.name: Pop
genres.description: Umbrella of popular styles closely tied to mass production and mass marketing, focusing on catchiness and accessibility through melody, rhythm, lyrics, and hooks.

genres.name: Adult Contemporary
genres.description: Slow to midtempo with a light and soothing tone, emerged as a successful radio format in the late 1970s and early 1980s.

genres.name: Afrobeats
genres.description: Originated in West Africa during the early 2010s and includes elements from Pop Rap, Contemporary R&B, and Dancehall.

genres.name: Alté
genres.description: More subdued, atmospheric, minimalist, and eclectic production and vocal styles compared to earlier styles, as well as more socially conscious lyrics.

genres.name: Alt-Pop
genres.description: Emerged in the late 2000s and early 2010s, combining chart Pop conventions with alternative/indie sensibilities and sometimes more minimal and contemplative atmosphere, often extracted from Alternative R&B.

genres.name: Arabic Pop
genres.description: Synthesis of Arabic Music with Western Pop melodies, almost always sung in Arabic and typically performed with Arabic instruments, alongside some Western instruments like the guitar.

genres.name: Al jeel
genres.description: Emerged in the 1970s as an alternative to Shaabi, taking influence from foreign Pop and incorporating rhythms of Reggae while retaining a distinctly Egyptian sound.

genres.name: Mūsīqā lubnāniyya
genres.description: Lebanese pop genre that emerged post-independence as a nationalist tradition distinct from Egyptian and Levantine music, blending local influences with western orchestration, peaking in Lebanon's 1957–1975 golden age through radio, cinema, and stage.

genres.name: Art Pop
genres.description: Inventive, idiosyncratic, or artistically ambitious, often experimenting with unconventional musical elements and conceptual approaches while retaining accessibility.

genres.name: Balkan Pop-Folk
genres.description: Balkan popular music which blends Pop, Folk, and ethnic music.

genres.name: Chalga
genres.description: Bulgarian blend of Contemporary Folk (Turkish, Bulgarian, Arabic & Romani) with Dance-Pop.

genres.name: Manele
genres.description: Mixture of Romanian Music with Turkish, Middle Eastern, Balkan, and Romani influences, usually electronic in production.

genres.name: Modern Laika
genres.description: Laiki music mixed with popular Western music, most notably pop and dance.

genres.name: Muzică de mahala
genres.description: Appeared in the 1980s, incorporating modern instruments and based on the model of Balkan Pop-Folk in neighboring countries.

genres.name: Skiladika
genres.description: Greek popular artists who used more Arabian elements; originally a derogatory term used to refer to a more decadent side of Laika.

genres.name: Tallava
genres.description: Mixture of Romani, Greek, Turkish, Albanian, and Slavic music, which incorporates Dance-Pop elements, and is very popular in Albania and Kosovo.

genres.name: Turbo-Folk
genres.description: Originated in Serbia during the 1980s, fusing traditional Western Balkan Folk Music with elements of contemporary popular music.

genres.name: Baroque Pop
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Western Classical Music, commonly featuring harpsichord or strings as well as the rhythmic flow and counterpoint of Baroque Music.

genres.name: Blue-Eyed Soul
genres.description: Usually refers to a Pop or Pop Rock song that contains strong Gospel-like elements, primarily popularized by white American and British singers in the 1960s through the 1980s.

genres.name: Boy Band
genres.description: Male vocal groups often put together by talent managers or record producers.

genres.name: Brega calypso
genres.description: Romantic vocals and lyrics, bubbly and sensual melodies and rhythms, horn sections and lush Caribbean-like guitar riffs over fast tempos.

genres.name: Brill Building
genres.description: Elaborate, polished, and typically melodramatic composition and arrangement associated with the songwriting teams at the Brill office building during the late 1950s and early 1960s.

genres.name: Bubblegum
genres.description: Upbeat, catchy, simple, and targeted at children and young teens; especially popular in the 1960s and 1970s.

genres.name: Cambodian Pop
genres.description: Popular music produced in Cambodia or by Khmer people.

genres.name: Rom kbach
genres.description: Cambodian pop with a slow melody that is similar to Luk thung.
genres.artist: ស៊ីនស៊ីសាមុត [Sinn Sisamouth] & រស់សេរីសុទ្ធា [Ros Sereysothea]
genres.track: យុវជនន័យស្នេហា
genres.album: កាសែតបទចម្រៀងថ្មីៗ [bat jomrieng thmey thmey]

genres.name: Canción melódica
genres.description: Sentimental vocal music sung in Spanish with a focus on the chorus, originally developed in the first half of the 20th century from a variety of traditional Hispanic genres.

genres.name: Bolero-Beat
genres.description: Latin American style stemming from both Canción melódica and the British Beat.

genres.name: Música cebolla
genres.description: Chilean offshoot of Canción melódica that expresses a much more melancholic or nostalgic side.

genres.name: City Pop
genres.description: Wave of Japanese Pop intended to reflect urban life during the period of the country's booming economy in the 1970s and 1980s, featuring a contemporary Western sound and lush arrangements.

genres.name: Neo-City Pop
genres.description: 2010s style blending emerging genres like Acid Jazz and Neo-Soul with the Western-inspired Japanese Pop styles of the 1970s and 1980s.

genres.name: Classical Crossover
genres.description: Takes specific Western Classical Music conventions and applies them into a straightfoward Pop context for mainstream appeal.

genres.name: Dangdut
genres.description: Indonesian popular music distinguished by a rhythmic blend of Indian, Arabic, Western, Malay, Sundanese, and Javanese influences within Indonesian Music, characterized by a unique rhythmic pattern from kendang.

genres.name: Dangdut koplo
genres.description: Development of Dangdut which originated in East Java in the 1990s, featuring a faster tempo and influences from international styles like Pop, Rock, and Reggae.

genres.name: Dansbandsmusik
genres.description: Nordic Pop style originating from 1960s Pop Rock, incorporating Swing, Schlager, Nordic Old Time Dance Music and Country influences.
genres.track: Det var dans bort I vägen

genres.name: Dansktop
genres.description: Danish equivalent to Dansbandsmusik with Schlager and Country influences and Contemporary Folk and Pop elements.

genres.name: Europop
genres.description: Emerged throughout mainland Europe in the early 1970s, referring to slick, highly commercial Pop songs that emphasize sugary melodies and light, bouncy instrumentation.
genres.track: Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! (A Man After Midnight)

genres.name: Flamenco Pop
genres.description: Incorporates Flamenco sub-styles into a more commercial Pop form; particularly through the vocal style and rhythms.

genres.name: French Pop
genres.description: Pop originating from France.

genres.name: Girl Group
genres.description: Combines elements of Rhythm & Blues, Rock & Roll, and Traditional Pop; typically performed by trios or quartets of female vocalists.
genres.album: Presenting the Fabulous Ronettes Featuring Veronica

genres.name: Hmong Pop
genres.description: Popular music of the Hmong ethnicity, with roots in the Hmong Folk Music and influenced by Western and East Asian forms of Pop music.

genres.name: Indian Pop
