genres.description: Commonly based out of India, Pakistan and Bangladesh and almost always sung in Hindi, Urdu or Bengali, implements South Asian Music in context of American and European Pop and Rock music.

genres.name: Bhojpuri Pop
genres.description: Modernized pop-folk variant of Bhojpuri Folk Music.
genres.track: Ham Dalab Ta Pura Hoi Kota

genres.name: Indie Pop
genres.description: Back-to-basics Rock approach combining a less mainstream and DIY ethos with melodic, lighthearted and straightforward songwriting.

genres.name: Bedroom Pop
genres.description: Named for solo producers and singer-songwriters from the 2010s onward who created intimate, "authentic" music in their own homes, outside of a traditional studio environment.

genres.name: C86
genres.description: Distinctly ramshackle, often Twee Pop-infused combination of British Indie Rock and Jangle Pop.

genres.name: Chamber Pop
genres.description: Based on the smooth and melodic songwriting of Lounge and other Easy Listening, as well as the orchestration of Baroque Pop and the production styles of other 1960s pop genres.

genres.name: Neo-Acoustic
genres.description: Cross-section of Indie Pop and Jangle Pop with more prominent acoustic instrumentation and songwriting/arrangements that draw from Sophisti-Pop.

genres.name: Tontipop
genres.description: Spanish scene known for its exuberant, child-like sound drawing directly from British Twee Pop, as well as Yé-yé, Bubblegum, and Synthpop.
genres.track: A mí ya me iba mal de antes

genres.name: Twee Pop
genres.description: Distinct Post-Punk background and often jangling guitars, defined by a cute aesthetic and lyrics combined with an indie/DIY attitude and a simplicity often indebted to Punk Rock.
genres.track: Get Me Away from Here, I'm Dying

genres.name: Cuddlecore
genres.description: Rawer and more Punk informed, downplaying jangly guitars in favor of heavier yet still light-hearted tones; often features influence from the contemporary Riot Grrrl movement.

genres.name: Irish Showband
genres.description: Phenomenon lasting from the mid-1950s until the early 1980s, often performed a mixture of currently popular music and skits.

genres.name: Italo Pop
genres.description: Romantic style developed in Italy in the late 1950s including various influences such as Chanson and Schlager.

genres.name: Canzone neomelodica
genres.description: Elements are derived from Canzone napoletana.

genres.name: J-Pop
genres.description: Commercial Pop of Japan after the advent of the Heisei era (1989), characterized by modernized production, a more eclectic sound palette, and a more westernized vocal style.
genres.track: エレクトロ・ワールド

genres.name: Akishibu-kei
genres.description: Otaku inclined update of the style pioneered by the Shibuya-kei scene, mixed with J-Pop and often tied to Anime and Video Game Music.

genres.name: Denpa
genres.description: Underground style aiming to be bizarre yet catchy, using off-key and high-pitched vocals, strange or nonsensical lyrics, repetitive chants, onomatopoeia, frantic and "off-kilter" production, and "moe" aesthetics.
genres.track: ガチャガチャきゅ～と・ふぃぎゅ@メイト(New Take)

genres.name: Yakousei
genres.description: Eclectic style of J-Pop developed in the late 2010s and influenced by the Vocaloid Scene; incorporates indie sensibilities, danceable rhythms and a focus on introspective lyricism.

genres.name: Jazz Pop
genres.description: Pop that incorporates elements from Jazz.

genres.name: K-Pop
genres.description: Contemporary style from South Korea, based on multiple mainstream influences such as Contemporary R&B, Dance-Pop, and Hip Hop.
genres.artist: 이달의 소녀 오드아이써클 [LOONA ODD EYE CIRCLE]

genres.name: Semi-Trot
genres.description: Contemporary form of Trot which takes influences from modern K-Pop and recent Pop substyles.

genres.name: Kayōkyoku
genres.description: Japanese popular music prominent during the later period of the Shōwa era (early 1950s to late 1980s).
genres.track: Kimi ni Mune Kyun (Uwaki na Bakansu)

genres.name: Idol kayō
genres.description: More Westernized and upbeat form of Kayōkyoku popular in the 1970s and 1980s which acted as a precursor to J-Pop.

genres.name: Mood kayō
genres.description: Early form of Kayōkyoku dominant in the 1950s and 1960s, prominently influenced by American Jazz, Hispanic American Music, and Hawaiian Music.
genres.album: 人の気も知らないで [Hito no ki mo shiranaide]

genres.name: Korean Ballad
genres.description: South Korean Pop from the 1980s to the early 90s taking influence from western Blues, Synthpop, Soul and Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Oriental Ballad
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1990s in South Korea, taking influence from more traditional forms of Korean Music.

genres.name: Latin Pop
genres.description: Incorporates elements and tropes from Hispanic and Latin American forms of music into a commercial Pop context.

genres.name: Cumbia pop
genres.description: Developed in the Río de la Plata region in the mid-2010s, featuring Latin Pop influences and lyrics related to romance, youth, and fun.

genres.name: Tropipop
genres.description: Subgenre of Colombian origin fusing Vallenato instrumentation into a Latin Pop context.

genres.name: Lokal musik
genres.description: Created by local, rural artists from Papua New Guinea that incorporate some elements of Papuan Folk Music into Pop.

genres.name: Mulatós
genres.description: Upbeat, danceable Hungarian Pop that takes strong influence from Hungarian Folk Music and Romani Folk Music.

genres.name: Nederpop
genres.description: Dutch language Pop which originally arose in the 1970s to describe the style of the 1950s and 1960s, but would also later be used for 1980s artists who incorporated elements of Ska and Reggae.

genres.name: Palingsound
genres.description: Originating from Volendam in the Netherlands; harmonizing vocals and orchestrated arrangements.

genres.name: New Music
genres.description: Developed when Japanese Singer-Songwriters incorporated elements of Contemporary Folk and Pop Rock with Kayōkyoku songwriting.

genres.name: OPM
genres.description: Filipino ballads prominent in the 1970s to early 1980s, combining the sentimentality, lush arrangements and vocal techniques of Kundiman with the instrumentations and rhythms of Manila Sound and Soft Rock.
genres.album: The First Metro Manila Popular Music Festival

genres.name: Orthodox Pop
genres.description: Combines Orthodox Jewish themes and prayer with Pop songwriting, usually sung in Hebrew.

genres.name: P-Pop
genres.description: Commercialized style from the Philippines, which served as the successor of Manila Sound and OPM, featuring various contemporary Western influences and primarily sung in Tagalog and English.

genres.name: Persian Pop
genres.description: Hybrid of Iranian and Persian-language popular music with Western instruments such as the guitar, drum kit, and synthesizer.

genres.name: Pop Batak
genres.description: Combines Western genres of music and instrumentation with a typical Batak flair, like lyrics about Batak life and the use of some traditional Batak instruments.
genres.album: Tradisional Batak - Gondang Uning Uningan Modern, Vol. 1

genres.name: Pop Ghazal
genres.description: Employs traditional Ghazal's verse, meter, and poetic inclinations in a pop form.

genres.name: Pop Minang
genres.description: Combines Minangkabau traditions with Pop structures and instrumentation.

genres.name: Talempong goyang
genres.description: Blends traditional Talempong elements with contemporary Pop influences, often featuring a female vocalist, and encourages audience participation.

genres.name: Pop Raï
genres.description: Fuses melodic sensibilities into the traditional Raï structure, with increased utilization of synthesizers, guitars, and drum machines.

genres.name: Pop Reggae
genres.description: Light, commercial form of Reggae designed to crossover and break through to a more mainstream Pop audience.

genres.name: Pop Rock
genres.description: Fuses conventional verse-chorus song structure and especially melodic songwriting with usage of guitars, drums, and propulsive rhythms.
genres.album: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars

genres.name: Beat
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1960s in the United Kingdom, drawing on Rock & Roll and the late 1950s Skiffle revival in a simple guitar-band format with strong melodies.
genres.track: You Must Have Crossed My Mind

genres.name: Freakbeat
genres.description: Outgrowth of the Mod movement which combines elements of British Rhythm & Blues and Beat with studio effects common in Psychedelia such as fuzztones, flanging and chorus; often seen as a British relative of the American Garage Psych scene.

genres.name: Group Sounds
genres.description: Japanese bands in the mid-to-late 1960s who began performing a style of Beat primarily in English.
genres.artist: 寺内タケシとバニーズ [Takeshi Terauchi and The Bunnys]

genres.name: Jovem Guarda
genres.description: 1960s Brazilian youth-oriented Pop Rock, with romantic lyrics and influenced by Merseybeat and Rockabilly.
genres.track: As Canções Que Você Fez Pra Mim

genres.name: Merseybeat
genres.description: Light, highly melodic style of Beat popular in the UK during the early 1960s, named due to the abundance of bands from Liverpool beside the River Mersey.

genres.name: Nederbeat
genres.description: Dutch answer to the British Beat boom of the 1960s.

genres.name: Beat Rock
genres.description: Japan-exclusive subgenre which combines Pop melodicism with a punchy, driving sound drawing on Punk Rock and New Wave.

genres.name: Big Music
genres.description: Rooted in Post-Punk and popular in the 1980s, with anthemic songwriting and a grandiose, stadium-ready sound.

genres.name: Britpop
genres.description: Emerged in the United Kingdom in the early 1990s, with a style hearkening back to the traditional guitar-driven songs and melodic hooks found in the British Pop Rock of the 1960s.

genres.name: Jangle Pop
genres.description: Treble-heavy guitars with arpeggiated melodies, distinct basslines, and often propulsive, repetitive strum-rhythms; frequently influenced by Post-Punk.
genres.track: There Is a Light That Never Goes Out

genres.name: Dolewave
genres.description: Loose, low-key, and sardonic with erudite lyrics and considerable influence from the Dunedin Sound and Slacker Rock; came to prominence in Melbourne in the early 2010s.
genres.album: Sometimes I Sit And Think, And Sometimes I Just Sit

genres.name: Paisley Underground
genres.description: Emerged in Los Angeles in the early 1980s, featuring the energy of Power Pop and New Wave adorned with retro Psychedelia.

genres.name: Neon Pop Punk
genres.description: Emerged from Scene culture; combines the upbeat tempos and catchy melodies of Pop Punk and Power Pop with synthesizers, auto-tuned vocals, or Dance beats, emphasizing a distinctly polished, hook-oriented sound.

genres.name: Piano Rock
genres.description: Primarily based around piano riffs and melodies, rather than having guitar as the focal instrument.

genres.name: Pop Yeh-Yeh
genres.description: Blends Western Beat and Psychedelia styles with asli singing and melodies drawn from Malay Folk Music.

genres.name: Post-Britpop
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1990s as a Britpop expansion mainly characterized by acoustic-leaning instrumentation, lush string arrangements, and mid-tempo song structures, as well as less apparent lyrical concerns for Britain in favor of introspective, contemplative themes.

genres.name: Power Pop
genres.description: Combines 1960s Pop melodies with loud power chords; characterized by prominent, sometimes jangly electric guitars, clear vocals, crisp harmonies, and economical arrangements.

genres.name: Soft Rock
genres.description: Clean production and light instrumentation paired with harmonious, radio-friendly songwriting; gained huge commercial success in the 1970s.

genres.name: Tropical Rock
genres.description: Combines influences from Country Rock and Caribbean Music to create an acoustic and breezy "island" themed sound.

genres.name: Yacht Rock
genres.description: Slick Pop Rock influenced by smoother R&B styles, popular in the late 1970s and often associated with California.

genres.name: Stereo
genres.description: Burmese Pop Rock genre which emerged in the mid-1960s.
genres.artist: စိုင်းဆိုင်မောဝ် [Sai Sai Mou]
genres.track: ယိုၼ်ႈမွဝ်ႇႁဝ်ဝိႈၷလႈ
genres.album: အမှတ်တရ သျှမ်းတေးစုများ အမှတ် 2 [Amanat taya Shan taysu mya amanat 2]

genres.name: Vocal Surf
genres.description: Appropriates the sounds of instrumental Surf Rock, combining surfing- and car-themed lyrics with a style that draws primarily from Doo-Wop and Rock & Roll.

genres.name: Pop Soul
genres.description: Fusion of Pop and Soul; originated in the 1960s as an attempt to give soul crossover success.

genres.name: Motown Sound
genres.description: Succinct, catchy song structures; complex arrangements; Gospel-influenced vocals; highly melodic and rhythmic bass lines; 4-4 drum patterns; often syncopated piano parts; regular use of horn and string sections; and historically a distinctive reverb and treble-heavy production.

genres.name: Pop Sunda
genres.description: Mixes Sundanese traditions with Pop structures and instrumentation.

genres.name: Progressive Pop
genres.description: Milder counterpart to Progressive Rock, emerging in the late 1960s and introducing complex songwriting and arrangements into a Pop context.
genres.track: Running Up That Hill (A Deal With God)

genres.name: Psychedelic Pop
genres.description: Combines unconventional instrumentation with studio effects to create a psychedelic atmosphere within melodic Pop music.
genres.track: Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds
genres.album: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

genres.name: Rabiz
genres.description: Elements of Armenian folk in its instrumentation, oftentimes incorporating influences from Arabic and other West Asian forms on a background of synthesizer arrangements.

genres.name: Rumba catalana
genres.description: Cheerful Catalan genre that takes influences from Rumba cubana, Andalusian Rumba flamenca, and Pop.

genres.name: Russian Chanson
genres.description: Divided into lyrical and criminal chanson, it is best described as narrative-driven popular music inspired by crime and prison.

genres.name: Schlager
genres.description: Light, sentimental, melodic pop music common mainly in northern and central Europe.

genres.name: Humppa
genres.description: Finnish music related to Jazz and the Foxtrot.

genres.name: Levenslied
genres.description: Dutch genre that enjoyed widespread popularity in the pre-Rock & Roll era. with simple melody and rhythm and lyrics composed of couplets and refrains.

genres.name: Volkstümliche Musik
genres.description: Light Pop with borrowings from German Folk Music (volksmusik), often misleadingly labeled as being volksmusik.

genres.name: Sertanejo romântico
genres.description: Electric instrumentation and romantic lyrics, made popular nationwide during the mid-to-late 1980s.

genres.name: Sertanejo universitário
genres.description: Modernized style combining rural themes and acoustic instrumentation with commercial production and Electronic instrumentation.

genres.name: Agronejo
genres.description: Early 2020s movement characterized by lyrical content with heavy agribusiness imagery, often featuring several Dance genres' sonic elements.

genres.name: Arrocha sertanejo
genres.description: Merged the Arrocha style with the younger audience creating a more energetic and more danceable rhythm.

genres.name: Funknejo
genres.description: Incorporates the rhythms, production, and idioms of Funk brasileiro into the universitário genre.
genres.track: Eu Quero Tchu Eu Quero Tcha
genres.album: Eu Quero Tchu Eu Quero Tcha

genres.name: Sophisti-Pop
genres.description: Incorporates influences from Jazz, classic R&B and Soul along with a slick, polished production style while retaining elements from its New Wave roots.

genres.name: Soviet Estrada
genres.description: Emerged in the USSR during the early 1930s, and encompassed the dominating popular music style composed by government-approved songwriters and the primary repertoire of professionally trained performers.

genres.name: Sunshine Pop
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1960s, characterized by a cheerful or wistful sound, light, lush production, and prominent vocal harmonies.

genres.name: Tarz
genres.description: Popular music from Afghanistan that combines various ethnic and regional traditions with influences from Indian, Persian, and Western popular music.

genres.name: Teen Pop
genres.description: Oriented to teen audiences and almost always sung by teens.

genres.name: Toytown Pop
genres.description: Niche offshoot of British Psychedelic Pop most popular in the late 1960s and early 70s; typically featuring strong influence from Music Hall and Novelty, as well as the culture of Victorian and Edwardian Britain, and characterised by a whimsical, childlike atmosphere.

genres.name: Traditional Pop
genres.description: Predominant form of Western commercial popular music in the pre-Rock & Roll era, particularly in the USA and starting with Tin Pan Alley; typically vocal-oriented with an orchestral arrangement.
genres.track: I Fall In Love Too Easily

genres.name: Romanţe
genres.description: Expressive and poetic Romanian style, generally sung similar to a Chanson and composed for piano and guitar orchestral arrangements.

genres.name: Standards
genres.description: Traditional compositions originating from the 1910s and onward which have become widely known, performed, and recorded across the world.
genres.album: Ella Fitzgerald Sings The Cole Porter Song Book

genres.name: Tin Pan Alley
genres.description: Early era of popular song in the USA, broadly from the 1890s-1930s; influences include Ragtime, Vaudeville, and Parlour Music.

genres.name: Turkish Pop
genres.description: Started in the late 1950s, when Turkish artists started to write their own lyrics to Western popular tunes.

genres.name: Yé-yé
genres.description: Upbeat, trendy Pop that emerged in Southern Europe in the early 1960s, focusing on image and risqué lyrics.
genres.album: Tous les garçons et les filles

genres.name: Psychedelia
genres.description: Umbrella of styles intended to replicate or enhance the altered state of consciousness brought on by the use of psychedelic drugs, originating in the 1960s.

genres.name: Neo-Psychedelia
genres.description: Developments in Psychedelia since the early 1980s, building on the drug-inspired styles developed in the 1960s.

genres.name: Baggy
genres.description: Blends Dance and Funk-based grooves with a laid-back, psychedelic atmosphere; features jangly guitars, looping basslines, four-bar drum patterns, and a hypnotic, carefree feel rooted in the Madchester scene of the late 1980s.

genres.name: Dream Pop
genres.description: Reverberated guitars, effects-laden vocals, and dense productions, creating a psychedelic, spacious, and dreamlike sound.

genres.name: Hypnagogic Pop
genres.description: 21st century style that refracts the pop culture of past decades through surreal, low-fidelity production and emulation of outdated media formats or equipment.
genres.album: volcanic bird enemy and the voiced concern

genres.name: Space Rock Revival
genres.description: Draws from the aesthetics and atmospheric soundscapes of Space Rock combined with the more minimal, back-to-basics approach of the Post-Punk era.

genres.name: Psychedelic Rock
genres.description: Often attempts to emulate or enhance the effects of psychedelic drugs, typically through a variety of instrumental and studio effects or eclectic influences.

genres.name: Acid Rock
genres.description: Loosely defined term often synonymous with Psychedelic Rock; sometimes also used for certain less commercial, more improvisational, or heavier styles.

genres.name: Garage Psych
genres.description: Emerged from mid-1960s US Garage Rock; characterised by fuzz guitars, cheap organs, experimentation with psychedelic effects and surreal lyricism, and a retained emphasis on raw energy and the pop song format.
genres.artist: King Gizzard and The Lizard Wizard

genres.name: Heavy Psych
genres.description: Influenced by Blues Rock's heavy dependence on riffs and improvisatory leanings; features thick, fuzzy guitars, usually slow-to-mid tempos, and extended soloing sections.
genres.album: It'll All Work Out In Boomland

genres.name: Raga Rock
genres.description: Influenced by South Asian Music, featuring a droning compositional quality and commonly incorporating instruments like sitar, tambura, and tablas.

genres.name: Space Rock
genres.description: Heavy use of synthesizers and guitar effects to create dense atmospheric soundscapes intended to evoke images of outer space and science fiction scenarios.

genres.name: Xian Psych
genres.description: Portrays Christian and biblical themes through a surreal, transcendent atmosphere, occasionally drawing influence from Christian Liturgical Music.

genres.name: Zamrock
genres.description: Developed in the Copperbelt region of Zambia in the 1970s, characterized by its blend of local sounds with influence from Funk, Hard Rock, and Blues Rock.

genres.name: Psychedelic Soul
genres.description: Soul which incorporates the effects and instrumentation of Psychedelic Rock.

genres.name: Psychsploitation
genres.description: Short-lived genre seeking to capitalise on the popularity of Psychedelia in the 1960s, featuring quickly and cheaply recorded material played by session musicians and put out by budget labels.

genres.name: Stoner Rock
genres.description: Psychedelic timbres, raw production, and stylistic influence from Doom Metal and Heavy Psych.

genres.name: Tropicália
genres.description: Blends Brazilian popular styles with the influence of Anglo-American Psychedelia; emerged as part of Brazil's late-1960s counterculture.
genres.track: Que Pena (Ele Já Não Gosta Mais De Mim)

genres.name: Punk
genres.description: Musical and cultural product of Punk Rock known for its simplistic, brash playstyle and anti-establishment themes.

genres.name: Art Punk
genres.description: Combines the stripped-down aggression of rudimentary Punk Rock with frequent experimentation ranging from instrumental interplay, noise, dissonance, and/or influences from other genres such as Jazz or Funk.

genres.name: Egg Punk
genres.description: Originated in the early 2010s; features lo-fi production, eccentric lyrics, quick tempos, nasally vocals, and cheap keyboard sounds.

genres.name: Cowpunk
genres.description: Mixes together Country Rock, Rockabilly, and Contemporary Folk with the familiar punk sound.

genres.name: Emo
genres.description: Focuses on emotional lyrics, expressive vocals, melodic songwriting, and dynamic song structures.

genres.name: Emo-Pop
genres.description: Mainstream derivative of Emo, puts more emphasis on the poppy sensibilities of Alternative Rock and Pop Punk.

genres.name: Emocore
genres.description: Emerged primarily in Washington D.C. in 1985 as a reaction to the stagnant Hardcore Punk scene, with a less aggressive style that was more melodic and often featured emotional, introspective lyrics.
genres.track: I'm Back Sleeping Or Fucking Or Something

genres.name: Mall Screamo
genres.description: Heavy instrumentation, melodic verse-chorus songwriting, and expressive singing contrasted with screaming vocals.
genres.track: Sir, This Is A Cutthroat Fashion

genres.name: Midwest Emo
genres.description: Characterized by shifts between loud and soft dynamics, off-key, strained and emotional vocals, sometimes with intricate instrumental arrangements and layered arpeggiated guitar parts.
genres.album: Just Got Back from the Discomfort We're Alright

genres.name: Screamo
genres.description: Intense, aggressive and complex approach to Emo featuring higher levels of abrasiveness and dissonance, accompanied by guitar-focused melodicism and harsh vocals.

genres.name: Emoviolence
genres.description: Shorter length and volatile song structures, while borrowing techniques from Powerviolence such as blast beats, unconventional screaming and noisier sounds.

genres.name: Folk Punk
genres.description: Influenced by various forms of Folk, including Traditional Folk Music as well as Contemporary Folk and Folk Rock.
genres.track: Fairytale of New York (feat. Kirsty MacColl)
genres.album: If I Should Fall from Grace with God

genres.name: Celtic Punk
genres.description: Infuses the sounds of Celtic Folk Music into Punk Rock.

genres.name: Gypsy Punk
genres.description: Strong Eastern European influences, especially various kinds of Romani Folk Music and Balkan Folk Music as well as Klezmer.

genres.name: Hardcore [Punk]
genres.description: Encompasses the first wave of Hardcore Punk beginning in the 1970s, as well as its derivative styles that incorporate diverse musical influences and stray away from the core Punk Rock sound.

genres.name: Beatdown Hardcore
genres.description: Heavy, urban-inspired and breakdown-oriented with strong relations to Metalcore.

genres.name: Electronicore
genres.description: Hybrid of Metalcore and/or Post-Hardcore with various Electronic Dance Music styles, utilizing Electronic instrumentation and occasional Dance beats.
genres.album: コインロッカーベイビー [Coin Locker Baby]

genres.name: Hardcore Punk
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1970s, often featuring extensive use of yelling or screaming, a stripped-down production style, and very short songs.

genres.name: Burning Spirits
genres.description: Emphasis on delivering a very energetic and triumphant sound with flashy and soaring Metal solos, "melodramatic" or "uplifting" chord progressions, and singalong, over the top, harsh vocals.

genres.name: Crust Punk
genres.description: Metallic outgrowth of Anarcho-Punk featuring a down-tuned, high-gain guitar sound, frequent D-Beat drum patterns, guttural vocals, and politically-charged lyrics often featuring apocalyptic imagery.

genres.name: Blackened Crust
genres.description: Borrows heavily from Black Metal production, blast beats, tremolo guitar, and vocals, while retaining the core Crust Punk sound, lyrical themes, and aesthetic.

genres.name: Neocrust
genres.description: Melodic, dark, and atmospheric style that often incorporates influences from Sludge Metal, Post-Metal, Black Metal, and Screamo.

genres.name: D-Beat
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1980s, features Metal influences, shouted vocals, and a distinct drum style known as the D-beat.
genres.track: Hear Nothing See Nothing Say Nothing
genres.album: Hear Nothing See Nothing Say Nothing

genres.name: Melodic Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the USA in the early to mid-1980s, placing emphasis on melodic vocals and technical guitar riffs rather than raw aggression.

genres.name: Skacore
genres.description: Fuses skank rhythms and frantic blasts of horns with hardcore intensity.

genres.name: Crack Rock Steady
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Crust Punk and sometimes Metal, coupled with anti-establishment lyrics.

genres.name: Street Punk
genres.description: Driven by Oi! style group vocals, catchy melodies, and aggressive songwriting akin to Punk Rock of the 1970s fused with Hardcore Punk of the 1980s.

genres.name: Thrashcore
genres.description: Fast tempos, brief song structures, and the occasional use of blast beats.

genres.name: Powerviolence
genres.description: Originated from the West Coast California Hardcore Punk scene in the late 1980s, utilizing strong elements of Noise Rock and abrupt tempo changes.

genres.name: Nintendocore
genres.description: Fuses Post-Hardcore and Metalcore influences with Chiptune instrumentation.

genres.name: Noisecore
genres.description: Short blasts of riff-less, Noise-driven music accompanied with chaotic drums and screamed vocals.

genres.name: Post-Hardcore
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s from Hardcore Punk that expanded on its aggression and dynamics through longer and more complex arrangements.

genres.name: Swancore
genres.description: High-register clean vocals and technical instrumentation drawn from Math Rock and Progressive Rock.

genres.name: Sass
genres.description: Emerged from Post-Hardcore in the early 2000s; characterized by sassy vocal styles and chaotic, erratic instrumentals.
genres.track: Give Me the Amulet, You Bitch

genres.name: Mod Revival
genres.description: Late 1970s and early 1980s revival of Mod fashion and music, featuring influence from the nascent Punk Rock scene.

genres.name: Pigfuck
genres.description: Sloppy, abrasive and feedback-laden riffing with vulgar and edgy lyricism, informed by Post-Hardcore's aggression and Post-Punk's rhythm section.

genres.name: Post-Punk
genres.description: Emerged alongside the initial Punk Rock explosion in the mid-to-late 1970s, putting a greater emphasis on experimentation and atmosphere.

genres.name: Coldwave
genres.description: Originated in Europe in the late 1970s and early 1980s and is known for its generally dark, gloomy atmosphere and heavy reliance on synthesizers.

genres.name: Dance-Punk
genres.description: Mixes the energy of Punk Rock with the danceable rhythms of Funk and Disco.

genres.name: Dance-Punk Revival
genres.description: Punchy and danceable variant of Post-Punk Revival that features Electronic instrumentation and influence from Alternative Dance.

genres.name: Gothic Rock
genres.description: Combines drama and a dark atmosphere with effects-laden guitars, prominent basslines, propulsive drums, and occasional keyboards and drum machines.

genres.name: Deathrock
genres.description: More Punk-oriented offshoot of Gothic Rock that emphasizes energy and an effect-laden sound over pure atmosphere.

genres.name: Positive Punk
genres.description: Early goth scene in London that grew out of the Anarcho-Punk movement and promoted themes of virtue and mysticism; commonly features wailing vocals, screeching guitars, prominent basslines, and eclectic drum patterns.

genres.name: Post-Punk Revival
genres.description: Incorporating the sounds and aesthetics of Post-Punk into Indie Rock, with jagged guitarwork, a dominant and danceable rhythm section, clean production, and poppy song structures.

genres.name: Proto-Punk
genres.description: Used to describe what influenced or in some way resembled Punk Rock before that genre's commercial breakthrough in 1976.

genres.name: Punk Blues
genres.description: Fusion of the instrumentation and scales of Blues Rock with Punk.

genres.name: Punk Poetry
genres.description: Fast and rhythmic vocal delivery of political or satirical themes; frequently backed by Post-Punk or Minimal Wave instrumentation.

genres.name: Punk Rock
genres.description: Fast tempos, loud and distorted riffs, simple songs, frequent use of power chords, and shouted vocals, originating in the mid-1970s in response to commercial, sentimental, and complex Rock.

genres.name: Anarcho-Punk
genres.description: Intentionally rougher and sloppier sound, with lyrics pertaining to anarchist ideology and sociopolitical injustices.

genres.name: Deutschpunk
genres.description: Partly a reaction to the commercialization of the German movement Neue Deutsche Welle; characterized by extreme speed, consciously basic songwriting, crude musicianship, and radical leftism.
genres.album: Welch ein Land! Was für Männer:

genres.name: Garage Punk
genres.description: Combination of the raw fuzztones of the original Garage Rock bands of the 1960s with the tempo and attitude of Punk Rock.

genres.name: Glam Punk
genres.description: Contrasts a snotty, nihilistic, and combative attitude of punk with theatrics and flamboyance.

genres.name: Horror Punk
genres.description: Thematically and lyrically derived from Horror movies, typically with a nostalgic and campy attitude.

genres.name: Könsrock
genres.description: Inspired by Post-Punk but with a more bizarre atmosphere with unusual or comic vocal techniques and a lyrical focus on the offensive and scatological.

genres.name: Oi!
genres.description: Rejection of perceived intellectualism and elitism in Post-Punk and Art Punk, characterized by a return to a straightforward, melodic Punk Rock sound, sing-along choruses, and a lyrical focus on working class youth culture.

genres.name: Pop Punk
genres.description: Blends the loud, fast-paced sound of Punk Rock with the melodic hooks of Pop.

genres.name: Easycore
genres.description: Combines the radio-friendly stylings of second-wave Pop Punk with Metalcore-inspired breakdowns, lower guitar tunings, and occasional unclean vocals.
genres.track: Heroes Get Remembered, Legends Never Die

genres.name: Seishun Punk
genres.description: Short-lived Japanese style popular in the early 2000s, characterized by a raw and abrasive style, Folk-inspired songwriting, and youth-oriented straightforward lyrics.
genres.album: 君と僕の第三次世界大戦的恋愛革命 [You & I's WW III Love Revolution]

genres.name: Psychobilly
genres.description: Cross-pollination of Punk Rock and Rockabilly.

genres.name: Ska Punk
genres.description: Utilizes skank rhythms, walking basslines, and often horn instrumentation in combination with a fast-paced Punk Rock playstyle.

genres.name: Skate Punk
genres.description: Combines the speed of Melodic Hardcore with the catchiness of Pop Punk, finding a middle ground between the two.

genres.name: Surf Punk
genres.description: Punk Rock that incorporates elements of Surf Rock.

genres.name: Vikingarock
genres.description: Incorporates influences from Nordic Folk Music and the imagery of Viking romanticism and Norse mythology.

genres.name: R&B
genres.description: Umbrella of styles covering the most popular forms of Black American music from the late 1940s, when the term Rhythm & Blues first appeared; includes the developments of Soul and Funk in the '60s and '70s, and the Contemporary R&B of the 1980s onward.
genres.album: Songs In The Key Of Life

genres.name: Acid Jazz
genres.description: Eclectic scene consisting of influences from Jazz, Funk, Hip Hop, Soul, and various styles of Dance that gained popularity during the 1990s.
genres.album: As segundas intenções do manual prático...

genres.name: Beach Music
genres.description: Danceable 4/4 "blues shuffle" rhythmic structure, vocal harmonies, and moderate tempos.

genres.name: Contemporary R&B
genres.description: Soulful, passionate and melismatic vocals originally derived from popular Soul and Disco, as well as smooth, lush and often synthesized production variously influenced by Hip Hop, Funk, and related strands of Pop.

genres.name: Alternative R&B
genres.description: Deviating from the traditional styles of Contemporary R&B and featuring smooth, reverberated, Electronic-influenced production with heavy bass and often reverberated vocals.

genres.name: Hip Hop Soul
genres.description: Hip Hop-oriented style that evolved out of New Jack Swing in the early 1990s.

genres.name: New Jack Swing
genres.description: Mixes light Hip Hop & Funk production techniques with Contemporary R&B vocals and melodies as well as swinging and danceable drum grooves.

genres.name: UK Street Soul
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1980s and early 1990s; combines raw basslines and breakbeats with Contemporary R&B/Soul vocals.

genres.name: Doo-Wop
genres.description: Heavy emphasis on male four-part harmonies and light instrumentation; peaked in popularity in the 1950s.
genres.track: I Only Have Eyes for You

genres.name: Funk
genres.description: Danceable, syncopated grooves carried by bass and drums alongside percussive guitar, keyboard, and/or horn parts, with rhythmic emphasis on the downbeat.

genres.name: Afro-Funk
genres.description: Strongly mixed with traditional and more modern genres in sub-Saharan West Africa.

genres.name: Britfunk
genres.description: Energetic, up-tempo style born out of late-1970s British Jazz-Funk nightclubs.

genres.name: Deep Funk
genres.description: Focuses more on grooves and rhythm than songwriting.

genres.name: Go-Go
genres.description: Dominated by drums and percussion (primarily congas) with heavily syncopated rhythms, bursts of horns, and call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Bounce Beat
genres.description: Modernized, youth oriented form heavily utilizing rototoms, timbale and keyboards for grooves.

genres.name: Latin Funk
genres.description: Funk combined with Hispanic American Music styles.

genres.name: P-Funk
genres.description: Features a "fat", monotonic drum sound, spaced-out synthesizers, "squelchy" basslines, tight, syncopated horns, and sometimes heavy guitars.
genres.track: Give Up The Funk (Tear The Roof Off The Sucker)

genres.name: Porn Groove
genres.description: Primarily found in the soundtracks to Pornographic films of the 1970s; characterized by a wah-wah electric guitar sound, slapped basslines, and minimal drums.
genres.album: The Golden Age of Danish Pornography

genres.name: Synth Funk
genres.description: Stripped-down and futuristic, driven by synthesizer melodies and often incorporating drum machines.
genres.track: This Must Be the Place (Naive Melody)

genres.name: Minneapolis Sound
genres.description: Emerged in late 1970s Minneapolis, characterized by glossy Contemporary R&B-influenced production techniques, angular New Wave-inspired rhythms, and a larger emphasis on electric guitar layers.

genres.name: New Orleans R&B
genres.description: Increased rhythmic complexity with added focus on piano and horns.

genres.name: Rhythm & Blues
genres.description: Predominantly African American style that retains the defined backbeats, Blues chord progressions/melodies and passionate singing/shouting of Jump Blues, while appealing more to an urban audience with smaller bands and reduced Jazz influence.

genres.name: British Rhythm & Blues
genres.description: A style infusing Rock and R&B that was hugely popular in the United Kingdom between 1963 and 1966.
genres.album: Having a Rave Up with The Yardbirds

genres.name: Swamp Pop
genres.description: Uniquely Cajun style of Rhythm & Blues distinguished by tripleted pianos and a slow Blues structure.

genres.name: Twist
genres.description: Simple, fast, and energetic dance popular in the early 1960s.

genres.name: West Side Sound
genres.description: Created in the 1950s by working-class Mexican-American teenagers in San Antonio, Texas, as a result of significant stylistic cross-pollination and an accommodating racial climate; features prominent tenor sax sections and Hammond organs.

genres.name: Soul
genres.description: Originated in the African American culture of the 20th century, resulting from the combination of the ecstatic vocals of Gospel with the upbeat instrumentation of Rhythm & Blues, consisting of guitar, bass and percussion.

genres.name: Chicago Soul
genres.description: Combination of the hard, groove-oriented rhythms of Southern Soul and the sophisticated gloss of the Motown Sound which was developed in Chicago.

genres.name: Country Soul
genres.description: Combining the gritty horn-driven sound of Southern Soul with the textures and aesthetics of Country.

genres.name: Deep Soul
genres.description: Draws on the typical Southern Soul groove and accentuates the Gospel and Blues influence, particularly Chicago Blues.
genres.album: I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You

genres.name: Latin Soul
genres.description: Soul combined with Hispanic American Music, such as Salsa and Mambo.

genres.name: Neo-Soul
genres.description: Emerged during the mid-to-late 1990s; defined by a combination of Soul with the rhythmic percussion and groove of Hip Hop.

genres.name: Philly Soul
genres.description: Defined by lush arrangements, often borrowing upon the orchestral instrumentation seen on productions from the 1960s, with the commercial atmosphere exemplified by Pop Soul and the Motown Sound.

genres.name: Progressive Soul
genres.description: Greater harmonic complexity, less conventional song structures, and conceptual, socially conscious or introspective lyrical themes, incorporating diverse influences and instrumentation from Jazz, Funk, Rock, and beyond.

genres.name: Smooth Soul
genres.description: Slow tempo ballads with silky, often sensual, vocals and light, polished arrangements, creating an intimate, romantic atmosphere.

genres.name: Southern Soul
genres.description: Soul primarily from the American South that was popular in the 1960s and 1970s, with a gritty and raw sound that places an emphasis on the groove, making it highly danceable.
genres.track: I've Been Loving You Too Long
genres.album: Otis Blue: Otis Redding Sings Soul

genres.name: Reggae / Ska / Dancehall
genres.description: Umbrella for related forms of Jamaican Music which have grown beyond their regional roots to become global phenomena.

genres.name: Dancehall
genres.description: Developed from Reggae in the late 1970s, when Roots Reggae became more stripped-down, with an increased emphasis on pure rhythm.

genres.name: Digital Dancehall
genres.description: First, pre-Ragga style of Dancehall to popularize Electronic rhythms that arose in the mid-1980s.

genres.name: Gommance
genres.description: Emerged in Réunion, mixing Caribbean, African and Afro-Dutch influences.

genres.name: Ragga
genres.description: Hardcore style with a deejay (equivalent to an MC in Hip Hop) rapping over predominantly Electronic rhythms.

genres.name: Shatta
genres.description: French Caribbean Dancehall subgenre with a focus on sparse percussion, heavy basslines and lyrics revolving around partying and sensuality, often in Creole.

genres.name: Trap Dancehall
genres.description: Combines midtempo Dancehall rhythms and tempos with major elements borrowed from Trap, namely in percussion and drum rhythms.

genres.name: Zess
genres.description: Trinidadian style that originated in the country's slums in the late 2010s, defined by its sexual, violent, and occasionally gang-related lyrics and its influence from Soca, as well as occasional influences from Hip Hop and Funk brasileiro.

genres.name: Reggae
genres.description: Developed in the 1960s; shuffling "bubble" and offbeat rhythms played on an organ, and staccato guitar and piano chords known as "skank."

genres.name: Deejay
genres.description: Reggae in which a deejay (similar to an MC in Hip Hop) talks or chants lyrics over a pre-recorded reggae rhythm.

genres.name: Dub
genres.description: Primarily instrumental Reggae which developed from the extensive use of studio techniques and effects like reverb and delay.

genres.name: Lovers Rock
genres.description: Smooth, quiet Reggae beats with lyrics focusing on romance and love.

genres.name: Pacific Reggae
genres.description: Developed in Pacific island communities, incorporating elements from local Oceanian Music styles.

genres.name: Jawaiian
genres.description: Hawaiian branch of Reggae, typically blends local traditional melodies, harmonies, incorporating specialty instruments such as ukulele and steel guitar.

genres.name: Roots Reggae
genres.description: Primarily defined through the political, spiritual, and socially conscious messages of its lyrics.

genres.name: Dub Poetry
genres.description: Poetry with Dub and Reggae backing rhythms, originating in Jamaica in the 1970s.

genres.name: Seggae
genres.description: Fusion of Séga and Reggae, popular on Mauritius and other Mascarene Islands.

genres.name: Skinhead Reggae

genres.name: New Tone

genres.name: Mozambique
genres.description: Cuban genre featuring energetic, African-influenced percussion.

genres.name: Pachanga
genres.description: Combination of Merengue, Conga, Rumba cubana, and Cumbia; fast, festive, and playful.

genres.name: Pilón
genres.description: Featuring rhythms described as mimicking those created while pounding sugarcane with African baton-like tools.

genres.name: Rumba cubana
genres.description: Folkloric manifestation of Afro-Cuban music that encompasses dance, voice, and drums.

genres.name: Guaguancó
genres.description: Emerged after the abolition of slavery in Cuba in 1886; usually features a lead singer, accompanied by three large drums, known as tumbadoras or congas, and a call-and-response chorus.

genres.name: Son cubano
genres.description: Cuban style popular from the 1920s to the 1950s that combines the structure of Spanish song-oriented styles with African rhythms and percussion.

genres.name: Bolero son
genres.description: Blend of Bolero and Son cubano that appeared during the 1920s.

genres.name: Son montuno
genres.description: Developed in the 1940s, characterized by more elaborate instrumental arrangements and larger ensembles typically adding a horn section, conga drums, and piano.
genres.album: Buena Vista Social Club Presents Manuel 'Guajiro' Mirabal

genres.name: Songo
genres.description: Cuban style originating in the late 1960s, combining elements from Rumba cubana and Son cubano with Jazz and Funk.

genres.name: Timba
genres.description: Combines Salsa with other genres such as Hip Hop, Disco, Funk, Jazz and Rock.

genres.name: Trova
genres.description: One of the most ancient expressions of Cuban Music, based around lone Singer-Songwriters who use nothing but a guitar as their preferred accompaniment and place emphasis on lyrics.

genres.name: Nueva trova
genres.description: Found inspiration in the 1950s Cuban Revolution and had the intention of introducing new musical ideas to the original Trova.

genres.name: Cumbia colombiana
genres.description: Style that incorporates elements of Colombian traditional music, which includes and keeps influences from Spanish, African, and Indigenous cultures.

genres.name: Dembow
genres.description: Originated in the Dominican Republic during the early 1990s, featuring rapping indebted to Hip Hop and a style drawing on Dancehall, particularly the "Dem Bow" riddim.

genres.name: French Caribbean Music
genres.description: Music from the French Antilles (Martinique, Guadeloupe, Dominica, Saint Lucia) and from Haiti.

genres.name: Biguine
genres.description: Dating back to the 19th century; originating as a fusion of traditional Bele music with Polka.
genres.album: El Maëstro et son Orchestre avec Guy Durosier

genres.name: Bouyon
genres.description: With a name translating to "broth", this fast-paced genre from Dominica originated as a blend of various traditional and modern Caribbean styles.

genres.name: Cadence lypso
genres.description: Caribbean genre originating in the 1970s, combining elements of Haiti's Cadence rampa and Compas with Trinidad's Calypso.

genres.name: Dennery Segment
genres.description: Developed in Saint Lucia in the early 2010s; heavily influenced by Angolan Kuduro, as well as incorporating elements of Zouk and Lucian drums alongside suggestive lyrics usually sung in Kwéyòl (Saint Lucian Creole).

genres.name: Gwo ka
genres.description: Developed in the island of Guadeloupe; driven by a group of gwo ka drums.

genres.name: Haitian Music
genres.description: Encompasses the styles of music developed by the Haitian people.

genres.name: Cadence rampa
genres.description: Developed in parallel with Compas, based on Méringue with a stronger Cuban influence.

genres.name: Compas
genres.description: Popular genre from Haiti, updating the older Méringue style with influences from Mambo and Jazz.

genres.name: Rabòday
genres.description: Fast-paced rhythm inspired by Rara, with Electronic instrumentation and humorous sexual and political lyrics.

genres.name: Rara
genres.description: Derived from the Haitian Vodou Drumming tradition, often played at street festivals and carnivals and usually having celebratory or political lyrics.

genres.name: Rasin
genres.description: Blends the highly rhythmic drumming of traditional Haitian Vodou music with Rock-influenced electric instrumentation such as guitar, keyboard, and bass.

genres.name: Twoubadou
genres.description: Pastoral, often satirical Haitian style usually performed by small groups centered around the acoustic guitar.

genres.name: Tumbélé
genres.description: Combines Haitian Compas, Soukous and Cuban Guaguancó with the local style of Biguine.

genres.name: Zouk
genres.description: Fast-paced danceable pop that began in early 1980s French Antilles, merging and updating more traditional local genres.

genres.name: Cabo-Zouk
genres.description: Popular in Cape Verde and the Cape Verdean diaspora in Europe and North America, with a slow and sensuous tempo, and favoring more sophisticated studio productions.

genres.name: Zouk Love
genres.description: More sentimental form of Zouk which emerged in the mid-1980s.

genres.name: Gaita zuliana
genres.description: Emerged in the state of Zulia in the 1950s, merging Spanish Folk Music and Venezuelan Christmas carols.

genres.name: Garifuna Music
genres.description: Music of the Garifuna, an Afro-Indigenous people from Central America and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

genres.name: Punta
genres.description: Garifuna Music with influences from other Caribbean genres such as Reggae, Soca, and Zouk, as well as Hispanic American Music.

genres.name: Goombay
genres.description: Bahamian music centered around the drum known as the goombay, a sort of membranophone.
genres.album: A Second Album Of Bahamian Songs

genres.name: Indo-Caribbean Music
genres.description: Music of the Indo-Caribbean diaspora.

genres.name: Baithak gana
genres.description: Indo-Caribbean genre from Suriname, consisting of Bhojpuri Folk Music with local Caribbean influence.
genres.album: Baithak Gana (Songs From Bihar, Uttar Pradesh And Surinam)

genres.name: Chutney
genres.description: Indo-Caribbean genre developing as a fusion of Bhojpuri Folk Music with traditional Caribbean songs; later influenced by Calypso, Soca and Filmi.
genres.album: Kaise Bani: A Unique Blend of Indian and Calypso Music

genres.name: Chutney Soca
genres.description: Mixture of Soca rhythms with Chutney's Indo-Caribbean traits and instrumentation.

genres.name: Jamaican Music
genres.description: Regional music of Jamaica ranges from its cultural origins in traditional and religious folk of the late 19th and early 20th centuries to the international popularity of Reggae from the 1970s onwards.

genres.name: Nyahbinghi
genres.description: Performed at Rastafari religious ceremonies, consisting of tripartite hand-drumming and often accompanied by vocal chants.

genres.name: Junkanoo
genres.description: Highly rhythmic Bahamian style which traditionally accompanies the arts festival and street parade of the same name.
genres.album: Religious Songs & Drums in the Bahamas

genres.name: Kaseko
genres.description: Surinamese popular music with roots in Surinamese Creole music, which was influenced by folk traditions of Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

genres.name: Merengue
genres.description: Dominican Republic dance genre that had a commercial boom at the end of the 1980s.

genres.name: Mambo urbano
genres.description: Rhythmically simpler and more eclectic style, absorbing influences from Hip Hop, Reggaetón, and other modern genres, particularly in regards to vocals.

genres.name: Merecumbé
genres.description: Colombian genre which combines Cumbia with Merengue.

genres.name: Merengue típico
genres.description: Earliest, most stripped-down form of Merengue.

genres.name: Merenhouse
genres.description: Popularized by Dominican-American artists of the 1990s, blending modern Merengue with electronic instrumentation and the combination of rapping/singing vocals.

genres.name: Tecnomerengue
genres.description: Fuses basic Merengue rhythms with influences from Cumbia and Lambada, being largely synthesized, with live instruments usually limited to percussion and brass.

genres.name: Palo de mayo
genres.description: Upbeat music accompanying maypole dancing from the Caribbean coast of Central America.

genres.name: Parang
genres.description: Latin-Caribbean genre central to Trinidad and Tobago and Venezuela traditionally used for nighttime celebrations in Trinidadian towns.

genres.name: Porro
genres.description: Lively Hispanic American Music and dance style native to Colombia which gained popularity in the 1940s.

genres.name: Soca
genres.description: Upbeat, poppy and danceable style rooted in Calypso and Indo-Caribbean Music; developed in the late 1960s and early 1970s in Trinidad and Tobago.

genres.name: Power Soca
genres.description: Often at a tempo of 160 BPM and incorporating hard, frantic rhythms, highly synthesized production, and call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Rapso
genres.description: Fusion of Soca and Hip Hop unique to Trinidad and Tobago.

genres.name: Steel Band
genres.description: Ensembles made out of steel drums that often perform Standards, Calypso, and Western Classical Music with densely rhythmic and colorful arrangements.

genres.name: Tropicanibalismo
genres.description: Colombian scene born in the early 2000s with the intention of reinventing Colombian coastal music, from a more current and experimental approach.

genres.name: Vallenato
genres.description: Accordion-led style of folk and popular music originating in Colombia's Caribbean region.
genres.track: En Teusaquillo Te Pueden Partir la Cara

genres.name: Central American Music
genres.description: Music from the Central American region (including Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama).

genres.name: Cumbia salvadoreña
genres.description: Takes influence from local Salvadoran music and traditionally features a distinctive ensemble.
genres.album: ¡Soy Salvadoreño! Chanchona Music from Eastern El Salvador

genres.name: Purísima
genres.description: Nicaraguan Hymn to the Immaculate Conception of Mary, sung during holiday celebrations and in liturgical or parochial services.

genres.name: Son nica
genres.description: Nicaraguan popular rhythm in distinctive guitar strums, with lyrics relating to the countryside and peasant life.
genres.artist: Carlos Mejía Godoy y Los de Palacagüina
genres.album: el son nuestro de cada dia

genres.name: Tamborera
genres.description: Panamanian popular genre which mixes local Tamborito with Cuban Music rhythms featuring the tambora as the main percussion instrument.

genres.name: Xuc
genres.description: Danceable style from El Salvador developed in the 1940s.
genres.album: Paquito Palaviccini presenta el xuc: nuevo ritmo salvadoreño

genres.name: Christian Liturgical Music
genres.description: Traditionally accompanies church services, as well as extra-liturgical functions such as processionals and sermons.
genres.track: Mass in B minor BWV 232: 2. Duet: Christe eleison

genres.name: Anglican Chant
genres.description: Simple, harmonized, English-language setting of the Christian liturgy, principally devised by the Anglican Church.
genres.track: Psalm 119 "Blessed Are Those That Are Undefiled in the Way" (Arr. for Choir & Organ): Verses 145-152
genres.album: The Complete Psalms of David: Volume 9, Series 2

genres.name: Kyivan Chant
genres.description: Chant form inspired by Znamenny Chant that's characterized by simplified melodic and rhythmic structures.
genres.artist: Monks Choir of Kiev Pechersk Monastery
genres.album: 1000 YEARS: Selected Chants of Russian Orthodox Church

genres.name: Mass
genres.description: Composition that sets to music text from the liturgy of the Eucharist, principally from the Latin rites of the Roman Catholic Church.

genres.name: Requiem
genres.description: Musical setting commemorating the deceased with text usually derived from the Roman Catholic mass of the dead.
genres.track: A German Requiem, Op. 45: I. Selig sind, die da Leid tragen

genres.name: Russian Orthodox Liturgical Music
genres.description: Tradition of the Russian Orthodox Church, implemented with the Christianization of Kievan Rus' in 988.
genres.track: Choir Concerto: I. O pavelitel' sushcheva fsevo

genres.name: Znamenny Chant
genres.description: Prototypical liturgical chant of the Russian Orthodox Church.

genres.name: Syriac Chant
genres.description: Liturgical chant repertoire practiced within Syriac Christianity, comprising the East Syrian and West Syrian liturgical rites.

genres.name: European Music
genres.description: Regional styles with roots in the European continent and surrounding islands.

genres.name: Alpenrock
genres.description: Mixes Hard Rock and Blues Rock with traditional Alpine Folk Music elements such as Yodeling and use of the accordion.

genres.name: Ashkenazi Music
genres.description: Encompasses the various traditions and genres of the Ashkenazi Jews, an ethnoreligious group that was prominent and influential in Europe throughout most of the Middle Ages and the modern period.

genres.name: Ashkenazi Cantorial Music
genres.description: Artistic, refined form of Chazzanut that greatly borrows from and implements elements of Western Classical Music and Christian Liturgical Music into the context of liturgical singing and chanting.

genres.name: Klezmer
genres.description: Secular Ashkenazi Music traditionally used in ceremonies such as weddings and bar and bat mitzvahs.

genres.name: Balkan Music
genres.description: Meta-genre covering all forms developed in the Balkan Peninsula.
genres.album: Le Mystère des voix bulgares, Volume 1

genres.name: Entechna
genres.description: First appeared in Greece in the late 1950s, featuring orchestrated arrangements with influence from Greek Folk Music and the popular Laika style.

genres.name: Entechna laika
genres.description: Artistic side of Laika played mainly but not always with the basic instruments of it, the bouzouki, Greek baglama, and the jouras, sometimes with the accompaniment of orchestras.

genres.name: Neo Kyma
genres.description: First appeared in the middle of the 1960s, rooted in Entechna, taking major inspiration from French Chanson.

genres.name: Laika
genres.description: Greek popular music played with local instruments like the bouzouki, Greek baglama, and the jouras.
genres.album: Μια στο καρφί και μια στο πέταλο [Mia sto Karfi kai Mia sto Petalo]

genres.name: Yu-Mex
genres.description: Style of popular music from former Yugoslavia that incorporates elements of Mexican Music.

genres.name: British Music
genres.description: Music of Great Britain, including the music of the English, Welsh and Scottish people.

genres.name: British Brass Band
genres.description: An ensemble consisting of a standardized range of brass and percussion instruments whose performances are based on the British tradition established in the early 19th century.

genres.name: British Folk Rock
genres.description: Developed in the late 1960s; influenced by traditional British folk music, particularly English Folk Music.

genres.name: Concertina Band
genres.description: Ensemble consisting of concertinas of various pitches and percussion instruments originating in 19th-century England.
genres.album: the mexborough english concertina prize band

genres.name: Celtic Rock
genres.description: Incorporates influences from Celtic Folk Music and its regional variants.

genres.name: Chanson
genres.description: French-language Singer-Songwriters for whom the quality of the text is essential and where the rhythm follows that of the text.

genres.name: Chanson alternative
genres.description: Usually politically engaged and humorous with eclectic influences of Regional Music, especially Fanfare, Musette, Jazz manouche and Romani Folk Music.

genres.name: Chanson québécoise
genres.description: French-language music of the Québécois singer-songwriters.

genres.name: Chanson réaliste
genres.description: Very popular in France in the late 19th century up to World War II, typically performed by female singers in a Cabaret or Vaudeville style and featuring "realist" lyrics.

genres.name: Chanson à texte
genres.description: French-language songs emphasising sophisticated and poetic lyricism.

genres.name: Nouvelle chanson française
genres.description: Both a subgenre of Chanson and a specific scene from the 1990s incorporating alternative trends from this period and new and unusual ways within Chanson tradition.

genres.name: Crimean Tatar Music
genres.description: Music of the Crimean Tatar people, a Turkic ethnic group indigenous to the Crimean Peninsula, located in southern Ukraine.

genres.name: Dechovka
genres.description: Brass band genre popular in Czechia and Slovakia, characterized by lively brass instrumentation, infectious rhythms, and vibrant melodies.

genres.name: Fanfare
genres.description: Brass-led tradition originating in Western Europe, commonly performed during important public events, typically featuring a ceremonious, triumphant, or uplifting sound.
genres.artist: くものすカルテット [Kumonosu Quartet]

genres.name: Finnish Tango
genres.description: Melancholic style developed in Finland in the 1930s and 1940s, influenced by traditional minor-key Finnish Folk Music melodies and the rhythms of German marches.

genres.name: German Music
genres.description: Music of the German-speaking people, spanning predominately central Europe, primarily Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, among others.

genres.name: Liedermacher
genres.description: German style having its origins in literature and theatre rather than American forms like Blues or Rock.

genres.name: Greek Music
genres.description: Music of the Greek people.

genres.name: Hornpipe
genres.description: Originally English dance characterized by dotted rhythms and strong downbeat emphasis.
genres.track: Durangs Hornpipe With Little Brown Jug
genres.album: Durangs Hornpipe With Little Brown Jug

genres.name: Iberian Music
genres.description: Music of the Iberian peninsula.

genres.name: Euskal kantagintza berria
genres.description: Basque genre born during the 1960s inspired by Nova cançó and Chanson.

genres.name: Nova cançó
genres.description: Arose in Catalonia during the Franco dictatorship, sung in Catalan as a way to resist restrictions placed on regional languages in Spain and retain a regional identity.

genres.name: Portuguese Music
genres.description: Music of Portugal.

genres.name: Música de intervenção
genres.description: Wave of Portuguese singer-songwriters in the 1960s and 1970s who agitated against the Estado Novo regime and the colonial war waged by Portugal against national liberation fronts.

genres.name: Pimba
genres.description: Humorous lyrics and a basic harmonic structure.
genres.track: Tu és a que eu quero

genres.name: Spanish Music
genres.description: Music of Spain.

genres.name: Bolero español
genres.description: Spanish genre originating in the 18th century, based around moderate tempos in a 3/4 time signature accompanied by a dance of the same name.

genres.name: Flamenco
genres.description: Traditional Spanish style based around fiery acoustic guitar rhythms, emotional vocals, and accompaniment from traditional percussion and dance.

genres.name: Bulería
genres.description: Fast flamenco made up of a 12 beat cycle characterized by its vibrant, spontaneous and festive style.

genres.name: Flamenco nuevo
genres.description: Contemporary style of Flamenco which departs from tradition by incorporating influences from other genres like Jazz, Blues, and Rock.

genres.name: Rumba flamenca
genres.description: Flamenco subgenre, derived from the exchange of influences between Spain and Latin America.

genres.name: Nueva canción española
genres.description: Arose in Spain in the 1960s, inspired in part by Nova cançó's reclaiming of Catalan regional identity, that spread across the country in regional variations.

genres.name: Rock andaluz
genres.description: Emerged during the mid-1970s in Spain; primarily utilizes Flamenco and often Symphonic Prog elements.

genres.name: Villancico
genres.description: Style of polyphonic lyric poetry popular between the 14th and 18th centuries that developed in Spain, Portugal, and their associated colonies.
genres.album: Villancicos y danzas criollas de la Iberia antigua al Nuevo Mundo (1550-1750)

genres.name: Italian Music
genres.description: Music of the Italian people.
genres.track: Canzone del maggio - Liberamente tratta da un canto del maggio francese 1968

genres.name: Canzone d'autore
genres.description: Music of the Italian Singer-Songwriters that emerged in the 1960s and early 1970s, initially influenced by French Chanson with the addition of uniquely Italian sensibilities.
genres.album: Non Al Denaro, Non All'Amore, Ne Al Cielo

genres.name: Kleinkunst
genres.description: Dutch-language genre from the Netherlands and Flanders with influences from Cabaret, protest songs, Chanson, and folk.

genres.name: Mittelalter-Rock
genres.description: Emerged in the 1990s from the German Neo-Medieval movement, incorporating medieval instruments with Rock music.

genres.name: Nordic Music
genres.description: Music from the Nordic countries, including Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and Finland.

genres.name: Greenlandic Music
genres.description: Majorly from Inuit ethnic groups in Greenland, a large island between the Atlantic and Arctic Oceans.

genres.name: Vaigat
genres.description: Contemporary popular music shaped by American cultural exchanges and indigenous Greenlandic heritage.

genres.name: Nordic Folk Rock
genres.description: Fusion of Nordic Folk Music and Rock.

genres.name: Rautalanka
genres.description: Nordic guitar style mainly influenced by Rock & Roll, and traditional European Schlager.

genres.name: Visa
genres.description: Nordic balladry focusing on lyrical content and simple vocal melodies.
genres.album: Tio vackra visor och personliga Person

genres.name: Nòva cançon
genres.description: Arose in the Occitania region of southern France, sung in the Occitan language as a way to preserve their culture and resist forced usage of French.
genres.track: Istòria au còrn deu temps : País vençut / L'aulhèr / L'òmi de nueit / Qu'éra lo temps / Causir

genres.name: Polish Music
genres.description: Music rooted in the traditions of the Poles.
genres.album: Ewa Demarczyk śpiewa piosenki Zygmunta Koniecznego

genres.name: Mazurka
genres.description: Folk or folk-inspired form based on the triple-time rhythm of Mazur, Kujawiak and Oberek.

genres.name: Miejski folk
genres.description: Alternative and Punk music influenced by Folklor miejski and Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Poezja śpiewana
genres.description: Polish sung poetry; the poem is the centerpiece of a song, often with sparse instrumental accompaniment.

genres.name: Polonaise
genres.description: Stately national dance with music in triple meter and moderate tempo.

genres.name: Romanian Music
genres.description: Music of the Romanian people.
genres.album: Honourable Brigands, Magic Horses & Evil Eye

genres.name: Romanian Etno Music
genres.description: Romanian style which emerged in the early 1990s as a revival of Romanian Folk Music, blending traditional music with dance-pop rhythms.

genres.name: Russian Music
genres.description: Music of the Russian people.

genres.name: Avtorskaya pesnya
genres.description: Originating in the Soviet Union taking cues from forms of Russian Romance and Russian poetry with the main focus on lyrics.
genres.track: It Is Echoing All Over the World

genres.name: Bard Rock
genres.description: Mixes Rock music and styles with Avtorskaya pesnya.

genres.name: Russian Romance
genres.description: Popular Russian genre of melancholy balladry.

genres.name: Schottische
genres.description: Social dance with a simple, bouncy rhythm in 2/4 or 4/4 which originated from central Europe by the late 18th century, developing into a wide number of regional variations around the world.

genres.name: Trampská hudba
genres.description: Associated with the tramping lifestyle, typically mixing acoustic guitar driven Contemporary Folk with strong Country influences and vocal harmonies in peaceful, simple and relatively short songs.

genres.name: Waltz
genres.description: Typically in a 3/4 time signature and popular in the 18th century in central Europe, as it accompanied the ballroom dance of the same name.
genres.track: Waltzes, Op. 69: No. 1 in A-Flat Major, B. 95

genres.name: Vals venezolano
genres.description: Venezuelan dance music that employs heavy use of syncopation, complex rhythms, and regional instruments.

genres.name: Hispanic Music
genres.description: Music of Hispanic America and Spain, and the genres shared between them.

genres.name: Hispanic American Music
genres.description: Includes all genres created by Hispanic Americans.

genres.name: Argentine Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Argentine people.

genres.name: Cuarteto
genres.description: Originated in the Argentinian province of Córdoba, usually with an upbeat rhythm and originally performed with a four-piece band.
genres.track: Te voy a romper el or...

genres.name: Cumbia argentina
genres.description: Almost always features synthesizer keyboards and electronic percussion with an upbeat rhythm.

genres.name: Cumbia santafesina
genres.description: Originated in the Argentinian province of Santa Fe, particularly in its capital city Santa Fe de la Vera Cruz, with lyrics that tend to be romantic and relatively clean compared to later Cumbia argentina.

genres.name: Cumbia turra
genres.description: Cumbia argentina heavily influenced by Reggaetón and characterized by hard-hitting bass and heavy use of samples and Auto-Tune.

genres.name: Cumbia villera
genres.description: Developed in the villa miserias (shanty towns) by the lower classes of Argentina in the early 2000s, featuring basic rhythms and low budget productions combined with lyrics that can be openly sexual or touch on sociopolitical issues.

genres.name: Guaracha santiagueña
genres.description: Fast, upbeat and danceable rhythm originated in the province of Santiago del Estero, Argentina as a fusion of Chacarera and Chamamé.

genres.name: Nuevo Cancionero
genres.description: Musical-literary movement in Argentina that aimed to reevaluate and reinvigorate "la música popular nativa" (native popular music) and to be the voice of poor and marginalized Argentines.

genres.name: RKT
genres.description: Emerged in the early 2010s, characterized by minimalistic, rhythm-centric production heavily influenced by Cumbia villera and other Cumbia argentina styles.

genres.name: Bolero
genres.description: Ballad with a 2/4 time signature that appeared in eastern Cuba towards the end of the 19th century.

genres.name: Boogaloo
genres.description: Upbeat fusion of American Rhythm & Blues and Jazz with Son cubano which originated in the early 1960s in New York City and became popular with both its Black and Latino communities.

genres.name: Caporal
genres.description: Bolivian neofolkloric dance music characterized by a double beat bass drum pattern that emerged in the latter half of the twentieth century.

genres.name: Carnaval cruceño
genres.description: Danceable genre, similar to the Polka, from the city of Santa Cruz, Bolivia, characteristic of the area’s Carnival celebrations and generally composed for brass band musicians.

genres.name: Chilean Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Chilean people.

genres.name: Chilote Music
genres.description: Music of the Chiloé Archipelago.

genres.name: Cumbia chilena
genres.description: Incorporates Chilean Music into the traditional sound of Cumbia.

genres.name: Nueva cumbia chilena
genres.description: Rock-infused instrumentation, incorporating an eclectic repertoire of influences, such as Ska, Salsa, Indigenous Andean Music, Reggae, and Bolero.

genres.name: Jazz guachaca
genres.description: Encompasses Jazz influences with Hispanic American Music styles such as Cueca, Bolero, Tango and Corrido.
genres.album: Los Tiempos de la Negra Ester

genres.name: Mambo chileno
genres.description: Emerged in the early 2010s in Chile, characterized by upbeat rhythms and rapping, usually on topics of parties, dancing, and urban life.

genres.name: Música típica chilena
genres.description: Incorporation of rural folklore music to urban fields, adding vocal groups accompanied mainly by guitar and a "huaso" symbolism.

genres.name: Nueva canción chilena
genres.description: Socially conscious style that sought to recover traditional Chilean folk music and fuse it with the broader musical trends of Latin America.

genres.name: Conjunto andino
genres.description: Urban folk ensembles using musical instruments of Andean Indigenous origin or association; despite frequent association with Indigenous villages, they bear little resemblance to the Indigenous expressions of the Southern Andes.

genres.name: Cumbia
genres.description: Danceable folk genre formed during the 19th century in Colombia and eastern Panama.

genres.name: Cumbia mexicana
genres.description: Incorporation of Rock & Roll, Mexican popular music, and Cuban influences, often adopting electric instruments, brass ensembles, accordion, and Cuban timbales, while retaining a beat-driven sound and traditional Colombian features.
genres.track: La Perra Más Bonita del Cielo

genres.name: Cumbia sonidera
genres.description: Cumbia mexicana from Mexico City that developed in the 1990s as discomóviles (analogous to DJs) experimented with slowing down original cumbia to fit the popular dance tempos.

genres.name: Cumbia rebajada
genres.description: Based on Cumbia colombiana slowed down to around 76 bpm, with a lower timbre and less joyful sound.

genres.name: Cumbia peruana
genres.description: Developed in Peru and diversified into various subgenres, each with its own regional influences.

genres.name: Chicha
genres.description: Emerged during the Andean migration to the Peruvian coast between the 1960s and 1980s; largely influenced by Huayno and occasionally Psychedelic Rock

genres.name: Cumbia amazónica
genres.description: Mixes Cumbia peruana with selvatic dances, Afro-Latin rhythms, Surf Rock, and Psychedelic Rock between the 1960s and 1980s.

genres.name: Cumbia norteña peruana
genres.description: Developed on the Peruvian coast, with influences from Cumbia colombiana and cumbia ecuatoriana and lyrics mostly about love and heartbreak.

genres.name: Currulao
genres.description: Pacific coast Afro-Colombian music and folk dance performed by a marimba/percussion ensemble with heavy use of call-and-response vocals.

genres.name: Guarania
genres.description: Slow and melancholic rhythms, primarily performed on the Paraguayan harp.

genres.name: Huayno
genres.description: Andean dance music that incorporates both pre-Hispanic and Western musical elements.
genres.track: Canto A La Mujer De Mi Pueblo
genres.album: Canto a la Mujer de mi Pueblo

genres.name: Bolivian Huayño
genres.description: One of the most popular genres of Andean music in Bolivia, particularly present in the departments of Cochabamba, Chuquisaca, La Paz, Oruro and Potosí.

genres.name: Carnavalito
genres.description: Fast and lively; mostly played in northwestern Argentina in the provinces of Jujuy, Salta, and Tucumán.

genres.name: Latin Alternative
genres.description: Incorporates common elements from Hispanic American Music like Cumbia, Tango or Mexican Music into Rock.

genres.name: Latin Rock
genres.description: Fusion of Rock, often Psychedelic Rock, with Latin American rhythms, especially Afro-Latin genres.

genres.name: Mexican Music
genres.description: Music of Mexico and those deeply rooted in Mexican traditions.

genres.name: Bandas de viento de México
genres.description: Mexican ensemble with many regional variations dating back to the 1860s and 1870s, when locals attempted to imitate the military bands that were present in the country.

genres.name: Banda sinaloense
genres.description: Performed with militaristic-type arrangements of traditional Bandas de viento de México, with prominence on the tuba/sousaphone backing and tenor tuned horns.

genres.name: Movimiento alterado
genres.description: Arose from Sinaloa in the late 2000s; radicalizes some of the characteristics of Banda sinaloense and Norteño.

genres.name: Tecnobanda
genres.description: Emerged in the mid-1980s from the Banda sinaloense tradition, replacing certain instruments with synthesizers and electric instruments, allowing for faster tempos.

genres.name: Chilena
genres.description: Developed when music from the Costa Chica of Guerrero and Oaxaca in Mexico mixed with Cueca brought by Chilean sailors to the region in the 19th century.
genres.artist: Fonoteca del INAH Vol. 21: Música de la Costa Chica de Guerrero y Oaxaca
genres.album: Fonoteca del INAH Vol. 21: Música de la Costa Chica de Guerrero y Oaxaca

genres.name: Corrido
genres.description: Narrative ballad which arose in the late 18th century and flourished after the Mexican Independence War, originally meant for folk singers to spread news throughout Mexico accompanied by a guitar.

genres.name: Cumbiatón
genres.description: Combining Reggaetón with Cumbia mexicana, and less frequently with other forms of traditional Mexican Music.

genres.name: Mariachi
genres.description: Mexican style performed in unique costumes by ensembles known as mariachi bands, with a distinctive sound combining high, bright tones with low and rich voicings.
genres.album: Con El Mariachi Vargas De Tecalitlan

genres.name: Norteño
genres.description: More traditional, rural version of Tejano Music whose name translates to "northern".

genres.name: Cumbia norteña mexicana
genres.description: Norteño heavily influenced by Cumbia.

genres.name: Duranguense
genres.description: Features aspects of banda music, sped up, with the addition of synthesizers.

genres.name: Sierreño
genres.description: Norteño that is mainly played with guitars, as opposed to the traditional bajo sexto used in norteño.

genres.name: Corrido tumbado
genres.description: Modern take of regional Mexican music derived from Sierreño with heavy influence from the atmosphere of Trap music, while not engaging in that genre's characteristic sound.

genres.name: Ranchera
genres.description: Originating in rural Mexico in the 19th century and popularized in the 1930s; emphasizes passionate and emotional performances and love-focused lyrics, often performed with a Mariachi ensemble.

genres.name: Tejano Music
genres.description: Mexican-American style infusing the conjunto Norteño ensemble with European dances and American popular music.

genres.name: New Mexico Music
genres.description: Derived from the Traditional Folk Music of New Mexico mixed with influences from Western, Country and Norteño, particularly associated with Spanish-speaking Nuevomexicanos.

genres.name: Nueva canción latinoamericana
genres.description: Politically-charged messages associated with the rise of leftist social movements; striving for a renewal of traditional Latin and Hispanic American Folk Music expressions.
genres.album: las ultimas composiciones de violeta parra

genres.name: Onda nueva
genres.description: Based on Joropo, it incorporates elements of Bossa nova and Jazz.
genres.album: El Fabuloso Aldemaro y Su Onda Nueva

genres.name: Pasillo
genres.description: Traditional dance popular in Ecuador and Colombia; based on European Waltz and often performed with guitar and mandolin.

genres.name: Peruvian Music
genres.description: Music developed by the Peruvian people.

genres.name: Huaylarsh
genres.description: Festive Andean music with vibrant rhythm featuring saxophones and violins, typical of the central Peruvian region.

genres.name: Música criolla peruana
genres.description: Coastal Peruvian music tradition blending Spanish, African, and local influences, developed in urban contexts through creolized European dance forms.

genres.name: Festejo
genres.description: Happy and danceable Afro-Peruvian rhythm originating in the 17th century.

genres.name: Landó
