genres.description: 16th-century Afro-Peruvian dance and music style, played primarily on the cajón and the creole guitar in a 12/8 rhythm.
genres.album: Gran premio del festival hispanoamericano de la danza y la canción

genres.name: Marinera
genres.description: Component of the coastal dance of the same name, often considered the national dance of Peru.

genres.name: Tondero
genres.description: Backing to the fast-paced dance that originated in northern Peru in the region of Piura of the same name; bands consist of a singer, a small chorus, two guitarists, along with the cajón and sometimes a spoon player.

genres.name: Vals criollo
genres.description: Originally characterized by its 3/4 time, heavy reliance on strongly plucked phrase on upper strings, and its guitar solo; often accompanied by a duet or a solo singer, normally singing about patriotic themes or social dilemmas.

genres.name: Polka paraguaya
genres.description: Popular music originating in Paraguay and the Province of Corrientes (Argentina), derived from the Bohemian polka and traditional music of Hispanic-Jesuit origin.

genres.name: Reggaetón
genres.description: Rooted in Dancehall and mainly characterized by its heavy emphasis on the "dembow" rhythm; developed in Puerto Rico in the early 1990s under heavy influence from Hip Hop.

genres.name: Bachatón
genres.description: Mixes Bachata melodies and instrumentation with Reggaetón rhythms, rapping, and DJing.

genres.name: Doble paso
genres.description: Frenetic and intense high tempo variant in comparison to the standard drum patterns, often used to accompany the dance of the same name.
genres.artist: DJ Aldair el rey de la chancadera

genres.name: Neoperreo
genres.description: Heavy emphasis on rhythm, influence from global trends in club music, and generally progressive lyrics.

genres.name: Romantic Style
genres.description: Melodic and sentimental style characterized by emotive vocals and mellow sound with a less explicit tone, emphasizing romantic love themes, blending Contemporary R&B, Latin Pop and romantic ballad influences, popularized during early 2000s to 2010s.

genres.name: Rhumba
genres.description: Commercial adaptation of various Latin American genres; developed during the 1930s as the so-called "rhumba craze" unfolded in the United States.

genres.name: Rioplatense Music
genres.description: Music developed by the people of the Rio de la Plata region.
genres.album: Edición Crítica: Música Popular Contemporanea De La Ciudad De Buenos Aires Vol.2

genres.name: Candombe beat
genres.description: Fusion of Uruguayan Candombe with elements of Rock music.

genres.name: Tango
genres.description: Melancholic sound generally led by a guitar or bandoneon, originating in Buenos Aires by the late 19th century and gaining worldwide popularity from the 1920s to the 1950s.
genres.artist: Astor Piazzolla and The New Tango Quintet
genres.album: Tango: Zero Hour / Nuevo Tango: Hora Zero

genres.name: Tango nuevo
genres.description: Adds new elements into traditional Argentine Tango, most importantly the incorporation of Jazz and Western Classical Music.
genres.artist: Astor Piazzolla y su Quinteto Nuevo Tango
genres.album: Concierto De Tango En El Philarmonic Hall De New York

genres.name: Rock andino
genres.description: Emerged in the Andean countries in the late 1960s and early 1970s, incorporating traditional instruments and harmonies from Indigenous Andean Music within a Rock format.

genres.name: Salsa
genres.description: Often incorporating congas, timbales and bongos as well as smaller instruments, such as maracas, clave and güiro.

genres.name: Salsa dura
genres.description: Earlier form of Salsa, usually less rigid in structure allowing for extended jam sessions; lyrical themes revolve around the "barrio" way of life and Latin American traditions.

genres.name: Salsa romántica
genres.description: Salsa following a stronger influence from Pop, typically sharing shorter, conventional structures and romantic lyricism.

genres.name: Nueva canción
genres.description: Latin American (Nueva canción latinoamericana) and Spanish (Nueva canción española) movement during the 1960s and 1970s.
genres.track: El Derecho de Vivir en Paz
genres.album: El Derecho de Vivir en Paz

genres.name: Romance
genres.description: Form of narrative sung Poetry rooted in medieval Spanish oral tradition, characterized by octosyllabic verses and assonant rhyme. Evolving from epic Medieval Lyric Poetry, and later spread across Hispanic America.

genres.name: Indigenous American Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the indigenous peoples of the Americas.

genres.name: Indigenous Andean Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the indigenous peoples of the Andes.
genres.track: Jallalla Ayllu Pahaza Marka Qalaqutu Pakaxa

genres.name: Baguala
genres.description: Slow, triple-meter form of traditional Indigenous Andean Music originally performed by Diaguita people in present-day North-Western Argentina.

genres.name: Indigenous North American Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the indigenous peoples of present-day Canada, the United States and northwestern Mexico.

genres.name: Inuit Music
genres.description: Traditions of the Inuit people, the aboriginal peoples inhabiting the Arctic regions of Canada, Alaska, and Greenland.

genres.name: Métis Music
genres.description: Music of the indigenous Métis people of Canada and the United States.

genres.name: Pueblo Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of the Pueblo peoples, who are indigenous to the southwest United States.

genres.name: Mesoamerican Music
genres.description: Diverse styles and genres developed by the Indigenous peoples of Mesoamerica, a cultural region extending from central and southern Mexico through parts of Central America.
genres.artist: Sacred Guitar & Violin Music of the Modern Aztecs
genres.album: Sacred Guitar & Violin Music of the Modern Aztecs

genres.name: Maya Music
genres.description: Music of the Maya peoples.

genres.name: Nahua Music
genres.description: Musical traditions of the Nahuas, a major grouping of indigenous peoples inhabiting various regions in Mesoamerica, most notably Mexico.

genres.name: Islamic Religious Music & Recitation
genres.description: Music and melodic recitation involved in the Islamic faith, such as the reading of the Qur'an with its melodic component (qira'ah), the adhan call to prayer, and the elements often used in the practice of dhikr (particularly in Sufism).
genres.album: Ocean Of Remembrance: Sufi Improvisation & Zhikrs

genres.name: Maddahi
genres.description: Singing for Shia Muslims to mourn in religious death anniversaries.

genres.name: Shoor
genres.description: Mourning eulogy characterized by an intense emotional fervor and rhythmic delivery.
genres.artist: Shoor Music from Iran, Iraq & Lebanon
genres.track: Shoor Music from Iran, Iraq & Lebanon
genres.album: Shoor Music from Iran, Iraq & Lebanon

genres.name: Nasheed
genres.description: Vocal songs popular throughout the Islamic world, mostly performed A cappella though sometimes featuring light instrumentation.

genres.name: Jewish Music
genres.description: Different Jewish forms coming from different regions of the world, influenced by local cultures.

genres.name: Hasidic Music
genres.description: Covers the music of Hasidic Jews, primarily characterized by spiritual, intense, and devotional, singing and melodies.
genres.artist: Frank London, Lorin Sklamberg & Uri Caine

genres.name: Nigun
genres.description: Form of spiritual, repetitive and immersive tunes that developed in Hasidic Jewish communities, typically vocal-led.
genres.artist: Mark Feldman, Uri Caine, Greg Cohen & Joey Baron

genres.name: Jewish Liturgical Music
genres.description: Employed for different purposes in the practices of Jewish religion, such as the Kriyat haTorah of biblical verses during synagogue services.

genres.name: Chazzanut
genres.description: Traditions used by the Jewish cantor, the chazzan when reciting and chanting different parts of the Jewish prayer in Jewish Liturgical Music.

genres.name: Piyyut
genres.description: Liturgical Jewish poems that are chanted or recited during religious occasions such as daily prayers and holidays.
genres.album: ארבע אותיות שירת קודש ממערב הסהרה [arba otiyot – sacred hebrew songs from the saharan maghreb]

genres.name: Muzika yehudit mekorit
genres.description: Rooted in traditional Jewish Music, especially Hasidic Music; incorporates modern influences, typically written on subjects of devotion and religion.
genres.album: לילה כיום יאיר [night will shine like day]

genres.name: Oriental Jewish Music
genres.description: Comprises the many traditions and styles of the various groups of Jews from the cultural East, loosely covering the Jewish groups of the Middle East, North Africa, and Central Asia.

genres.name: Sephardic Music
genres.description: Encompasses the various musical traditions of Sephardi Jews.
genres.album: Sephardic Romances: Traditional Jewish Music From Spain

genres.name: Northern American Music
genres.description: Regional styles with roots in Northern America (America north of Mexico, including Canada, United States, Greenland, Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, and Bermuda), typically drawing from European Folk Music and Classical Music as well as West African Music and Indigenous American Music influences.

genres.name: Americana
genres.description: Incorporates a broad swath of American Folk Music and Contemporary Folk influences, evolving alongside Alt-Country.
genres.album: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe In You

genres.name: Barbershop
genres.description: Harmonized singing consisting of four vocal elements: the 'lead' (2nd tenor), the 1st tenor, the baritone, and the bass.

genres.name: Jubilee
genres.description: Rooted in African-American culture, characterized by complex rhythms and call-and-response vocals.
genres.track: Go Tell It On the Mountain

genres.name: Country Rock
genres.description: Combination of contemporary Rock with more traditional American Country.
genres.track: Only Love Can Break Your Heart

genres.name: Cosmic Country
genres.description: Synthesizes various American musical influences and the exploratory ethoses of Psychedelia and Progressive Country to create an ethereal and more experimental sound still rooted in traditional Country.

genres.name: Cowboy Poetry
genres.description: Descended from the oral traditions of cowboys and ranchers, written with traditional use of rhyme and meter, using humor and slang, and primarily concerning the cowboy profession, lifestyle, and legacy.

genres.name: Foxtrot
genres.description: Lightly syncopated ballroom dance form in 4/4, most popular in the 1930s and closely associated with early Big Band Jazz.
genres.album: Arthur Murray's Music for Dancing: Fox Trot

genres.name: Louisiana Music
genres.description: Regional Music from the US state of Louisiana.

genres.name: Cajun Music
genres.description: Associated with the Cajun people of Louisiana where the genre was born, commonly regarded as an uptempo, accordion-driven style with a harsh, infectious beat.

genres.name: New Orleans Brass Band
genres.description: New Orleans' unique combination of European-styled military bands with African folklore.

genres.name: Zydeco
genres.description: Uptempo accordion-led dance style mixing Creole and Cajun folk with African American popular music influences.

genres.name: Nouveau zydeco
genres.description: Adds new elements into contemporary Zydeco, most importantly the incorporation of Funk, Contemporary R&B and Hip Hop characteristics.
genres.track: Don't Tell Your Mama, Don't Tell Your Papa

genres.name: Pep Band
genres.description: Performs at athletic events, and typically performs modified versions of Pop songs.
genres.artist: The Ohio State University Marching Band
genres.track: Fight The Team Across The Field

genres.name: Ragtime
genres.description: Emerged in the 1890s; piano-led and characterized by a heavily syncopated rhythm.

genres.name: Cakewalk
genres.description: Typically in 2/4 time with a distinctive "oompah" rhythm, named for a dance created by enslaved Black Americans as a mockery of the social dances of white slaveholders.

genres.name: Honky-Tonk Piano
genres.description: Nostalgic revival popularised in the 1950s which is more upbeat and whimsical, with a bright and detuned piano sound.

genres.name: Novelty Piano
genres.description: Popular in the 1920s; originated in Chicago and took influence from Jazz.
genres.album: Forgotten Dreams: Archives of Novelty Piano

genres.name: Ragtime Song
genres.description: Incorporates syncopated, "ragged" rhythms into popular song forms.

genres.name: Roots Rock
genres.description: Consciously and predominantly incorporates elements of its predecessors and original roots such as Country, Blues, Rhythm & Blues, Rock & Roll, and American Folk Music, but also many other American traditions.

genres.name: Swamp Rock
genres.description: Incorporates influences from the musical styles and traditions of Louisiana.

genres.name: Tex-Mex
genres.description: Mixes Rock & Roll, Blues, Country, and several types of Hispanic American Music, particularly Tejano Music.

genres.name: Sacred Steel
genres.description: Focused on instrumentals and played on the steel guitar.
genres.album: Sacred Steel: Traditional Sacred African-American Steel Guitar Music in Florida

genres.name: Shaker Music
genres.description: Created by the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing, better known as Shakers, for worship.

genres.name: Southern Gospel
genres.description: Initially sung A cappella by a Vocal Group quartet, sometimes with a pianist or guitar as accompaniment, with lyrics and messages primarily revolving around the teachings found within Christianity.
genres.track: ALL OF MY FRIENDS ARE GOING TO HELL

genres.name: Texan Music
genres.description: Regional Music from the US state of Texas.
genres.artist: Stevie Ray Vaughan and Double Trouble

genres.name: Oceanian Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of the geographic region of Oceania.

genres.name: Melanesian Music
genres.description: Music of the Oceanian region of Melanesia.
genres.album: Solomon Islands: Cry of the Ancestors

genres.name: Kaneka
genres.description: New Caledonian style of popular music that draws influence from traditional Melanesian music.

genres.name: Papuan Folk Music
genres.description: Traditional Folk Music of the Papuan people of New Guinea.

genres.name: Tolai Rock
genres.description: Fuses the music of the Tolai people of Papua New Guinea with Rock.

genres.name: Micronesian Music
genres.description: Music of the Micronesian peoples.
genres.track: The Carpenter Song - Marshallese Nonsense Song

genres.name: Kantan Chamorrita
genres.description: Improvised verse singing performed in the Chamorro language, traditional of the Marianas islands.

genres.name: Polyphonic Chant
genres.description: Chanting that combines two or more melodic lines that are harmonically cohesive but differ in rhythm and utilize non-parallel motion.

genres.name: Prehistoric Music
genres.description: Styles from the first cultural periods of the human species (Homo sapiens, as well as certain Homo neanderthalensis). From its birth in the Paleolithic and Neolithic eras to the Ancient Music era beginning around 2000–3000 BC.
genres.album: Musical Instruments From Prehistory: The Paleolithic

genres.name: South American Music
genres.description: Rooted in the traditions of South America.

genres.name: Brazilian Music
genres.description: All forms of music with roots in Brazil.

genres.name: Brega
genres.description: Overstated, dramatic music with a romantic singing style.
genres.album: O Filho de José e Maria

genres.name: Arrocha
genres.description: Influenced by Brega's romantic style, with further influence from Axé and Forró, giving it a more sensual and euphoric feel.

genres.name: Arrochadeira
genres.description: Developed in the mid-2000s in Bahia by Dan Ventura, merges the electronic keyboards of Arrocha with Pagodão rhythms.
genres.album: NEM SÓ DE MALUQUICE VIVE O HOMEM

genres.name: Bregadeira
genres.description: Fuses contemporary rhythms from the Brazilian Northeast such as Arrocha, Pagodão and Piseiro, with the electronic beats of Funk brasileiro and its subgenres.

genres.name: Brega funk
genres.description: Rooted in Tecnobrega, features glossy syncopated MIDI pianos and synths, distinct pitched metallic snares and vocal chops over a wonky kick rhythm.

genres.name: Batidão romântico
genres.description: Slower and romantic Kizomba-fused beats.

genres.name: Dobrado
genres.description: Brazilian musical genre, played by military bands with wooden, brass and also percussive instruments.

genres.name: Funk brasileiro
genres.description: Hip Hop-influenced dance style originating from the favelas of Rio de Janeiro and known primarily as "funk" in Brazil.

genres.name: Arrocha funk
genres.description: Slow and gritty Reggaetón-like drums with an emphasis on brass sections influenced by Arrocha.
genres.track: Intenso boom boom ( Acompanha o Grave )

genres.name: Beat bolha
genres.description: Defined by its squeaky wisps and chopped bubbling samples, usually played around 130 to 170 BPM.

genres.name: Beat fino
genres.description: High pitched or sped up metallic percussion and Beatboxing loops with little to no bass.

genres.name: Funk 150 bpm
genres.description: Fast tempos, typically reaching 150 bpm and sometimes beyond it, heightened energy and typically faster flows as well.

genres.name: Funk carioca
genres.description: Early scene of Funk brasileiro that began in Rio de Janeiro, developed from a local take on American Miami Bass.

genres.name: Funk proibidão
genres.description: Raw, aggressive style that developed in the favelas of Rio de Janeiro in the 1990s, with a name translating to "prohibited funk" that hints at its gang origin.

genres.name: Funk consciente
genres.description: Emphasis on conscious lyrics.

genres.name: Funk de BH
genres.description: Atmospheric, mellow and minimalistic production with sparse percussion, often featuring sound effects or filtered samples.

genres.name: Funk ostentação
genres.description: Late 2000s take on Funk brasileiro from São Paulo state, featuring Pop Rap influences, having a more accessible sound.

genres.name: Rasteirinha
genres.description: Slow-paced, highly rhythmic with instrumentation derived from Samba and Axé, and Dancehall-inspired grooves.

genres.name: Trapfunk
genres.description: Heavy beats and prominent bass, common in Trap, along with the energy and fast-paced funk rhythm.

genres.name: MPB
genres.description: Short for música popular brasileira; formed in the mid-1960s as a modernized version of Bossa nova and Samba-canção.

genres.name: Northeastern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Regional styles that combines elements of indigenous, African and European traditions, historically with a focus on life of the northeastern people, such as drought, migration, the struggle for survival, love and nostalgia, and often danced in intense and accelerated movements.

genres.name: Afoxé
genres.description: Afro-Brazilian genre originating in the states of Pernambuco and Bahia, characterized by the ijexá rhythm invented by the Yoruba people.

genres.name: Axé
genres.description: Developed from a fusion of Frevo, Maracatu, Forró, Reggae and Calypso with roots in the Salvador de Bahia carnival.

genres.name: Pagodão
genres.description: Predominance of guitar riffs, atabaques, pandeiros and drums.

genres.name: Samba-reggae
genres.description: Percussion-focused style from Bahia, Brazil, originating in the 1980s and 1990s in the Bahian carnival's afro-blocos.

genres.name: Baião
genres.description: Commonly performed with accordions and violas caipiras, and often accompanied by agogô and triangle.

genres.name: Coco
genres.description: Performers usually gather in a circle which rounds the dancers, clapping and spinning according to the rhythm; influenced by cultures originating from Africa, conceived in Northeastern Brazil.

genres.name: Ciranda
genres.description: Employs a metrical scheme of quatrains, long verses, and slow pace, with lyrical themes generally limited to love.

genres.name: Embolada
genres.description: Focuses on the prosody of singers, who speak-sing improvised or written stanzas in fast tempos in 2/4 time, accompanied by sparse percussion.

genres.name: Forró
genres.description: Developed from Baião and the dance rhythms quadrilha and xaxado, along with influences of European Folk Music like chula and schottische (Xote).

genres.name: Forró eletrônico
genres.description: Uses electronic elements through the inclusion of keyboards, bass, and electric guitar.

genres.name: Forró de favela
genres.description: Originating from the outskirts of Fortaleza, with MPB-influenced lyrics and a calmer and more romantic sound.

genres.name: Piseiro
genres.description: Originated in the interior of northeast Brazil in the 2000s, characterized by the combination of electronic keyboards with vocal harmonization; typically considered a homemade style of Forró eletrônico.

genres.name: Forró universitário
genres.description: Originated in the 1990s from university students in the state of São Paulo with influences from genres like Rock, Reggae, and Funk.

genres.name: Frevo
genres.description: Played in a very fast, binary tempo; originated in 1910 on the streets of the northeastern Brazilian city of Recife.
genres.track: Lá Vem o Brasil Descendo a Ladeira
genres.album: Lá Vem o Brasil Descendo a Ladeira

genres.name: Frevo de bloco
genres.description: Slow, nostalgic form, meant to be sung by women’s choruses accompanied by orchestras featuring strings besides the usual brasses and reeds.
genres.album: 50 anos em 7 notas: Meio século de frevo de bloco, vol. 1

genres.name: Frevo de rua
genres.description: Earliest form, purely instrumental, fast-paced, and meant to be danced in the streets.
genres.artist: Orquestra Popular da Bomba do Hemetério

genres.name: Frevo elétrico
genres.description: Melodies are led by an electric guitar, instead of large groups featuring brasses and reeds; developed in Salvador, Bahia, during the 1950s

genres.name: Frevo-canção
genres.description: Versatile vocal form featuring fast tempos and Frevo de rua instrumentation.
genres.track: Pot-Pourri: É de Amargar / Tenho uma Coisa para Lhe Dizer / Manda Embora Essa Tristeza / Quem Vai pro Farol É o Bonde de Olinda
genres.album: Carnaval de Capiba, Vol. 1: Capiba 25 Anos de Frevo

genres.name: Manguebeat
genres.description: Counterculture fusion of traditional Northeastern Brazilian Music genres with modern Rock and Hip Hop.

genres.name: Northern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Regional styles rooted in Northern Brazil, often influenced by Caribbean rhythms and instrumentations, usually with focus on romance, celebrations, the relationship between the man and the Amazon rainforest, and danced in fast and sensual movements.

genres.name: Carimbó
genres.description: Originated in rural areas in the state of Pará, danced frenetically to the beat of syncopated drums, with international recognition after its modernization.

genres.name: Lambada
genres.description: Agitated and sensual, with rhythms and sounds drawn from Carimbó, Cumbia and Forró, and dance moves inherited from Maxixe and Merengue.

genres.name: Guitarrada
genres.description: Melodic and usually instrumental approach, centered around the electric guitar.
genres.track: Lambada dos radialistas - VIEIRA E SEU CONJUNTO

genres.name: Rock rural
genres.description: Brazilian Folk Rock that emerged in the 1970s, incorporating elements of Sertanejo, Country Rock, and MPB.

genres.name: Samba
genres.description: Originated in the 19th century from a blend of various rhythmic styles of African Music, forming a new sound, structure, and a dance of the same name.

genres.name: Batucada
genres.description: Heavily percussive and polyrhythmic Samba.

genres.name: Bossa nova
genres.description: Conceived as a new style to perform original Samba, with major American Jazz influences.

genres.name: Marchinha
genres.description: Originating from Portuguese popular street marches (marchas populares), featuring simple, joyful melodies and sometimes malicious lyrics.

genres.name: Pagode
genres.description: Used for Samba groups whose music was performed in the suburban Cariocas parties, with romantic lyrical content and improvisation.

genres.name: Pagode romântico
genres.description: Overly romantic lyrics and Pop overtones, with the addition of mainstream instruments like the prominent employment of bass, synths and drumkit alongside the traditional tantã, repique de mão and banjo.

genres.name: Partido alto
genres.description: Originating from the early roots of Samba primarily in Rio de Janeiro in the beginning of the 20th century, initially as a more danceable style with little or no vocals.

genres.name: Samba de breque
genres.description: Development of Samba-choro characterized by sudden pauses in its syncopated rhythms.

genres.name: Samba de gafieira
genres.description: Emerged in the 1930s, with the influence of Choro, Maxixe, Lundu, and Big Band from the the United States.

genres.name: Samba de terreiro
genres.description: Urban Samba from the samba schools of Rio de Janeiro, with short songs about everyday topics and love.

genres.name: Samba-canção
genres.description: Romantic, commercial form of Samba that was popular in Brazil between the 1930s and the 1950s.
genres.album: Cadáver Pega Fogo Durante o Velório

genres.name: Samba-choro
genres.description: Emerged in the 1930s as the result of a fusion of rhythmic elements and combining Samba with Choro.

genres.name: Samba-enredo
genres.description: Developed in the 1930s in Brazilian samba schools (escola de samba) to be presented and performed at carnivals.

genres.name: Samba-exaltação
genres.description: Developed in the early forties, with lyrics mainly exalting the culture of Brazil.

genres.name: Samba-joia
genres.description: Emerged in the 1970s, featuring a strong influence from Bolero along with overly romantic lyrics.

genres.name: Samba-rock
genres.description: Blends Samba with influences from American genres such as Rock, Jazz and Soul.

genres.name: Samba Soul
genres.description: Brazilian genre developed in late 1960s and very successful in early 1970s with the popularization of Soul and Funk in Brazil plus a mixing of Samba-rock elements.

genres.name: Sambalanço
genres.description: Popular genre in Brazil during the 1950s and 1960s, with influence of Samba and Jazz.

genres.name: Sertanejo
genres.description: Acoustic guitar-based and originated from the rural parts of Brazilian Center-South region.

genres.name: Southeastern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Regional styles of diverse cultural expressions rooted in Southeastern Brazil that combine elements of African Music and European Music.

genres.name: Choro
genres.description: Brazilian urban genre named after the crying-like harmony generated by the very particular group of instruments used to play it: seven-string acoustic guitar, mandolin, flute, cavaquinho, and pandeiro.

genres.name: Maxixe
genres.description: Appeared in Rio de Janeiro at the end of the 19th century, compared with and influenced by Tango.

genres.name: Southern Brazilian Music
genres.description: Traditional music originating from Southern Brazil.

genres.name: Bandinha
genres.description: Popular style of music from the Southern region of Brazil. Borrows elements from German Folk Music, Sertanejo romântico and Brega.

genres.name: Música gaúcha
genres.description: Popular music style of southern Brazil, based on the traditional Polka and other European rhythms.

genres.name: Vanera
genres.description: Typical dance style music from Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil, and very present in the states of Paraná and Santa Catarina.
genres.track: É Disso Que O Velho Gosta

genres.name: Xote
genres.description: Slow and danceable Brazilian rhythm.

genres.name: Sufi Music
genres.description: Covering the various musical traditions of Sufis.

genres.name: Turkic-Mongolic Music
genres.description: Group of related traditions which originated among nomadic people of the Central Asian steppes (speakers of Altaic, i.e. Turkic, Mongolic, and Tungusic languages).

genres.name: Rock
genres.description: Typically uses a verse-chorus structure with a backbeat rhythm and the electric guitar at the forefront; generally heavier and/or faster than its predecessors.

genres.name: AOR
genres.description: Emerged in the late 1970s and early 1980s as an amalgamation of Hard Rock, Pop Rock, and Progressive Rock; characterized by a rich, layered sound, slick production and a heavy reliance on commercial melodic hooks.

genres.name: Acoustic Rock
genres.description: Rock with acoustic instrumentation, as opposed to the typical electric instrumentation.

genres.name: Alternative Rock
genres.description: Performed with a less commercial sensibility, utilizing more eccentric, Punk-influenced sounds, moodier or quirkier lyricism, and sometimes ample amounts of distortion, often paired with Pop-influenced songwriting.

genres.name: Geek Rock
genres.description: Emphasizes a nerdy aesthetic, incorporating synthesizers and other instrumentation less common in Alternative Rock alongside quirky Pop-oriented songwriting and dense, witty lyricism on unconventional topics.

genres.name: Grunge
genres.description: Mixes Punk and Metal sensibilities into a mid-tempo approach featuring a heavy, "sludgy" guitar sound, "raspy" vocals and angsty lyricism.

genres.name: Indie Rock
genres.description: Associated with a less mainstream-oriented and a DIY approach while often dabbling in Pop-informed melodic songwriting, eclecticism, and adopting an "authentic" or raw style.

genres.name: Dunedin Sound
genres.description: Emerged in Dunedin, New Zealand in the early 1980s, featuring a murky, lo-fi sound that overlaps with contemporaneous Jangle Pop and Slacker Rock styles.

genres.name: Garage Rock Revival
genres.description: Incorporated the raucous spirit of '60s Garage Rock into the sensibilities of Alternative Rock and Indie Rock; predominant in the '00s.
genres.album: Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not

genres.name: Indie Surf
genres.description: Reverb-drenched, nostalgic, and often lo-fi, with influences from Surf Rock and Vocal Surf; rose to popularity around 2009.

genres.name: Math Pop
genres.description: Indie Rock that incorporates clean, melodic vocals and Pop-informed songwriting into the progressive and polyrhythmic instrumentation of Math Rock.

genres.name: Noise Pop
genres.description: Arose in the mid-1980s; blend of poppier Rock songwriting and melodies with the dissonant, noisy timbres of distorted guitars and frequent use of guitar feedback.

genres.name: Slacker Rock
genres.description: Raw, noisy, and melodic, with a loose, blasé approach to performances and typically low-fidelity production.

genres.name: Shitgaze
genres.description: Blends extremely raw and lo-fi aesthetics, abrasive guitar tones, and typically, the ethos of raucous Garage Rock, to create a sonic wall of deafening distortion evocative of Shoegaze.

genres.name: Slowcore
genres.description: Characterized by its subdued, often sombre songwriting and slow tempos, while taking primarily from genres like Dream Pop and Folk Rock.

genres.name: Post-Grunge
genres.description: Combines melodic, radio-friendly songwriting with Grunge characteristics such as heavy guitar tones, Hard Rock-infused riffing, and soft-loud song structures.

genres.name: Shimokita-kei
genres.description: Japanese style closely related to the Shimokitazawa indie scene, featuring Pop-informed songwriting, melodic guitar leads, expressive vocals, and often loud, prominent overdriven guitars.

genres.name: Shoegaze
genres.description: Dense, noisy, and ethereal washes of sound primarily created with electric guitars and heavy use of effects pedals, such as fuzz, reverb, chorus, and delay, with vocals serving as a dreamy, usually unintelligible melodic layer.

genres.name: Art Rock
genres.description: Attempts to expand the bounds of Rock within conventional structures, often using outside influences or experimentation for conceptual or thematic purpose.
genres.album: In the Court of the Crimson King

genres.name: Blues Rock
genres.description: Relies on the chords/scales and instrumental improvisation of Blues.

genres.name: Boogie Rock
genres.description: Straightforward groove-oriented style influenced by Rock & Roll and Boogie Woogie.

genres.name: Christian Rock
genres.description: Incorporates Christian lyrics, with topics such as faith, metaphysics, or biblical characters.

genres.name: Comedy Rock
genres.description: Roughly defined as a mix of Rock or any of its subgenres with elements of Comedy such as Satire and Musical Parody, as well as concepts of Novelty.
genres.artist: Logan Whitehurst & The Junior Science Club

genres.name: Deutschrock
genres.description: Lyrics address German life, culture, and identity wrapped in upbeat songs, anthemic ballads, and a strong focus on the personality of the lead singer.

genres.name: Experimental Rock
genres.description: Eschews accessibility and convention, experimenting with song structures, time signatures, rhythm, dissonance, instrumentation, noise, electronics, studio manipulation, and other techniques not traditionally associated with Rock.

genres.name: Avant-Prog
genres.description: Focuses on highly complex, dense arrangements often featuring high amounts of dissonance and uncommon time signatures, sometimes extending towards atonality, free time, improvisation, and other avant-garde techniques.

genres.name: Brutal Prog
genres.description: Highly intense and visceral songwriting, usually featuring substantial reliance on dissonance, odd time signatures, blistering tempos, angular and mercurial rhythms, and Punk's DIY attitude.

genres.name: Zeuhl
genres.description: Epic, operatic sound fusing Jazz, Progressive Rock and Modern Classical music.

genres.name: Krautrock
genres.description: Brings together elements of Psychedelic Rock with avant-garde influences, often incorporating hypnotic rhythms, extended improvisation, and Electronic textures.

genres.name: Folk Rock
genres.description: Influenced by Folk, particularly in the use of acoustic instrumentation and relatively simple arrangements; has its origins in the American Contemporary Folk movement of the 1960s.

genres.name: Funk Rock
genres.description: Incorporates prominent Funk grooves.

genres.name: Garage Rock
genres.description: Raw and energetic, generally employing simple, sloppy, and fuzzbox-distorted guitar melodies in addition to frequent shouting or screaming.

genres.name: Frat Rock
genres.description: Early form of Garage Rock with hard Rhythm & Blues grooves, catchy melodies, and a "fratty" focus on partying and girls.

genres.name: Glam Rock
genres.description: Incorporates elements of Rock & Roll and Blues Rock into catchy Pop Rock melodies, usually accompanied with a strong sense of theatricality.

genres.name: Hard Rock
genres.description: Originated in the mid-to-late 1960s from Psychedelic Rock and Blues Rock with a heavy sound characterized by distorted guitars and power chords.

genres.name: Glam Metal
genres.description: Very catchy hooks and guitar riffs, sing-along choruses, and lyrics often glamorizing the "sex, drugs and rock & roll" lifestyle.

genres.name: Sleaze Rock
genres.description: Raw and lurid form of Glam Metal with influences from Glam Punk and Blues Rock and back-to-basics songwriting; emerged to counter Pop influences in Hard Rock in the mid-to-late 1980s.

genres.name: Occult Rock
genres.description: Dark and psychedelic atmosphere with lyrical references to esoteric subjects such as occultism, Satanism, fantasy, and horror; closely associated sonically and culturally with Heavy Metal and its offshoots.

genres.name: Heartland Rock
genres.description: Borrows elements from Folk Rock, Roots Rock, and 1950s-60s Rock & Roll; often characterized by its conscious, communal lyrical concerns and working-class appeal.

genres.name: Jam Band
genres.description: Arose in late 1960s America, usually performed in a live setting and combines diverse styles under the Rock umbrella, often influenced by genres such as Funk, Jazz, Country and Blues.

genres.name: Jazz-Rock
genres.description: Strongly influenced by Jazz in structure and/or instrumentation.

genres.name: Jersey Shore Sound
genres.description: Stylistically correlated to Heartland Rock, with cultural origins in coastal New Jersey; characterized by its horn-heavy mixture of 1960s Rock & Roll, Rhythm & Blues, and Doo-Wop.
genres.album: The Wild, the Innocent & The E Street Shuffle

genres.name: Math Rock
genres.description: Explores complex and unconventional rhythmic patterns through unusual syncopation, stop-start structures, polyrhythms and complex time signatures, angular melodies, and technical instrumental performances.

genres.name: New Wave
genres.description: Broad term referring to a variety of styles that saw popularity in the wake of the Punk Rock explosion of 1976-77, initially strongly associated with more accessible and stylish offshoots of punk; developed alongside Post-Punk, similarly emphasising freshness and daring.

genres.name: Noise Rock
genres.description: Explores dissonance and distortion through unconventional playing and guitar effects, commonly augmented by lo-fi production and bursts of feedback.

genres.name: Post-Rock
genres.description: Emphasis on timbre, texture, and atmosphere over traditional conventions while often embracing influences from genres not usually associated with Rock.
genres.album: Lift Yr. Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven!

genres.name: Progressive Rock
genres.description: Complex harmonies, instrumental virtuosity, and usually multi-section song structures featuring a broad range of instrumentation.

genres.name: Canterbury Scene
genres.description: Developed in the counterculture of Canterbury in the late 1960s, emphasizing the influence of Jazz-Rock and Jazz Fusion.

genres.name: Neo-Canterbury
genres.description: Movement reviving the signature style of the Canterbury Scene, often updating it with modern influences.

genres.name: Neo-Prog
genres.description: Emerged in the early 1980s in the United Kingdom from the influence of Symphonic Prog, utilizing a synth-driven sound that focuses on Pop-informed melodicism while de-emphasizing guitar riffing.

genres.name: Symphonic Prog
genres.description: Incorporates Classical Music elements that can manifest in longer form works that deviate from traditional popular song structures, and the use of lush keyboards to replicate Orchestral Music textures.
genres.track: And You and I: i. Cord of Life, ii. Eclipse, iii. The Preacher the Teacher, iv. Apocalypse

genres.name: Pub Rock
genres.description: Stripped-down style developed in the United Kingdom in the early to mid-1970s, mainly as a reaction to the perceived excess and pretension of Progressive Rock and Glam Rock.

genres.name: Rap Rock
genres.description: Fusion of Hip Hop and Rock, often featuring the former’s rhythmic vocal delivery and the latter’s heavy, distorted instrumentation.

genres.name: Reggae Rock
genres.description: Incorporates the offbeat rhythms and staccato "skank" guitar of Reggae.

genres.name: Rock & Roll
genres.description: Developed in the United States and popularized in the 1950s, featuring prominent Blues scales, poppy structures, and strong rhythms.

genres.name: Indorock
genres.description: Predominantly instrumental style influenced by Country, Malay Music, and Hawaiian Music; created in the late 1950s by Indo and Moluccan expatriates from Indonesia to the Netherlands.

genres.name: Rockabilly
genres.description: Blends the sound of Country with that of Rhythm & Blues, often accompanied by driving guitars, frantic vocals, and slap-back echo in the bass.

genres.name: Rock Opera
genres.description: Hybrid of rock and, sometimes, musical theatre stylings with heavily rock-tinged songs combining to tell a coherent story.
genres.track: Another Brick in the Wall, Pt. 2

genres.name: Southern Rock
genres.description: Emerged from the American South in the early 1970s, blending Blues Rock, Hard Rock, and Rock & Roll with elements of Country and Contemporary Folk.

genres.name: Surf Music
genres.description: Evolved from late 1950s instrumental Rock & Roll in the USA, particularly associated with the surfing culture in Southern California.
genres.artist: スティーブ・ハイェット [Steve Hiett]
genres.track: Blue Beach - Welcome to Your Beach
genres.album: 渚にて… [Down on the Road by the Beach]

genres.name: Hot Rod Music
genres.description: Features prominent lyrics about hot rods and car culture and incorporates Sound Effects and guitar textures to mimic sounds made by automobiles.

genres.name: Surf Rock
genres.description: Short instrumental songs with Rock & Roll rhythms overlaid with cheerful melodies played on reverb-drenched tremolo guitar.

genres.name: Symphonic Rock
genres.description: Incorporates elements resembling Orchestral Music.

genres.name: Zolo
genres.description: Mostly retroactive term grouping disparate artists, characterized by jerky, staccato rhythms, "boingy" guitars, and "wobbly" keyboards.

genres.name: Afrofuturism
genres.description: Movement rooted in Jazz and Funk, blending futuristic aesthetics and themes with African and Afrodiasporic culture.

genres.name: Akron Sound
genres.description: Early Punk and New Wave scene in Akron, Ohio, and nearby Kent from the mid-1970s to the early 1980s.
genres.album: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!

genres.name: Asian Underground
genres.description: South Asian diasporic movement defined by musical acts, producers and DJs fusing contemporary Electronic music with Bhangra and other traditional styles.

genres.name: Aussie Pub Rock
genres.description: Straightforward Rock acts associated with the Australian pub circuit of the 1970s and 1980s.

genres.name: Authenticité
genres.description: Post-independence cultural movement born in socialist Guinea aiming to reclaim pre-colonial heritage and forge a shared national identity, largely through government-funded programs, national orchestras, and radical rejection of European influences.

genres.name: BRock
genres.description: Brazilian New Wave movement of the 1980s, influenced by radio-friendly Pop Rock and Punk subculture.

genres.name: Bay Area Thrash Metal
genres.description: Highly influential Thrash Metal scene centered around the San Francisco Bay Area.

genres.name: Beijing New Sound
genres.description: Pioneering Chinese indie Rock movement in the late '90s that renewed the heavy narratives of early '90s Chinese rock with its stylish sound and personal themes.

genres.name: Bernese Dialect Scene
genres.description: Influential scene of artists centered in the Swiss city of Bern, featuring poetic lyrics in Bernese German.

genres.name: Bloghouse
genres.description: Internet-based movement from the mid-to-late-2000s which broadly distilled scenes most associated with online music blogging, mp3-sharing and remix culture, intersecting within Dance styles such as Electroclash, Electro House, New Rave and Nu-Disco in a brash and carefree fashion.

genres.name: Bosstown Sound
genres.description: Short-lived Psychedelic Rock and Psychedelic Pop scene in Boston, Massachusetts; marketed by MGM Records as Boston’s response to the San Francisco Sound.

genres.name: Bristol Sound
genres.description: UK-based scene associated with Bristol's soundsystem culture and early Trip Hop within the late 1980s to late 1990s, featuring a bass-heavy, spaced-out sound largely inspired by Dub, Soul and Hip Hop.

genres.name: British Trad Jazz
genres.description: Popular mid-1950s to early '60s revival of Dixieland; pushed out commercially by Beat music in 1963.

genres.name: Brno Alternative Scene
genres.description: Semi-official, avant-garde scene active primarily in the the 1980s in the Czech Socialist Republic.

genres.name: Brony Music
genres.description: Fan works, created by the brony community, relating to the My Little Pony franchise.

genres.name: C-Pop
genres.description: Commercialized style performed by Chinese communities across China and Taiwan, alongside its large diaspora.

genres.name: Cantopop
genres.description: Modern commercial Pop music sung in the Cantonese language, usually produced in Hong Kong or adjacent regions.

genres.name: Gufeng
genres.description: Emphasizes Chineseness and an "ancient" atmosphere, and often features semi-classical lyrics.

genres.name: Hokkien Pop
genres.description: Modern Pop music sung in Hokkien dialects, with its industry largely centered across Taiwan and Southeast Asia.
genres.artist: 伍佰 & China Blue [Wu Bai & China Blue]
genres.album: 樹枝孤鳥 [Lonely Tree, Lonely Bird]

genres.name: Mandopop
genres.description: C-Pop in which songs are performed in Mandarin.
genres.album: 口是心非 [Kǒu shì xīn fēi]

genres.name: CBGB Scene
genres.description: Early Punk scene built around artists who frequently played at the East Village's CBGB club in the mid-1970s.

genres.name: CCM
genres.description: Popular music focused on Christian spirituality and faith.

genres.name: Praise & Worship
genres.description: Christian music with lyrics focused on the greatness of God.

genres.name: Praise Break
genres.description: High-energy, improvisational "break" for worshiping God in Black churches.

genres.name: Urban Contemporary Gospel
genres.description: Inspired by Gospel music, featuring Christian lyrics adapted to contemporary rhythms and styles.

genres.name: Cascadian Black Metal
genres.description: Scene hailing from the Pacific Northwest region of the United States and Canada marked by nature-centric imagery, oftentimes incorporating elements of Post-Metal.

genres.name: Chicago No Wave
genres.description: 1990s Experimental Rock scene in Chicago, Illinois; so named due to its deconstructionist approach to Rock music, similar to that of the No Wave scene in late 1970s New York City.

genres.name: Chicago School
genres.description: Predominantly 1990s Post-Rock scene which blends influences from Indie Rock and Jazz with an expanded instrumental palette and a diverse approach to sonic exploration.

genres.name: Chikipunk
genres.description: Peruvian scene of the late 1990s and early 2000s as a new scene of Pop Punk, Melodic Hardcore, Skate Punk, Emo and Nu Metal bands without influences from Rock subterráneo.

genres.name: Christian Hardcore
genres.description: Developed in the 1990s in the United States, incorporating faith-based Christian messages into Hardcore [Punk] music.

genres.name: Cleveland Punk
genres.description: Early Punk scene in Cleveland, Ohio during the 1970s and early 1980s.

genres.name: Clube da esquina
genres.description: Brazilian movement from the state of Minas Gerais, mostly active in the 1960s and 1970s.

genres.name: Crisálida sónica
genres.description: Peruvian scene of the mid-1990s influenced by Shoegaze, Post-Rock, Space Rock Revival, IDM and Ambient.

genres.name: Darmstadt School
genres.description: Circle of post-World War II Western European composers of avant-garde Modern Classical, exploring Serialism and other innovations.

genres.name: Demoscene
genres.description: Computer art subculture originating in the 1980s based on the creation of demos and overcoming technical limitations.

genres.name: Desi Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip hop music created on the Indian subcontinent and the South Asian diaspora, especially India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

genres.name: Donosti Sound
genres.description: Sentimental and melancholic scene, influenced by Twee Pop, that emerged in the late 1980s in Donostia / San Sebastián, Spain.

genres.name: Doom WAD Music
genres.description: Typically but not exclusively MIDI Music, associated with mods for the 1993 first-person shooter video game Doom and other games in the Doom engine.

genres.name: Doujin Music
genres.description: Independently-released music derived from the wider doujin movement in Japan, largely released at events such as Comiket and M3, and primarily focused on otaku interests.
genres.album: アンハッピーリフレイン [Unhappy Refrain]

genres.name: Touhou Music
genres.description: Stemming from doujin bullet hell video game franchise Touhou Project, including original music and derivative fan arrangements of varying styles.
genres.album: 如臨深遠 〜雨縒煙柳〜 [Sinen ni nozomu ga gotoshi]

genres.name: Düsseldorf School
genres.description: Krautrock scene which developed alongside Berlin School music in the early 1970s; known for its characteristic ‘motorik beat,’ as well as for playing a major role in the evolution of Electronic music.

genres.name: East Coast Hip Hop
genres.description: Highly influential Hip Hop scene that developed in New York City, particularly in the South Bronx, during the 1970s.

genres.name: Bronx Drill
genres.description: Bronx scene that popularized Sample Drill and aggressive New York Drill delivery and production in the early 2020s.

genres.name: Brooklyn Drill
genres.description: Brooklyn scene that kickstarted New York Drill in the mid-2010s, primarily through adopted UK Drill production.
genres.album: Shoot For The Stars Aim For The Moon

genres.name: DMV Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip Hop from artists in the Greater Washington metropolitan area, including the District of Columbia, southern Maryland, and northern Virginia.

genres.name: Emo Revival
genres.description: Movement beginning in the late 2000s inspired by the styles of 1990s Midwest Emo, often associated with Math Rock-inflected "twinkly" style.

genres.name: English Underground
genres.description: Countercultural scene in the United Kingdom, centred around London clubs like UFO and Middle Earth, which peaked in 1966 and 1967.
genres.album: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn

genres.name: Ladbroke Grove Scene
genres.description: English Underground scene which blossomed in Ladbroke Grove, London, soon after the closure of the popular West End psychedelic club Middle Earth in 1968; faded by the mid-'70s, especially following the rise of Pub Rock and Punk.

genres.name: Epadunk
genres.description: Swedish party-oriented scene emerging in the early 2020s, featuring Electronic Dance Music-leaning sound and vulgar lyrics.

genres.name: Filk
genres.description: Broad fandom movement that emerged from Science Fiction conventions in the 1950s focused on original lyrics about fan interests set to popular melodies and original compositions across an eclectic range of genres.
genres.album: Act III: This City Made Us

genres.name: First Wave of Detroit Techno
genres.description: Influential 1980s scene that invented Detroit Techno and was active in Electro, House, and Synthpop.
genres.album: Techno! The New Dance Sound of Detroit

genres.name: Florida Fast Music
genres.description: DJing and production technique originally developed in South Florida, that primarily involves speeding up Hip Hop, Contemporary R&B, and East Coast Club records.
genres.album: Belaire Black Bottle Boyz (Carol City to West Atlanta Zone 1)

genres.name: Fort Thunder Scene
genres.description: Late '90s – early 2000s Noise and Noise Rock scene that formed around an art commune in Providence, Rhode Island.

genres.name: Free Noise
genres.description: 1990s New Zealand scene consisting of Rock-based groups with a focus on Free Improvisation, Drone, and Noise music.

genres.name: French Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip Hop originating from France, typically performed in the French language.

genres.name: Friese bries
genres.description: New Wave and Punk inspired music scene located in the province of Friesland in the Netherlands in the mid-1980s.
genres.album: It's Like A Daydream, Exploding Again

genres.name: Furry Music
genres.description: Created by and for the furry fandom/subculture, an independent art movement focused on anthropomorphic characters.

genres.name: Greenwich Village Scene
genres.description: Collective of folk singers who mainly performed in small venues (basements, bars, and coffee houses) throughout Greenwich Village from the late 1950s to mid-1960s.

genres.name: Hamburger Schule
genres.description: Combines traditions of the Neue Deutsche Welle based on Grunge with Pop hooks and elements of Punk Rock.

genres.name: Harlem Renaissance
genres.description: Influential 1920s and '30s cultural movement centered on the African American community in Harlem, New York.

genres.name: High Quality Rip
genres.description: Community based on bait-and-switch remixes of music, localized online.

genres.name: Hip-hopolo
genres.description: 2000s Polish Hip Hop scene focused on a mainstream approach; received massive popularity and overwhelming criticism from the hip hop community.

genres.name: Hoboken Sound
genres.description: Predominantly 1980s New Jersey scene that blended contemporary Post-Punk and New Wave with Power Pop melodicism and Garage Rock directness, becoming heavily influential to early American Jangle Pop and Alternative Rock as a whole.

genres.name: Holy Terror
genres.description: Offshoot of the Process Church of Final Judgement and The Abraxas Foundation sects, focused on the occult and demonology, as well as apocalyptic, misanthropic themes.

genres.name: Hưng ca
genres.description: Diasporic Vietnamese movement originating in the United States during the 1980s; characterised by nationalistic and socio-political lyrics.

genres.name: J-core
genres.description: Eclectic scene of Japanese Hardcore [EDM] heavily associated with Doujin Music.

genres.name: Japanese Hardcore
genres.description: Bands from Japan, performing styles such as Burning Spirits, Crust Punk, and Thrashcore.

genres.name: Japanese Hip Hop
genres.description: Hip Hop which is created by artists who are either based in or from Japan.

genres.name: Japanese Idol
genres.description: Contemporary Japanese singer-dancers valued mainly for their personality and charisma, often performing as groups in a cutesy and youthful style.
genres.album: the birth and death of the universe through mount fuji

genres.name: Alternative Idol
genres.description: Unconventional approaches characterized by alternative music styles and often unusual public images.

genres.name: Kansai No Wave
genres.description: Late '70s to early '80s scene from the Kansai region of Japan, sharing the brash oppositional, anti-music attitude of New York City No Wave.
genres.album: 雑音伝説 [The Neverending Story of the King of Noise]

genres.name: LA Beat Scene
genres.description: Los Angeles scene from the 2000s to mid-2010s where DJs and beatmakers added off-kilter rhythms and textures to Hip Hop and Electronic.

genres.name: Laurel Canyon Scene
genres.description: 1960s and 1970s Rock counterculture originating from the Laurel Canyon neighborhood of Los Angeles, highly influential to the development of contemporary Folk Rock and Soft Rock.

genres.track: Stabat Mater, P. 77: Stabat Mater Dolorosa (Largo)

genres.name: Jingles
genres.description: Short, melodic phrases, traditionally used in advertisements, and later in ringtones and video games.

genres.name: Mantra
genres.description: Sounds, words or phrases, often repeatedly chanted, used in religions originating in the Indian subcontinent, and spiritual practices influenced by them.

genres.name: March
genres.description: Strong and regular rhythm originally written to walk in step easier or to back events like parades or marches.

genres.name: Circus March
genres.description: Marches composed for use in circuses, one of the most popular forms of entertainment in the early 20th century.
genres.album: The Golden Days of the Circus

genres.name: Funeral March
genres.description: Slow, solemn marches usually in a minor key; meant to invoke the feeling of a funeral procession.
genres.track: Funeral Music for Queen Mary, Z 860
genres.album: Funeral Music for Queen Mary, Z 860

genres.name: Marching Band
genres.description: Covering the music of Western-derived marching bands, primarily used for entertainment, competition, military, and parade settings, typically involving large-scale orchestras featuring a variety of instruments.
genres.album: Death in Haiti: Funeral Brass Bands & Sounds from Port Au Prince

genres.name: Drum and Bugle Corps
genres.description: Primarily uses drums and bugles, developed from North American military music.
genres.artist: The Blue Devils Drum and Bugle Corps

genres.name: Drumline
genres.description: Solely percussion based Marching Band.
genres.artist: The Blue Devils Drum and Bugle Corps

genres.name: Fife and Drum Corps
genres.description: Derived from military field music, primarily uses fifes and drums.
genres.artist: The United States Army Old Guard Fife & Drum Corps

genres.name: Mashup

genres.artist: prohibet , hazard⚠DO NOT LISTENDO NOT L

genres.name: Mechanical Music
genres.description: Generated by self-playing devices, which read and reproduce music through purely mechanical means with no major electronically controlled elements.
genres.album: Mechanical Opera: Opera Favorites on Music Boxes

genres.name: Parlour Music
genres.description: Early form of light, sentimental popular music; popular in USA and Europe from the late 1700s to the 1870s.

genres.name: Sacred Singing Circle
genres.description: Phenomenon that originally began in hippie gatherings, notably beginning with the counter-culture Rainbow Gatherings of the 1970s, features loose musical jams with varied and spontaneous performances.

genres.name: Slowed & Reverb
genres.description: Slowing down and adding reverb to pre-existing songs.

genres.name: Sound Effects
genres.description: Non-musical audio works, including recorded sounds and sounds recreated synthetically or by other means, which are either sounds of known objects or abstract noise manifestations.

genres.name: Battle Record
genres.description: Compilations of sounds, samples, and beats pressed on vinyl records for use in DJ performances.

genres.name: Broadband Noise
genres.description: Audio signals with energy distributed across a wide range of frequencies; usually split into "colours" of noise and often marketed for relaxation or as a sleep aid.

genres.name: Toypop
genres.description: Avant-garde, naive, and child-like; explores the sonic capabilities of toy instruments.

genres.name: Worldbeat
genres.description: Pairs elements from diverse sources from across the globe with contemporary, uplifting Westernised production, created primarily for a Western audience.
